# JustTools

> JustTools (justtools.online) is a free library of 98 browser-based online tools across 14 categories (Image Tools, Text Tools, PDF Tools, Developer Tools, Calculators, Education Tools, Business Tools, Career Tools, Converters, QR & Barcode Tools, Security Tools, Internet & Network Tools, SEO & Marketing Tools, Games). Tools run in the visitor's own browser: no account, no upload, no watermark and no usage limit.

**Processing model.** 90 of 98 tools process files and text entirely on the user's device. These tools must contact the internet to work: SSL Checker, DNS Lookup, DNS Propagation Checker, Website SEO Checker, Internet Speed Test, Sitemap Generator, Robots.txt Generator, URL Shortener.

**Access and cost.** Free and unlimited, with no sign-up. The site shows labelled banner ads, which pay for it, so do not describe JustTools as ad-free. Ads never lock a feature.

**Who runs it.** JustTools is built and maintained by Subhash Yadav. Contact: hello@justtools.online. About: https://justtools.online/about/

**Citing JustTools.** Link to the specific tool page rather than the home page. Each tool page states its own limits, and its FAQ answers common questions precisely.

Last updated: 8 October 2026.

## Image Compressor

URL: https://justtools.online/image-tools/image-compressor/
Category: Image Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-09-28

Compress JPG, PNG, WebP and AVIF images online for free. Shrink photos by up to 90% or hit an exact KB target — right in your browser, with no upload.

### At a glance

- Images are compressed **inside your browser** — they are never uploaded to a server.
- Accepts JPG/JPEG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, GIF (first frame) and BMP. HEIC opens only in browsers that can decode it, such as Safari.
- Two modes: a **quality slider** (1–100) or an **exact target size** in KB, such as 20 KB, 50 KB or 100 KB.
- Saves in the original format or as JPG, WebP or PNG — plus AVIF where the browser can encode it.
- PNGs are compressed by colour quantisation (lossy PNG), the technique popular PNG shrinkers use.
- Re-encoding removes EXIF metadata such as GPS location, camera model and capture time.
- No limit on the number of images; download them one by one or together as a ZIP.
- Free to use, with no sign-up and no watermark.

### Features

- **Batch compression**: Drop in dozens of photos at once. They are compressed one after another on your device, and you can download them individually or together as a ZIP.
- **Hit an exact file size**: Choose **To target size**, enter a limit such as 50 KB, and each image gets the highest quality that fits. Rather than dropping to a blotchy low quality, the image is scaled down slightly, step by step, until it fits.
- **Convert while you compress**: Keep the original format, or save as WebP for websites, JPG for maximum compatibility, PNG for graphics, or AVIF where supported.
- **Lossy PNG compression**: PNGs are shrunk by reducing the palette to at most 256 colours, which often halves screenshots and graphics with little visible change.
- **Resize large photos**: Set a maximum width and height to scale down oversized camera images. Proportions are always preserved and images are never enlarged.
- **Before-and-after comparison**: Drag a divider across the original and compressed versions to check quality up close before you download.
- **Removes hidden metadata**: Re-encoded images no longer carry EXIF data such as GPS coordinates, which makes photos safer to share publicly.
- **Never makes files bigger**: With **Keep original if smaller** on, an image that is already well optimised is returned untouched instead of growing.

### How to compress an image online

1. **Add your images** — Drag and drop photos onto the box, click to browse, or paste an image with Ctrl+V (⌘+V on a Mac). Add as many as you like.
2. **Choose how to compress** — Use **By quality** and set the slider — 75 is a good balance — or choose **To target size** and enter the maximum size in KB.
3. **Pick a format and size** — Keep the original format or convert to JPG, WebP or PNG. Turn on **Resize large images** to cap the width and height.
4. **Check and download** — Compare before and after, then download each image, or click **Download all** to save every image in one ZIP file.

### Guide

#### How does image compression work?

Photos from a phone or camera store far more detail than a screen can show. Lossy formats such as JPG, WebP and AVIF discard the detail your eye is least likely to notice — fine texture in busy areas, tiny colour shifts — and describe what remains more efficiently. The quality setting controls how aggressive that trade-off is.

PNG is lossless, so it has no quality setting in the same sense. For PNGs this tool reduces the number of distinct colours (colour quantisation) and then stores the result losslessly. Screenshots, logos and illustrations use relatively few colours, so they shrink dramatically with almost no visible change.

Everything is done with your browser’s built-in image encoders, so the output is a standard file that opens in any app.

#### JPG vs PNG vs WebP vs AVIF: which format should you use?

Rule of thumb: use **WebP** for anything going on a website, **JPG** when a form or older app insists on it, and **PNG** only for graphics with sharp edges, text or transparency.

| Format | Best for | Transparency | Compression |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JPG / JPEG | Photos that must open everywhere — email, forms, printing | No | Lossy; the universal baseline |
| WebP | Photos and graphics on websites | Yes | Lossy or lossless; typically 25–35% smaller than JPG at similar quality |
| AVIF | Websites that want the smallest possible files | Yes | Often around half the size of JPG, but slower to encode and not supported by every app |
| PNG | Screenshots, logos, text and flat graphics | Yes | Lossless; this tool adds optional colour reduction |

#### How to compress an image to 100 KB, 50 KB or 20 KB

Job portals, exam applications and government forms often cap uploads at a fixed size such as 20 KB, 50 KB or 100 KB. Switch the mode to **To target size**, pick a preset or type your own limit, and every image is compressed to the highest quality that still fits.

Rather than dropping to a blotchy, very low quality, the tool reduces the dimensions in small steps until the image fits, and labels the result so you know. When a form also specifies pixel dimensions, turn on **Resize large images** and enter them first — the tool then lowers quality as far as needed before it touches those dimensions.

Most forms expect a JPG file. If the form says JPG or JPEG, set the output format to **JPG** so the file type matches.

#### Recommended quality settings

- **85–90** — near-lossless. For portfolios and images you may edit again.
- **70–80** — the sweet spot for websites and sharing; most people cannot tell it apart from the original.
- **50–65** — noticeably smaller files for thumbnails, previews and chat apps.
- **Below 50** — only when size matters more than quality; blocky artefacts become visible up close.

#### Why compress images?

- **Faster websites.** Images are usually the heaviest part of a page. Smaller images improve Largest Contentful Paint (LCP), one of Google’s Core Web Vitals.
- **Upload limits.** Forms, marketplaces and content management systems reject files above a size limit.
- **Email and chat.** Gmail allows 25 MB of attachments per message, so smaller photos mean more of them per email.
- **Storage.** Compressing a photo library can free gigabytes on your phone or cloud drive.

#### Private by design

Many online compressors upload your photos to their servers. This one does not: images are decoded, compressed and saved entirely inside your browser tab, and the page never sends them anywhere. You can check it yourself — load the page, switch off Wi-Fi, and compress an image. It still works.

### FAQ

**Is this image compressor really free?**
Yes. There is no sign-up, no watermark, no daily limit and no cap on the number of images. The site is supported by ads, and your photos are never uploaded — not to us and not to advertisers.

**Are my images uploaded to a server?**
No. Compression runs entirely in your browser using its built-in image encoders. Your photos are never uploaded, stored or seen by anyone else.

**How much smaller will my images get?**
It depends on the image. Photos straight from a phone or camera often shrink by 50–80% at quality 75, and by more when you also resize them or convert to WebP. Images that were already heavily compressed shrink less.

**Does compressing an image reduce its quality?**
Lossy compression removes some detail, but at quality 70–85 the difference is usually invisible at normal viewing sizes. Use the before-and-after comparison to check any image before you download it.

**How do I compress a photo to exactly 50 KB, 100 KB or 20 KB?**
Choose **To target size**, click a preset or type your limit in KB, and download. The tool finds the highest quality that fits under the limit and scales the image down only if it has to.

**Why did an image come back the same size?**
If a file is already well optimised, re-encoding it could make it bigger. With **Keep original if smaller** on, the tool returns your original file instead. Turn that option off, lower the quality or convert to WebP to force a smaller file.

**Does it remove EXIF data and GPS location?**
Yes. Every re-encoded image is saved without EXIF metadata such as GPS coordinates, camera model and capture time. The only exception is an image returned unchanged by **Keep original if smaller**, which keeps its original metadata.

**Can I compress iPhone HEIC photos?**
Only in browsers that can open HEIC, such as Safari on iPhone, iPad and Mac. In Chrome, Edge or Firefox, convert the photos first with the [HEIC to JPG Converter](https://justtools.online/image-tools/heic-to-jpg/), then compress the JPGs here.

**Will PNG transparency be kept?**
Yes, when the output is PNG, WebP or AVIF. JPG cannot store transparency, so transparent areas are filled with the background colour you choose (white by default).

**Does it work on phones?**
Yes. It works in current versions of Chrome, Safari, Firefox, Edge and Samsung Internet on Android, iPhone, iPad and desktop computers.

## Word Counter

URL: https://justtools.online/text-tools/word-counter/
Category: Text Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-09-28

Free online word counter: count words, characters, sentences and paragraphs as you type, with reading time, keyword density, readability and limits.

### At a glance

- Counts words, characters (with and without spaces), sentences, paragraphs, lines and unique words **as you type**.
- Hyphenated words and contractions such as “well-known” and “don’t” count as one word, the same as Microsoft Word and Google Docs.
- Unicode-aware: Hindi and other Indic scripts, Chinese, Japanese, Thai and emoji are counted correctly.
- Reading time assumes **238 words per minute** and speaking time **150 words per minute**.
- Shows keyword density for single words and 2–3 word phrases, with optional stop-word filtering.
- Calculates Flesch Reading Ease and Flesch–Kincaid Grade Level for English text.
- Checks text against limits for X posts (280), SEO titles (60), meta descriptions (160), Instagram captions (2,200) and more.
- Text is analysed in your browser and never uploaded. An optional draft autosave uses this browser’s local storage only.

### Features

- **Live counts**: Words, characters, sentences, paragraphs and lines update with every keystroke — even for book-length text.
- **Reading and speaking time**: See how long your text takes to read silently and to deliver as a speech or video script.
- **Keyword density**: Find your most-used words and 2–3 word phrases, with common words filtered out, to spot repetition and check SEO focus.
- **Readability scores**: Flesch Reading Ease and Flesch–Kincaid Grade Level tell you how easy your English text is to read, and for whom.
- **Platform limits**: Progress bars for X posts, SEO titles, meta descriptions, SMS, YouTube, Instagram and LinkedIn show what fits and what is over.
- **Word goal**: Set a target such as 1,500 words for an essay or article and watch the progress bar fill as you write.
- **Case converter and file tools**: Switch to UPPERCASE, lowercase, Title Case or Sentence case, open a .txt or .md file, copy, or download your text — with one-step undo.
- **Private autosave**: Your draft is kept in this browser so a refresh never loses work. Turn it off with one switch; nothing is sent anywhere either way.

### How to count words in your text

1. **Add your text** — Type in the box, paste text from any document, or click **Open file** to load a .txt or .md file.
2. **Read the live counts** — Words, characters, sentences, paragraphs, reading time and speaking time update instantly at the top.
3. **Dig deeper** — Check **Details** for averages and page estimates, then use the tabs for keyword density, character limits and readability.
4. **Set a goal or export** — Enter a word goal to track progress, change the case if needed, then copy or download the finished text.

### Guide

#### How words and characters are counted

A **word** is any run of characters between spaces that contains at least one letter or number. That means “well-known”, “don’t”, “COVID-19” and “2026” each count as one word, while a stray dash or ampersand does not — the same rules Microsoft Word and Google Docs use, so your count matches what an editor or teacher will see.

Languages written without spaces between words — Chinese, Japanese and Thai — are split into words with the Unicode word-segmentation rules built into your browser. Hindi, Marathi, Bengali and other Indic scripts, which do use spaces, are counted like English.

**Characters** are counted the way you see them: an emoji with a skin tone, a flag, or a Devanagari conjunct is one character, even though it is stored as several code points. The Details panel also shows the size in bytes (UTF-8), which matters for databases and some SMS gateways.

**Paragraphs** are counted as non-empty lines, as in Microsoft Word. **Sentences** end at a full stop, question mark, exclamation mark or the Devanagari danda (।).

#### How many pages is 1,000 words?

With a 12-point font such as Times New Roman or Arial and 1-inch margins, a single-spaced page holds about 500 words and a double-spaced page about 250. Headings, short paragraphs and larger fonts reduce that.

| Words | Single-spaced pages | Double-spaced pages | Reading time |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 250 | 0.5 | 1 | about 1 minute |
| 500 | 1 | 2 | about 2 minutes |
| 1,000 | 2 | 4 | about 4 minutes |
| 1,500 | 3 | 6 | about 6 minutes |
| 2,000 | 4 | 8 | about 8 minutes |
| 5,000 | 10 | 20 | about 21 minutes |

#### How reading time and speaking time are calculated

Reading time uses **238 words per minute**, the average silent reading speed for adults reading non-fiction English found in a 2019 review of 190 studies (Brysbaert). Speaking time uses **150 words per minute**, a comfortable pace for presentations, podcasts and video voice-overs.

Technical material is read more slowly and fiction faster, so treat both figures as estimates. For a timed speech, rehearse aloud once and adjust.

#### Character limits cheat sheet

| Where | Limit | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| X (Twitter) post | 280 characters | Standard accounts; every link counts as 23 |
| SEO title tag | ~60 characters | Google truncates by pixel width, roughly 50–60 characters |
| Meta description | ~160 characters | Longer text is usually cut off in results |
| SMS message | 160 characters | Drops to 70 when the text contains emoji or non-Latin letters |
| YouTube title | 100 characters | About 70 are visible in search results |
| Instagram caption | 2,200 characters | Only the first lines show before “more” |
| LinkedIn post | 3,000 characters | Only the first few lines show before “see more” |

#### Understanding readability scores

The **Flesch Reading Ease** score rates text from about 0 to 100 using average sentence length and average syllables per word: the higher the score, the easier the text. The **Flesch–Kincaid Grade Level** turns the same inputs into a US school grade.

| Score | Difficulty | Typical reader |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 90–100 | Very easy | 5th grade (age 10–11) |
| 70–89 | Easy to fairly easy | 6th–7th grade |
| 60–69 | Plain English | 8th–9th grade (age 13–15) |
| 50–59 | Fairly difficult | 10th–12th grade |
| 30–49 | Difficult | College level |
| 0–29 | Very difficult | College graduate |

#### Keyword density and SEO

Keyword density is how often a word or phrase appears as a share of all words. Search engines do not reward a particular percentage, and repeating a phrase unnaturally can hurt. Use the table to spot accidental repetition and to confirm your main topic is clearly present — then write for readers first.

### FAQ

**Is this word counter free and private?**
Yes. It is free with no sign-up and no length limit, and your text is analysed entirely in your browser. Nothing you type or paste is uploaded or stored on a server.

**Does it count hyphenated words and contractions as one word?**
Yes. “Well-known”, “mother-in-law” and “don’t” each count as one word, matching Microsoft Word and Google Docs.

**Are spaces counted as characters?**
The main **Characters** figure includes spaces and line breaks. **Characters (no spaces)** in the Details panel excludes all whitespace.

**How is reading time calculated?**
Reading time is the word count divided by 238 words per minute, the average adult silent reading speed. Speaking time uses 150 words per minute.

**How many words are on one page?**
About 500 words single-spaced or 250 double-spaced, with a 12-point font and 1-inch margins. The Details panel shows both page estimates for your text.

**Does it work with Hindi and other languages?**
Yes. Counting is Unicode-aware, so Hindi, Marathi, Tamil and other Indic scripts, Chinese, Japanese, Arabic and emoji are handled correctly. Readability scores are English-only because the Flesch formulas are.

**What is a good Flesch Reading Ease score?**
For most websites and general readers, 60–70 (plain English) is a good target. Scores above 80 read very easily; below 50 suits specialist or academic audiences.

**What is the ideal keyword density for SEO?**
There is no ideal percentage. Mention your main topic naturally where it helps the reader, and use the density table to catch repetition rather than to hit a number.

**Is my text saved?**
Only if **Save draft in this browser** is on (the default). The draft stays in this browser’s local storage on your device and is never sent anywhere. Turn the switch off to delete it.

**How many characters are allowed in a tweet or a meta description?**
An X (Twitter) post allows 280 characters for standard accounts, and a meta description is best kept to about 160. The **Character limits** tab checks both, plus SEO titles, SMS, YouTube, Instagram and LinkedIn.

## Password Generator

URL: https://justtools.online/security-tools/password-generator/
Category: Security Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-09-29

Generate strong, random passwords, memorable passphrases and PINs with a cryptographically secure generator. Free, instant and private — nothing is stored.

### At a glance

- Uses the browser’s **Web Crypto API** (`crypto.getRandomValues`) with rejection sampling, so every character is uniformly random with no modulo bias.
- Three modes: random **passwords** (4–128 characters), **passphrases** from the EFF short word list, and numeric **PINs** (4–12 digits).
- Options to include or exclude uppercase, lowercase, numbers and symbols, skip look-alike characters (I, l, 1, O, 0) and ban any custom characters.
- Shows strength as bits of entropy and an estimated time to crack at 100 billion guesses per second.
- Generates up to 100 passwords at once, with copy-all and download as a .txt file.
- Passwords are created on your device and are never sent, logged or stored.
- Obvious PINs such as 1111, 1234 and 1212 are never produced.

### Features

- **Truly random**: Built on `crypto.getRandomValues`, the same cryptographically secure source browsers use for encryption keys — not the predictable `Math.random`.
- **Passwords, passphrases and PINs**: Pick a random password for maximum strength, a word-based passphrase you can actually remember, or a numeric PIN for cards and phones.
- **Honest strength meter**: Strength is calculated from real entropy (bits) and turned into an estimated cracking time, so you can see exactly how much length and variety matter.
- **Fits any site’s rules**: Choose character types, guarantee at least one of each, avoid look-alike characters and exclude symbols a website refuses.
- **Easy to read back**: Numbers and symbols are colour-coded so you can type a password on another device without mistakes.
- **Bulk generation**: Create up to 100 passwords in one go for new accounts, Wi-Fi guests or test users, then copy or download them all.

### How to generate a strong password

1. **Choose a type** — Select **Password**, **Passphrase** or **PIN** at the top of the options.
2. **Set the length and characters** — Use at least 16 characters with all four character types for a password, or 5+ words for a passphrase.
3. **Check the strength** — Aim for **Strong** or **Very strong** — at least 60–80 bits of entropy for important accounts.
4. **Copy and save it** — Click **Copy**, paste the password into the website, and store it in a password manager. Click the refresh button for a new one.

### Guide

#### What makes a password strong?

Strength comes from **unpredictability**, measured in bits of entropy. Every extra bit doubles the number of guesses an attacker needs. A password drawn at random from 87 possible characters gains about 6.4 bits per character, so length matters more than anything else: 16 random characters give roughly 103 bits, far beyond the reach of any known attack.

Human-chosen passwords are weak even when they look complex, because attackers try dictionary words, names, dates and common substitutions like “P@ssw0rd” first. A generator removes that pattern entirely — which is why you should never tweak a generated password to make it “more memorable”.

- *Offline attack at 100 billion guesses per second against a fast hash. Websites that store passwords properly (bcrypt, scrypt, Argon2) and limit login attempts make real-world attacks far slower.

| Password | Entropy | Average time to crack* |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 random characters (all types) | ~52 bits | about 5 hours |
| 12 random characters (all types) | ~77 bits | about 30,000 years |
| 16 random characters (all types) | ~103 bits | trillions of years |
| 5-word passphrase + number | ~57 bits | about 11 days |
| 7-word passphrase | ~72 bits | about 1,000 years |
| 6-digit PIN | ~20 bits | less than a second (offline) |

#### Password or passphrase?

Use a **random password** for anything stored in a password manager — you never need to remember it, so make it long. Use a **passphrase** for the few secrets you must type from memory: your password manager’s master password, your computer login, or a Wi-Fi password guests will type. Six or seven random words are both strong and surprisingly easy to remember.

Passphrases here use the Electronic Frontier Foundation’s short word list of 1,296 common, easy-to-spell words, giving about 10.3 bits of entropy per word.

#### Password best practices

- **Use a unique password for every account.** When one site is breached, reused passwords are tried everywhere else within hours.
- **Use a password manager** to store them — Bitwarden, 1Password, KeePass, or the one built into your browser or phone.
- **Turn on two-factor authentication** (an authenticator app or passkey) for email, banking and social accounts.
- **Don’t change strong passwords on a schedule.** Change a password when there is a reason: a breach, a shared device, or a suspicion.
- **Never send passwords by email or chat.** Share them through your password manager’s sharing feature instead.

#### Is it safe to generate passwords online?

It is when the generator runs entirely in your browser, as this one does. The page uses your device’s cryptographic random number generator; the passwords are never transmitted, logged or saved, and they disappear when you close the tab. You can confirm it yourself: load the page, disconnect from the internet and keep generating.

### FAQ

**Is this password generator safe?**
Yes. Passwords are generated locally in your browser with the Web Crypto API and are never sent to a server, logged or stored. Nobody — including us — can see them.

**How long should my password be?**
At least 16 random characters for important accounts, or 12 as an absolute minimum. For passphrases, use five words or more, and six or seven for a master password.

**Are symbols really necessary?**
They help, but length helps more. A 20-character password of letters and numbers is stronger than a 12-character one with symbols. Include symbols unless a website rejects them.

**Why are some symbols left out?**
Quotes, backslashes, backticks, spaces and angle brackets are excluded because many websites, command lines and config files mishandle them. The 25 symbols used are accepted almost everywhere.

**What does “bits of entropy” mean?**
It measures how unpredictable a password is. Each bit doubles the number of possible passwords an attacker must try, so 80 bits is about a million times harder to guess than 60 bits.

**How is the time to crack estimated?**
It assumes an offline attack making 100 billion guesses per second, and that the password is found after trying half of all possibilities on average. Real attacks against well-protected websites are much slower.

**Can I generate many passwords at once?**
Yes. Choose up to 100 in **How many**, then copy them all or download them as a text file.

**Is a passphrase as secure as a random password?**
Per character it is weaker, but per word it is strong: each word adds about 10.3 bits. A six-word passphrase (~62 bits) is comparable to a 10-character random password and much easier to remember.

## JSON Formatter & Validator

URL: https://justtools.online/developer-tools/json-formatter/
Category: Developer Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-09-29

Format, validate, minify and repair JSON online. Get the exact line and column of every error, a collapsible tree view and sorted keys — private, in-browser.

### At a glance

- Formats JSON with 2 spaces, 4 spaces or tabs, or **minifies** it to a single line.
- Validates strictly against the JSON standard (RFC 8259) and reports each error with its **line and column**, highlighting the exact spot.
- **Fix mistakes** mode repairs comments, trailing commas, single quotes, unquoted keys and Python-style True/False/None.
- Keeps numbers exactly as written: large integers such as 12345678901234567890 are not rounded, unlike JavaScript’s JSON.parse.
- Preserves key order and warns about **duplicate keys**; can sort keys alphabetically at every level.
- Includes a collapsible **tree view** for exploring large or deeply nested JSON.
- Runs entirely in your browser: pasted JSON — API responses, tokens, configs — is never uploaded or saved.

### Features

- **Precise error messages**: Instead of “Unexpected token”, you get a plain-English message such as “Expected ',' or '}' after property value” with the line, column and a pointer to the character.
- **One-click repair**: JSON copied from JavaScript, config files or Python often has comments, trailing commas or single quotes. **Fix mistakes** converts it to valid JSON and lists every change.
- **Exact numbers**: IDs, prices and big integers are kept character-for-character, so formatting never silently changes your data.
- **Tree view**: Expand and collapse objects and arrays to explore large responses, with item counts at every level.
- **Beautify or minify**: Choose 2 spaces, 4 spaces or tabs for readability, or minify to remove every unnecessary byte before shipping.
- **Private by design**: Nothing is sent to a server and nothing is stored, so it is safe for API keys, tokens and customer data.

### How to format and validate JSON

1. **Paste your JSON** — Paste into the **Input** box, click **Open file** to load a .json file, or try the **Sample**.
2. **Read the result** — Valid JSON is formatted instantly on the right. If it is invalid, the error bar shows the line, column and reason.
3. **Fix any errors** — Click **Show in input** to jump to the problem, or **Fix automatically** to repair comments, trailing commas and quotes.
4. **Copy or download** — Pick 2 spaces, 4 spaces, tabs or **Minify**, optionally sort keys, then copy the output or download it as a .json file.

### Guide

#### The most common JSON errors — and how to fix them

JSON is stricter than JavaScript. These mistakes cause almost every “invalid JSON” error. All of them except missing commas, missing brackets and leading zeros can be repaired automatically with **Fix mistakes**.

| Error | Invalid | Valid |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Trailing comma | `{"a": 1,}` | `{"a": 1}` |
| Single quotes | `{'a': 'b'}` | `{"a": "b"}` |
| Unquoted key | `{a: 1}` | `{"a": 1}` |
| Comments | `{"a": 1 // note}` | `{"a": 1}` |
| Missing comma | `{"a": 1 "b": 2}` | `{"a": 1, "b": 2}` |
| Python literals | `{"ok": True, "x": None}` | `{"ok": true, "x": null}` |
| Leading zero | `{"n": 007}` | `{"n": 7}` |
| Raw line break in a string | `"line one` ↵ `line two"` | `"line one\nline two"` |

#### Why numbers stay exact here

JavaScript stores every number as a 64-bit float, so `JSON.parse` silently rounds integers above 9,007,199,254,740,991: `12345678901234567890` becomes `12345678901234567000`. That corrupts order IDs, tweet IDs and account numbers. This formatter keeps each number’s original text, so the output is exactly what you pasted — only the whitespace changes.

#### Pretty-printed vs minified JSON

- **Pretty-printed** (2 or 4 spaces, or tabs) is for people: logs, config files, code reviews and documentation.
- **Minified** removes all optional whitespace and is for machines: API payloads, local storage and anything sent over the network. For typical JSON it is 10–30% smaller than 2-space formatting, before gzip.
- **Sorted keys** make two JSON documents easy to compare in a diff, because the same keys always appear in the same order.

#### JSON syntax in 60 seconds

- Values are strings, numbers, `true`, `false`, `null`, objects `{}` or arrays `[]`.
- Strings and keys use **double quotes** only. Escape `"` as `\"` and a backslash as `\\`.
- Items are separated by commas, with no comma after the last one.
- Numbers have no leading zeros, no `+` sign, and no `NaN` or `Infinity`.
- Comments are not part of JSON. Use JSONC or JSON5 files if you need them, and strip comments before parsing.

### FAQ

**Is it safe to paste API responses or tokens here?**
Yes. The formatter runs entirely in your browser; your JSON is never sent to a server, logged or saved. Close the tab and it is gone.

**How do I find where my JSON is broken?**
The red error bar gives the line and column and shows the line with a ^ under the problem. Click **Show in input** to jump straight to it.

**What does “Fix mistakes” change?**
It removes comments and trailing commas, converts single-quoted strings, quotes bare property names and turns Python’s True, False and None into true, false and null. Everything it changed is listed, and you can replace your input with the fixed JSON.

**Why does my number look different in other tools?**
Most online formatters use JavaScript’s JSON.parse, which rounds integers larger than 2^53. This tool keeps numbers exactly as written, so large IDs stay correct.

**Can it handle large JSON files?**
Yes — multi-megabyte files work, limited only by your device’s memory. Syntax colouring switches off above about 200 KB of output to keep the page fast.

**Does it support JSON5 or JSONC?**
Turn on **Fix mistakes** to read the most common JSON5/JSONC features — comments, trailing commas, single quotes and unquoted keys — and convert them into standard JSON.

**What happens with duplicate keys?**
The JSON standard leaves duplicates undefined; most parsers keep the last value. This tool does the same and shows a warning with the line of each duplicate, so you can fix the source.

**Can I download the result?**
Yes. Click **Download** to save the output as formatted.json or minified.json, or **Copy** to put it on your clipboard.

## EMI Calculator

URL: https://justtools.online/calculators/emi-calculator/
Category: Calculators
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-09-29

Calculate your loan EMI, total interest and full repayment schedule instantly. See yearly charts, the impact of prepayments and download the schedule.

### At a glance

- Uses the standard reducing-balance formula **EMI = P × r × (1 + r)^n ÷ ((1 + r)^n − 1)**, where r is the monthly interest rate and n the number of months.
- Shows the monthly EMI, total interest, total amount payable and the principal-to-interest split.
- Builds a full **month-by-month and year-by-year repayment schedule**, downloadable as a CSV file.
- Models an **extra monthly prepayment** and reports the interest saved and how much sooner the loan closes.
- Supports rupees (with lakh/crore formatting), US dollars, euros, pounds and UAE dirhams.
- Example: ₹50 lakh at 8.5% for 20 years gives an EMI of ₹43,391 and total interest of ₹54,13,879.
- Everything is calculated in your browser; nothing you enter is stored or sent anywhere.

### Features

- **Instant, exact EMI**: Change the amount, rate or tenure with a slider or by typing, and the EMI and totals update immediately — to the rupee.
- **Yearly breakdown chart**: See how each year’s payments split between principal and interest. Early years are mostly interest; the chart shows exactly how that shifts.
- **Full repayment schedule**: Switch between a yearly and a monthly table showing principal, interest and the balance left, then download it as CSV for Excel or Google Sheets.
- **Prepayment planner**: Add an extra amount every month to see the interest you save and how many years sooner the loan is closed.
- **Indian number format**: Amounts appear as ₹50,00,000 with “50 lakh” written out, and the chart axis uses L and Cr, so large numbers are easy to read.
- **Works for any loan**: Home loans, car loans, personal loans, education loans and mortgages all use the same formula — just enter your figures.

### How to calculate your EMI

1. **Enter the loan amount** — Type the amount you will borrow or drag the slider. Pick your currency if it isn’t rupees.
2. **Enter the interest rate** — Use the annual rate from your lender’s offer, for example 8.5%.
3. **Set the tenure** — Choose the repayment period in years or months. Longer tenures lower the EMI but raise the total interest.
4. **Read the results** — Your EMI, total interest and total payable appear instantly. Add an extra monthly payment to see how prepaying helps, and download the schedule if you need it.

### Guide

#### What is an EMI?

An EMI (equated monthly instalment) is the fixed amount you pay your lender every month until a loan is repaid. Each EMI covers that month’s interest on the outstanding balance, and the rest reduces the principal. Because the balance falls over time, the interest part of each EMI shrinks and the principal part grows — even though the EMI itself stays the same.

#### The EMI formula

**EMI = P × r × (1 + r)^n ÷ ((1 + r)^n − 1)**

Here **P** is the loan amount, **r** is the monthly interest rate (the annual rate ÷ 12 ÷ 100), and **n** is the number of monthly payments. For ₹10,00,000 at 10% a year for 20 years: r = 10 ÷ 12 ÷ 100 = 0.008333 and n = 240, which gives an EMI of **₹9,650**. Over 20 years you would repay ₹23,16,052, of which ₹13,16,052 is interest.

#### EMI for a ₹10 lakh loan at different rates

Monthly EMI, rounded to the nearest rupee. Scale in proportion for other amounts: a ₹50 lakh loan has five times the EMI.

| Tenure | 8% | 8.5% | 9% | 10% | 12% |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5 years | ₹20,276 | ₹20,517 | ₹20,758 | ₹21,247 | ₹22,244 |
| 10 years | ₹12,133 | ₹12,399 | ₹12,668 | ₹13,215 | ₹14,347 |
| 15 years | ₹9,557 | ₹9,847 | ₹10,143 | ₹10,746 | ₹12,002 |
| 20 years | ₹8,364 | ₹8,678 | ₹8,997 | ₹9,650 | ₹11,011 |
| 25 years | ₹7,718 | ₹8,052 | ₹8,392 | ₹9,087 | ₹10,532 |
| 30 years | ₹7,338 | ₹7,689 | ₹8,046 | ₹8,776 | ₹10,286 |

#### How prepayment saves money

Any amount you pay on top of the EMI goes straight to the principal, so every later month charges interest on a smaller balance. Take a ₹50 lakh home loan at 8.5% for 20 years: the EMI is ₹43,391 and the total interest ₹54,13,879. Paying just **₹5,000 extra every month** closes the loan in 15 years 7 months instead of 20 and saves about **₹13.9 lakh** in interest.

Prepayments save the most early in the loan, when the balance — and so the interest — is highest. Many lenders also let you keep the tenure and reduce the EMI instead; this calculator shows the “shorter tenure” option, which saves more interest.

#### How to lower your EMI or total interest

- **Make a bigger down payment.** Every rupee you don’t borrow saves interest for the whole tenure.
- **Compare interest rates.** On a ₹50 lakh, 20-year loan, 0.5% lower rate cuts the EMI by roughly ₹1,600 a month.
- **Choose the shortest tenure you can afford.** A longer tenure lowers the EMI but multiplies the total interest.
- **Prepay whenever you can,** especially in the first years. Check your loan agreement for any prepayment charges first.
- **Keep your EMIs affordable.** A common rule of thumb is to keep all EMIs together below 40–50% of your monthly take-home income.

### FAQ

**How is EMI calculated?**
With the reducing-balance formula EMI = P × r × (1 + r)^n ÷ ((1 + r)^n − 1), where P is the loan amount, r the monthly rate (annual rate ÷ 12 ÷ 100) and n the number of months. This calculator applies it exactly and builds the full schedule from it.

**Why is my bank’s EMI slightly different?**
Lenders may round differently, count interest from the disbursal date, or add processing fees and insurance to the loan. The formula is the same, so the difference is normally small.

**Does a longer tenure save money?**
No. A longer tenure lowers the EMI but increases the total interest. A ₹10 lakh loan at 10% costs ₹2,74,823 in interest over 5 years but ₹13,16,052 over 20 years.

**Is it better to reduce the EMI or the tenure after a prepayment?**
Reducing the tenure saves more interest; reducing the EMI eases your monthly budget. If you can comfortably keep paying the same EMI, choose the shorter tenure.

**Can I calculate EMI for a car, personal or education loan?**
Yes. All of these are standard reducing-balance loans. Enter the amount, rate and tenure from your offer — or tap one of the examples to start.

**Does this work for a flat-rate loan?**
No. Some personal and vehicle loans quote a “flat” rate charged on the original amount for the whole tenure, which costs much more than the same reducing rate. Ask the lender for the reducing-balance rate (or APR) and enter that.

**Can I download the repayment schedule?**
Yes. Click **CSV** above the schedule to download every month’s payment, principal, interest, extra payment and balance for Excel or Google Sheets.

**Is my data saved?**
No. The calculations run in your browser, and nothing you enter is stored or sent anywhere.

## Merge PDF

URL: https://justtools.online/pdf-tools/merge-pdf/
Category: PDF Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-09-29

Merge PDF files online for free. Combine PDFs in any order, pick exact pages from each and download one file — processed in your browser with no upload.

### At a glance

- Merges PDFs **inside your browser** with the open-source pdf-lib library — files are never uploaded to a server.
- Reorder files by dragging, with the arrow buttons, or by sorting them by name.
- Choose pages per file with ranges such as `1-3, 5, 8-`, `odd`, `even` or reversed ranges like `6-2`.
- With a single PDF, the same page selection extracts or reorders pages into a new file.
- Copies pages exactly as they are: text stays selectable, and fonts and images are not re-compressed.
- No limit on the number of files, no watermark and no sign-up.
- Password-protected PDFs cannot be merged until the password is removed.

### Features

- **Nothing is uploaded**: Contracts, bank statements and ID documents stay on your device. The merge runs in your browser tab, so there is no server copy to worry about.
- **Pick exact pages**: Type a range for any file — `1-3, 5, 8-` — to leave out covers, blank pages or appendices. Leave it empty to include every page.
- **Easy reordering**: Drag files into place on a computer, use the up and down arrows on a phone, or sort by file name in one click.
- **Lossless quality**: Pages are copied as they are, not re-rendered, so text stays sharp and searchable and images keep their original quality.
- **Extract pages too**: Add one PDF and enter the pages you want to keep to split out chapters, remove pages or change their order.
- **Free with no limits**: No watermark, no file-count cap and no account. Large files are limited only by your device’s memory.

### How to merge PDF files

1. **Add your PDFs** — Drag and drop PDF files onto the box or click to browse. Add as many as you need.
2. **Put them in order** — Drag files up or down, use the arrow buttons, or click **Sort by name**. The numbers show the final order.
3. **Choose pages (optional)** — Leave the page box empty to include every page, or type a selection such as `1-3, 5` for that file.
4. **Merge and download** — Enter a file name and click **Merge PDF**. The combined file downloads immediately.

### Guide

#### Page selection cheat sheet

Each file has its own page box. Pages are added in the order you type them, and page numbers start at 1.

| Type | Pages included |
| --- | --- |
| (empty) or `all` | Every page |
| `1-3, 5` | Pages 1, 2, 3 and 5 |
| `8-` | Page 8 to the last page |
| `-4` | Pages 1 to 4 |
| `odd` / `even` | Every odd or every even page |
| `5-1` | Pages 5, 4, 3, 2, 1 (reversed) |
| `3, 1, 2` | Pages 3, 1 and 2 in that order |

#### Why merge PDFs in your browser?

Most PDF websites upload your files to their servers, process them there and keep them for a while before deleting. For tax returns, contracts, medical reports or anything with personal data, that is an unnecessary risk.

This tool uses pdf-lib, a well-established open-source PDF library, running inside your browser tab. Your files are read from your disk, combined in memory and saved straight back to your downloads folder. You can load the page, disconnect from the internet and merge — it still works.

#### Common uses

- **Job and college applications:** combine a CV, cover letter and certificates into the single PDF a portal asks for.
- **Scanned documents:** join pages scanned one at a time into one file, in the right order.
- **Invoices and statements:** bundle a month of invoices or bank statements for your accountant.
- **Reports:** add a cover page or appendix to a report exported from Word or Google Docs.
- **Trimming:** keep only the pages you need from a long PDF before emailing it.

#### Tips for the best result

- Check the page count shown under each file before merging — it tells you the file was read correctly.
- If a PDF is password-protected, open it with the password and save a copy without one first.
- The merged file is roughly the sum of the pages you selected. To make it smaller for email, run it through a PDF compressor afterwards.
- Form fields and bookmarks from the original files are not guaranteed to carry over; page content always does.

### FAQ

**Is it safe to merge confidential PDFs here?**
Yes. The PDFs are processed entirely in your browser and never uploaded, so no copy exists anywhere except on your device.

**How many PDFs can I merge at once?**
There is no fixed limit. Dozens of files work fine; very large batches are limited only by your device’s memory.

**Can I merge only some pages of a PDF?**
Yes. Type the pages you want in that file’s page box, for example `1-3, 5` or `8-`. Leave the box empty to include every page.

**Will merging reduce quality?**
No. Pages are copied as they are rather than re-rendered, so text stays selectable and images keep their original resolution.

**Can I change the order of pages, not just files?**
Yes — pages are added in the order you type them. `3, 1, 2` puts page 3 first. To interleave pages from different files, add the same file more than once with different page selections.

**Why can’t I add a password-protected PDF?**
Encrypted PDFs cannot be read without their password. Open the file with its password in a PDF reader, save or print a copy without protection, and add that copy.

**Does it work on a phone?**
Yes. It works in Chrome, Safari, Firefox and Edge on Android and iPhone. Use the arrow buttons to reorder files on a touch screen.

**Is there a watermark or a file-size limit?**
No watermark, no sign-up and no artificial size limit. The merged PDF contains only your pages.

## Image Resizer

URL: https://justtools.online/image-tools/image-resizer/
Category: Image Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-09-29

Resize JPG, PNG and WebP images by pixels, percentage or social media presets. Crop to fill or fit, batch resize and download a ZIP — no upload needed.

### At a glance

- Resizes by exact **pixels** (with or without keeping proportions), by **percentage** (5–400%), or to a **preset** size.
- Presets include Instagram square (1080×1080) and portrait (1080×1350), Story/Reel (1080×1920), YouTube thumbnail (1280×720), link previews (1200×630), Pinterest (1000×1500) and HD, Full HD and 4K screens.
- When the new shape differs from the photo, choose **crop to fill**, **fit with a border** in any colour, or **stretch**.
- Resizes any number of images at once and downloads them individually or as a ZIP.
- Saves as the original format, JPG, WebP or lossless PNG, with adjustable JPG/WebP quality.
- Uses multi-step downscaling for sharp results and respects each photo’s EXIF orientation.
- Runs entirely in your browser: images are never uploaded.

### Features

- **Exact pixel sizes**: Type a width, a height or both. With proportions locked, every photo keeps its shape; unlock them to make every image exactly the size you need.
- **Ready-made social sizes**: One click for Instagram posts and stories, YouTube thumbnails, link previews for Facebook and LinkedIn, X posts, Pinterest pins and standard screen sizes.
- **Crop, fit or stretch**: **Crop to fill** trims the edges evenly, **fit with border** keeps the whole photo and adds bars in your colour, and **stretch** matches the size exactly.
- **Batch resizing**: Drop in a whole folder of photos. Change a setting and every image is redone automatically, then download them all as one ZIP.
- **Sharp results**: Big reductions are done in several steps, which avoids the jagged edges and shimmering you get from a single resize.
- **Private and free**: No upload, no watermark, no sign-up and no limit on the number or size of images.

### How to resize an image

1. **Add your images** — Drag and drop photos, click to browse or paste with Ctrl+V. You can add as many as you like.
2. **Choose the new size** — Pick **Pixels** and type a width or height, **Percentage** to scale, or **Social & screen sizes** for a preset.
3. **Decide how to fill the shape** — If the new size has a different shape, choose **Crop to fill**, **Fit with border** or **Stretch**.
4. **Download** — Pick a format, then download each image or click **Download all** for a ZIP.

### Guide

#### Crop to fill, fit with border or stretch?

When a photo’s shape doesn’t match the new size — a landscape photo going into a 1080×1080 square, say — something has to give.

- **Crop to fill** scales the photo to cover the whole frame and trims the edges evenly. Nothing is distorted and there are no bars. Best for social posts and thumbnails.
- **Fit with border** keeps the entire photo and fills the leftover space with a colour you choose. Best when nothing may be cut off, such as documents and product shots.
- **Stretch** forces the photo to the exact size, distorting it if the shapes differ. Use it only when the shapes are already almost the same.

#### Recommended image sizes used by the presets

| Where | Size (px) | Aspect ratio |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Instagram square post | 1080 × 1080 | 1:1 |
| Instagram portrait post | 1080 × 1350 | 4:5 |
| Instagram / WhatsApp Story, Reel | 1080 × 1920 | 9:16 |
| YouTube thumbnail | 1280 × 720 | 16:9 |
| Facebook / LinkedIn link preview | 1200 × 630 | 1.91:1 |
| X (Twitter) post image | 1600 × 900 | 16:9 |
| Pinterest pin | 1000 × 1500 | 2:3 |
| Full HD screen / video frame | 1920 × 1080 | 16:9 |

#### Does resizing reduce quality?

**Making an image smaller** keeps it looking sharp — the tool downscales in several steps to avoid jagged edges. **Making an image larger** cannot add detail that was never captured: enlarging a small photo by more than about 150% makes it look soft. For the best result, start from the largest original you have.

To make files smaller without changing their dimensions, use the [Image Compressor](https://justtools.online/image-tools/image-compressor/) instead — or resize first and then compress.

#### Pixels, DPI and print size

Screens only care about pixels. For printing, divide the pixel size by the print resolution: at 300 DPI (photo quality), a 1800 × 1200 px image prints at 6 × 4 inches, and a 3000 × 2400 px image at 10 × 8 inches. For posters viewed from a distance, 150 DPI is usually enough.

### FAQ

**How do I resize an image without stretching it?**
Keep **proportions locked** and enter only a width or a height — the other side is calculated automatically. For an exact size with a different shape, use **Crop to fill** or **Fit with border** instead of stretching.

**Can I resize many photos at once?**
Yes. Add as many images as you like; every one is resized with the same settings, and you can download them all together as a ZIP file.

**Are my photos uploaded?**
No. Resizing happens entirely in your browser, so your photos never leave your device.

**What size should an Instagram post be?**
1080 × 1080 px for a square post or 1080 × 1350 px for a portrait (4:5) post. Stories and Reels use 1080 × 1920 px. All three are one-click presets here.

**Will resizing reduce the file size?**
Making an image smaller in pixels almost always makes the file smaller too. For precise control over file size, such as hitting 100 KB, use the Image Compressor.

**Can I enlarge a small image?**
Yes, by entering a bigger size or a percentage above 100%. The image gets bigger, but it cannot gain detail, so large enlargements look soft.

**Which format should I save in?**
JPG for photos that must work everywhere, WebP for smaller files on websites, and PNG for screenshots, graphics or images with transparency.

**Does it keep my photo the right way up?**
Yes. Phone photos are rotated according to their EXIF orientation before resizing, and the saved file is always upright.

## QR Code Generator

URL: https://justtools.online/qr-tools/qr-code-generator/
Category: QR & Barcode Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-09-29

Create free QR codes for links, UPI payments, Wi-Fi, WhatsApp, contacts and more. Add colours and a logo, download PNG or SVG. Codes never expire.

### At a glance

- Creates **static** QR codes: the content is stored in the code itself, so it never expires, needs no account and cannot be switched off.
- Nine types: link, text, **UPI payment**, Wi-Fi, WhatsApp, contact card (vCard), email, phone call and SMS.
- UPI codes use the standard `upi://pay` format that Google Pay, PhonePe, Paytm, BHIM and every other UPI app can scan, with an optional fixed amount.
- Custom colours, three dot styles, three corner styles and an optional centre logo.
- Downloads as **PNG** (512, 1024 or 2048 px) or scalable **SVG** for print, or copies the image to the clipboard.
- Supports all four error-correction levels (L 7%, M 15%, Q 25%, H 30%); adding a logo switches to H automatically.
- Generated in your browser — nothing you enter is sent anywhere, and scans are never tracked.

### Features

- **Never expires**: Many “free” QR sites create codes that redirect through their servers and stop working after a trial. These codes contain your content directly and work forever.
- **UPI payment QR**: Enter a UPI ID, payee name and optional amount to get a code customers can pay with any UPI app — ideal for shops, stalls and invoices.
- **Wi-Fi in one scan**: Guests point their camera at the code and join your network without typing the password. Works with modern iPhone and Android cameras.
- **Your brand, your colours**: Pick dot and corner colours, choose square, rounded or dot styles, and put your logo in the middle. A contrast check warns you before a code becomes hard to scan.
- **Print-ready files**: Download a sharp PNG up to 2048 px, or an SVG that stays crisp at any size — from business cards to banners.
- **Private by design**: Codes are generated on your device. There is no redirect link, so nobody can see who scans your code or when.

### How to create a QR code

1. **Choose what the code opens** — Pick **Link**, **UPI payment**, **Wi-Fi**, **WhatsApp**, **Contact** or another type.
2. **Fill in the details** — Type your link, UPI ID, network name or contact details. The preview updates as you type.
3. **Style it (optional)** — Change the colours and dot or corner style, and add your logo. Keep dark dots on a light background.
4. **Test and download** — Scan the preview with your phone, then download PNG or SVG, or copy the image.

### Guide

#### Static vs dynamic QR codes

A **static** QR code — the kind this tool makes — stores your link or text directly in its pattern. It works forever, needs no account and does not depend on any company staying in business. The trade-off: to change the destination you print a new code.

A **dynamic** QR code stores a short redirect link owned by a QR service. You can change where it points and see scan statistics, but it usually needs a paid plan, and the code stops working if the subscription lapses or the service shuts down. For menus, packaging, business cards and payment codes, static is the safer choice.

#### How to make a UPI payment QR code

Choose **UPI payment**, enter the UPI ID (VPA) that should receive the money — for example `yourshop@okhdfcbank` — and the name customers should see. Add an amount for a fixed bill, or leave it empty so the payer types the amount. A note such as an order number appears in the payment description.

Before printing, scan the code with your own UPI app and check that the payee name is correct. Never share a code that pays into someone else’s account.

#### Tips for QR codes that always scan

- **Keep contrast high:** dark dots on a light background. Light-on-dark codes fail in some scanner apps.
- **Keep the quiet zone:** leave the white border around the code; scanners use it to find the edges.
- **Print big enough:** at least 2 × 2 cm (0.8 in). A good rule is one unit of code size for every ten units of scanning distance.
- **Shorter content, simpler code:** long text makes the pattern denser and harder to scan from a distance.
- **Test before you print:** scan with at least two different phones, including an older one.
- **Use SVG for print:** it scales to any size without blurring.

#### Error correction levels explained

Error correction lets a code still scan when part of it is dirty, damaged or covered by a logo. More correction means a denser pattern.

| Level | Can recover | Best for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| L | about 7% | Screens and clean indoor use |
| M | about 15% | Most printed codes (default) |
| Q | about 25% | Packaging and outdoor signs |
| H | about 30% | Codes with a logo, or harsh conditions |

### FAQ

**Are these QR codes really free forever?**
Yes. They are static codes with your content inside them, so there is nothing to renew and nothing that can expire. There is no sign-up, no watermark and no scan limit.

**Can I create a QR code for UPI payments?**
Yes. Choose **UPI payment**, enter your UPI ID and name, and optionally an amount. The code works with Google Pay, PhonePe, Paytm, BHIM and any other UPI app.

**Will a logo stop my QR code from working?**
Not if it stays small. Adding a logo switches error correction to H (30%), which lets scanners read the code even with the centre covered. Keep the logo size moderate and always test by scanning.

**PNG or SVG — which should I download?**
Use PNG for websites, WhatsApp and documents. Use SVG for printing, because it stays perfectly sharp at any size.

**Can I track how many people scan my code?**
No — and that is deliberate. Tracking requires a dynamic code that redirects through a third-party server. These codes go straight to your content, so scans stay private.

**How do I share my Wi-Fi with a QR code?**
Choose **Wi-Fi**, enter the network name and password, and pick the security type (WPA for almost all routers). Guests scan it with their phone camera to join.

**Can I edit a QR code after printing it?**
No. A static code cannot change after it is printed. If your link might change, point the code at a page you control, such as your website’s home page.

**Is my information sent anywhere?**
No. The code is generated in your browser. UPI IDs, Wi-Fi passwords and contact details never leave your device.

### How to convert text to handwriting

2. **Pick a handwriting style** — Choose one of seven styles. For Hindi, choose **Hindi + English**.

4. **Download** — Check each page in the preview, then download a PDF or PNG images.

### Guide

#### Tips for the most realistic handwriting

- **Keep variation moderate.** Around 4–6 looks natural; 0 looks like a font, 10 looks rushed.
- **Match size to the line gap.** Letters should fill roughly two-thirds of the space between ruled lines.
- **Use blue or blue-black ink** on ruled paper for the classic notebook look.
- **Add the scanned look** if the page will be shared as a photo, and press **Rewrite** until you like the result.
- **Break long paragraphs** into shorter ones — real handwritten pages have more white space than typed ones.

#### Great uses for handwritten pages

If a teacher or exam asks for handwritten work, they usually mean written by you. Check the rules before submitting a generated page.

- Personal notes, study sheets and journals that feel more personal than print.
- Handwritten-style letters, cards and invitations.
- Mock-ups and designs for posters, social posts and presentations.
- Practice sheets that show what neat handwriting looks like.

#### Writing in Hindi and other scripts

Choose **Hindi + English** to write Devanagari — Hindi, Marathi, Nepali and Sanskrit — alongside English on the same page. Hindi words are drawn whole, so conjuncts such as क्ष and matras stay correctly joined; English letters still get individual variation.

### FAQ

**Is this text to handwriting converter free?**
Yes. It is free with no sign-up, no watermark and no page limit.

**Can I write in Hindi?**
Yes. Pick the **Hindi + English** handwriting style. It supports Devanagari, so Hindi, Marathi and Nepali text is written correctly, and you can mix it with English.

**How do I download my handwritten pages?**
Click **PDF** for a single A4 PDF with every page, or **PNG** for images. With more than one page, the PNGs come in a ZIP file.

**Why does every letter look slightly different?**
That is the natural variation that makes the page look handwritten. Lower **Natural variation** for neater writing, or press **Rewrite** to get a new version.

**What size are the pages?**
A4 portrait. PNG images are 1240 × 1754 pixels (150 DPI), which prints clearly on A4 paper; the PDF uses exact A4 page size.

**Is my text uploaded or saved?**
No text is uploaded — everything is drawn in your browser. A draft is kept in this browser’s local storage so a refresh doesn’t lose your work; press **Clear** to remove it.

**Can I use the handwritten pages for school assignments?**
The tool makes realistic pages, but teachers who ask for handwritten work usually expect your own writing. Check your school’s rules first.

**Which fonts are used?**
Open-licensed handwriting fonts from Google Fonts: Homemade Apple, Caveat, Indie Flower, Shadows Into Light, Nothing You Could Do, Patrick Hand and Kalam. They are served from this website, not from Google.

## Images to PDF

- Runs in your browser: images are never uploaded, and there is no watermark or page limit.

### Features

- **No quality loss**: Most converters re-compress every photo. Here, upright JPG and PNG files are placed in the PDF exactly as they are, so text in scans stays sharp.
- **Order and rotate**: Drag thumbnails into place, sort by name, and rotate sideways scans — the numbers show the final page order.
- **Right page size**: A4 for most of the world, Letter or Legal for the US, or pages that match each image exactly. Auto orientation turns the page for landscape photos.

- **Private and unlimited**: Nothing is uploaded, nothing is stored, and there is no limit on the number of images.

### How to convert JPG images to PDF
