Only a little. The watermark is stored once as a small image (typically 20–80 KB for text) and reused on every page, however many there are.

## HTML to PDF

URL: https://justtools.online/pdf-tools/html-to-pdf/
Category: PDF Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-09-30

Convert HTML code or an .html file to PDF with real, selectable text and clickable links. Choose A4 or Letter, margins and backgrounds. Free, no upload.

### At a glance

- Turns **HTML code or an .html file** into a PDF using your browser’s own print engine, so text stays **selectable and searchable** and links stay **clickable**.
- Works with a full page (with its own `<style>`) or a fragment such as `<h1>Hello</h1>`, which gets clean default styling.
- Page sizes **A4, Letter, Legal, A3 and A5**, portrait or landscape, with none, narrow, normal or wide margins.
- A live preview shows the page at its printed width, with dashed lines where the page breaks will fall.
- Keeps background colours, and can stop images, table rows and code blocks being cut in half across pages.
- JavaScript in the HTML is **not run**, for safety: pages that build their content with scripts need to be saved from the browser instead.
- The HTML never leaves your device — nothing is uploaded to a server.

### Features

- **Real text, not a screenshot**: The PDF is made by the browser’s print engine, so text is sharp at any zoom, can be searched and copied, and links work.
- **See page breaks first**: The preview is drawn at the exact paper width and marks where each new page starts, so you can fix the layout before saving.
- **Invoices and templates**: Ideal for HTML invoices, receipts, email templates, reports and resumes. Try the sample invoice to see how it works.
- **Clean page breaks**: Images, table rows and code blocks move to the next page instead of being sliced across two.
- **Your page setup wins**: The page size and margins you choose here override any @page rules in the HTML, so the PDF comes out as you expect.
- **Private and safe**: Everything happens in your browser, and scripts in the HTML are blocked so pasted code can’t do anything unexpected.

### How to convert HTML to PDF

1. **Add your HTML** — Paste HTML into the editor, click **Open file** to load an .html file, or try the **Sample invoice**.
2. **Set up the page** — Choose the **page size**, orientation and margins, and check the preview and its page-break lines.
3. **Save as PDF** — Click **Save as PDF**. In the print window, set the destination to **Save as PDF** and turn off **Headers and footers**.
4. **Download** — Click **Save** and choose where to keep the PDF. Its name is taken from the file name box or the page’s title.

### Guide

#### Getting a perfect PDF

**Use absolute links for images and styles.** A relative link like `images/logo.png` only works if you set the **Base URL** to the site the HTML came from, for example `https://example.com/`. Images embedded as `data:` URLs always work.

**Turn off headers and footers** in the print window (under *More settings* in Chrome and Edge) to remove the date, title and page URL printed at the edges.

**Force a new page** anywhere by adding `<div style="break-before: page"></div>` to the HTML. Headings are kept with the paragraph that follows them.

For the most faithful result, use **Chrome or Edge** on a computer — they follow the page size and margins exactly. Other browsers work too but may ignore some print settings.

#### Which page size to choose

| Page size | Dimensions | Typical use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A4 | 210 × 297 mm | India, Europe and most of the world |
| Letter | 8.5 × 11 in (216 × 279 mm) | USA and Canada |
| Legal | 8.5 × 14 in (216 × 356 mm) | US legal documents and contracts |
| A3 | 297 × 420 mm | Posters, wide tables and diagrams |
| A5 | 148 × 210 mm | Booklets, receipts and small notices |

### FAQ

**Is the text in the PDF selectable?**
Yes. Unlike converters that take a screenshot of the page, this uses the browser’s print engine, so text can be selected, searched and copied, and links remain clickable.

**Why doesn’t my JavaScript run?**
Scripts are blocked so that pasted code can’t act on this site or your device. If a page builds its content with JavaScript, open it in your browser and use **Print → Save as PDF** there instead.

**Can I convert a website URL to PDF?**
Not directly — browsers don’t allow one site to read another site’s pages. Open the website and press **Ctrl + P** (**Cmd + P** on a Mac), or save the page as HTML and open that file here.

**Why are my images missing?**
The images probably use relative links. Enter the website address in **Base URL**, or change the links to full `https://` addresses. Images on your computer must be embedded as data URLs.

**How do I remove the date and URL at the top and bottom?**
Those are the browser’s headers and footers. In the print window open **More settings** and untick **Headers and footers**.

**Does it work on a phone?**
Yes. On Android, choose **Save as PDF** as the printer. On iPhone, open the share sheet from the print preview and save it to Files.

## Flatten PDF

URL: https://justtools.online/pdf-tools/flatten-pdf/
Category: PDF Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-09-30

Flatten a PDF online: turn filled form fields, signatures, comments and highlights into fixed page content no one can edit. Free, private, no upload.

### At a glance

- **Flattening** turns interactive parts of a PDF — form fields, checkboxes, dropdowns, comments, highlights, stamps and drawn signatures — into ordinary page content that can’t be edited.
- The tool first **counts the form fields and comments** in your file, so you know what will be flattened.
- **Forms & comments** mode keeps text selectable and the file small; filled values look exactly as they did in the form.
- **Everything to images** mode turns each page into a picture at 150, 200 or 300 DPI, so nothing can be selected, copied or edited.
- Links and bookmarks are kept in Forms & comments mode.
- Password-protected PDFs can be flattened after entering the password; the flattened copy has no password.
- Runs entirely in your browser with QPDF (WebAssembly) and PDF.js — the file is never uploaded.

### Features

- **Lock filled forms**: Send a completed application, tax form or agreement knowing the values can’t be changed by the next person who opens it.
- **Same look everywhere**: Form values and comments can look different — or vanish — in some viewers and when printed. Flattened, they always show.
- **Know what’s inside**: See how many form fields and comments your PDF has before you flatten it, and what’s left afterwards.
- **Two strengths**: Keep searchable text with Forms & comments, or choose Everything to images for a page no one can edit or copy.
- **Portal-friendly**: Some upload portals reject fillable PDFs or lose the values. A flattened PDF is accepted like any scanned document.
- **Private**: Your form stays on your device. No upload, no sign-up and no watermark.

### How to flatten a PDF

1. **Open the PDF** — Drop the filled form or annotated PDF onto the box. Enter its password if it has one.
2. **Check what’s in it** — The tool shows how many **form fields** and **comments or drawings** it found.
3. **Choose how** — Pick **Forms & comments** (recommended) or **Everything to images**, with an image quality.
4. **Flatten and download** — Click **Flatten PDF**. The flattened copy downloads and the tool confirms nothing editable is left.

### Guide

#### Which mode should I use?

|  | Forms & comments | Everything to images |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Form fields and comments | Locked into the page | Locked into the page |
| Text can be selected and searched | Yes | No |
| Page content can be edited in a PDF editor | Harder, but possible | No — only as a picture |
| File size | About the same | Larger (depends on quality) |
| Links and bookmarks | Kept | Removed |
| Best for | Forms, signed agreements, reviewed drafts | Documents you don’t want copied or changed |

#### When to flatten a PDF

Flatten a form **after filling it in and before sending it** — for example a job application, a KYC form, a bank mandate or a government form. It stops anyone accidentally or deliberately changing the answers, and makes sure the values print.

Flatten a reviewed document to make **comments, highlights and sticky notes** a permanent part of the page, so they show in every viewer and on paper.

Keep your original! A flattened PDF can’t be filled in again. To stop others copying or printing too, [protect the PDF](https://justtools.online/pdf-tools/protect-pdf/) after flattening; to hide personal details, use [Redact PDF](https://justtools.online/pdf-tools/redact-pdf/).

### FAQ

**What does it mean to flatten a PDF?**
Flattening merges interactive layers — form fields, comments, stamps and signatures — into the page itself. The PDF looks the same, but those parts can no longer be clicked, changed or deleted separately.

**Can a flattened PDF be unflattened?**
No. The fields are gone, so the form can’t be filled in again. Keep your original if you might need to change it.

**Will my digital signature still be valid?**
No. Flattening changes the file, so a cryptographic (certificate) signature will no longer verify, although it still appears on the page. Flatten before signing if the signature must stay valid.

**Is my form uploaded anywhere?**
No. Flattening runs in your browser with WebAssembly, and the file never leaves your device.

**Why does it say some things are still editable?**
A few comments, such as some sticky notes, don’t store how they look, so they can’t be merged into the page and are left as they were. Choose **Everything to images** to lock in everything you see.

**Can I flatten a PDF without form fields?**
Yes, with **Everything to images**. It turns each page into a picture, so the text can’t be selected, copied or edited.

## DNS Lookup

URL: https://justtools.online/developer-tools/dns-lookup/
Category: Developer Tools
Processing: Contacts an external service to work (see the page).
Last updated: 2026-09-30

Free DNS lookup: check A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, NS, TXT, SOA and CAA records of any domain, see SPF and DMARC, and do reverse DNS for an IP address.

### At a glance

- Looks up **A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, NS, TXT, SOA, CAA, SRV, PTR, HTTPS, DS and DNSKEY** records, or all the everyday ones at once.
- **All records** mode adds an overview: where the domain points, who hosts its DNS, which provider handles its email, and whether **SPF** and **DMARC** are set up.
- Enter an **IP address** to find its host name (reverse DNS / PTR).
- Shows whether answers are **DNSSEC-signed** and validated, and each record’s **TTL** in plain words.
- Recognises common TXT records — SPF, DMARC, DKIM and verification codes for Google, Microsoft 365, Meta and others.
- Queries go straight from your browser to the public DNS server you choose (Google, Cloudflare and five others) over encrypted DNS-over-HTTPS. Only the name you look up is sent.

### Features

- **Every record at once**: One click shows IPv4 and IPv6 addresses, mail servers, name servers, TXT, SOA, CAA and HTTPS records — no need to query each type.
- **Email health check**: See at a glance whether the domain has MX, SPF and DMARC records, and what its DMARC policy tells receivers to do.
- **Plain-English answers**: MX priorities, SOA timers, CAA rules and TXT verification codes are explained, and TTLs are shown as “1 hour”, not 3600.
- **Choose the DNS server**: Compare the answer from Google Public DNS, Cloudflare 1.1.1.1 and other resolvers — handy right after changing a record.
- **Reverse DNS**: Paste an IPv4 or IPv6 address to see the host name its owner registered for it.
- **Copy and share**: Copy any value with one click, copy all records in dig format, or share a link that runs the same lookup.

### How to look up DNS records

1. **Enter the domain** — Type a domain such as **example.com**, paste a link or an email address, or enter an IP address for reverse DNS.
2. **Pick a record type** — Leave **All records** selected for a full overview, or choose one type such as **MX** or **TXT**.
3. **Look it up** — Click **Look up**. Records appear grouped by type, with their TTL and a short explanation.
4. **Compare or copy** — Switch the **DNS server** to compare answers, copy records, or open the **propagation checker** to see the answer worldwide.

### Guide

#### DNS record types explained

| Type | What it does | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A | Points a name to an IPv4 address | 203.0.113.10 |
| AAAA | Points a name to an IPv6 address | 2001:db8::10 |
| CNAME | Makes a name an alias of another name | www → example.netlify.app |
| MX | Mail servers for the domain, with priority | 10 mail.example.com |
| NS | Name servers that hold the domain’s records | ada.ns.cloudflare.com |
| TXT | Text: SPF, DMARC, DKIM, verification codes | v=spf1 include:_spf.google.com ~all |
| SOA | Zone details: primary server, admin, serial, timers | ns1.example.com … |
| CAA | Which authorities may issue SSL certificates | 0 issue "letsencrypt.org" |
| PTR | Host name for an IP address (reverse DNS) | dns.google |

#### Checking your email setup

For email to arrive — and for your own mail not to land in spam — a domain needs **MX** records pointing to its mail provider, an **SPF** TXT record listing the servers allowed to send for it, and a **DMARC** record at `_dmarc.yourdomain` saying what to do with mail that fails the checks. Gmail and Yahoo require SPF and DMARC from bulk senders.

There must be **only one SPF record**: two SPF records make both invalid. Start DMARC with `p=none` to monitor, then move to `quarantine` or `reject` once all your sending services pass. DKIM keys live at `selector._domainkey.yourdomain`; look them up by typing that full name and choosing **TXT**.

### FAQ

**What is a DNS lookup?**
A DNS lookup asks the Domain Name System for the records of a name — for example the IP address of a website (A record) or the mail servers of a domain (MX). It’s what your browser does every time you visit a site.

**Why does the DNS server I choose give a different answer?**
Each DNS server caches answers for the record’s TTL. After a change, some servers still hold the old answer until their copy expires. Sites on a CDN may also give different answers by location. Use the DNS Propagation Checker to see many servers at once.

**What does TTL mean?**
Time to live: how long DNS servers may keep an answer before asking again. A TTL of 1 hour means a change can take up to an hour to reach everyone. Lower it a day before planned changes.

**How do I do a reverse DNS lookup?**
Enter an IP address, such as 8.8.8.8. The tool looks up its PTR record automatically and shows the host name, if the owner of the address has set one.

**Is this the same as nslookup or dig?**
It gives the same answers as `nslookup` or `dig` pointed at a public resolver, in your browser and with explanations. **Copy records** gives you dig-style output.

**What is sent, and to whom?**
Only the name you look up and the record type, sent from your browser over encrypted DNS-over-HTTPS to the DNS server you pick (Google Public DNS by default). JustTools doesn’t receive or store your lookups.

## DNS Propagation Checker

URL: https://justtools.online/developer-tools/dns-propagation-checker/
Category: Developer Tools
Processing: Contacts an external service to work (see the page).
Last updated: 2026-09-30

Check DNS propagation worldwide: see the A, CNAME, MX, NS or TXT answer from 7 public DNS networks and 18 ISPs in 15 countries, and track the change.

### At a glance

- Checks **A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, NS, TXT, CAA and SOA** records on **25 DNS servers and networks** at once.
- **7 public DNS networks** — Google, Cloudflare, DNS.SB, Control D, CleanBrowsing, IIJ (Japan) and dnsforge (Germany) — each with its own cache.
- **18 ISP networks in 15 countries**, including Jio, Airtel and ACT in India, answered by Google Public DNS as it would for their users (EDNS Client Subnet) — this shows where CDNs and GeoDNS send visitors.
- Enter the **expected value** to see the percentage of servers already showing it, and roughly how long the rest may keep the old answer (their remaining TTL).
- Identical answers are grouped and colour-coded, so you can spot the odd one out.
- Can re-check automatically every minute while you wait. Queries go from your browser over encrypted DNS-over-HTTPS; only the domain and record type are sent.

### Features

- **Know when it’s live**: Type the new IP, CNAME target or TXT value and watch the percentage climb to 100% as servers pick up the change.
- **When will it finish?**: Servers still showing the old value report how long they’ll keep it. The tool tells you the longest wait left.
- **Worldwide view**: Public DNS networks plus ISP networks across India, the Americas, Europe, the Middle East, Africa and Asia-Pacific.
- **CDN and GeoDNS aware**: See which server address visitors in each country get from services such as CloudFront, Akamai or Google.
- **Auto-refresh**: Switch on “Check again every minute” and leave the tab open — no need to keep clicking.
- **Shareable**: Copy a link with the domain, record type and expected value, and send it to your developer or hosting support.

### How to check DNS propagation

1. **Enter your domain** — Type the domain or subdomain you changed, such as **www.example.com**.
2. **Choose the record type** — Pick **A** for a new server IP, **CNAME** for an alias, **MX** for email, **NS** for new name servers or **TXT** for verification codes.
3. **Add the new value** — Optionally type the value you set, so each server is marked as updated or not.
4. **Check** — Click **Check**. Results fill in within seconds; switch on auto-refresh to follow the change.

### Guide

#### How long does DNS propagation take?

There is no single “propagation” process: every DNS server keeps a cached copy of your old record until its **TTL** (time to live) runs out, then fetches the new one. So a change is visible everywhere after at most the old record’s TTL — often 5 minutes to 1 hour, sometimes up to a day.

**New name servers (NS)** take longer: the registry for your domain’s ending (.com, .in…) publishes them, and resolvers may keep the old delegation for up to 48 hours. To make planned changes fast, lower the record’s TTL to 5 minutes a day before the change, then raise it again afterwards.

#### Reading the results

| You see | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| Updated (green tick) | The server returns the value you expect. |
| Different value (red) | The server still has the old answer cached — wait for its TTL to run out. |
| No record | The name exists but has no record of this type on that server (possibly cached). |
| Domain not found | The server believes the name doesn’t exist — common just after registering or adding a subdomain. |
| Different answers by country | Normal for sites on a CDN or GeoDNS: visitors are sent to their nearest server. |
| No answer | That server couldn’t be reached from your network (it may be blocked by a firewall or ad blocker). |

### FAQ

**Why do I still see the old website after the checker shows 100%?**
Your computer, router or browser can cache DNS too. Try another browser or a private window, restart the router, or switch your device to a public DNS such as 1.1.1.1 or 8.8.8.8. On Windows, `ipconfig /flushdns` clears the system cache.

**Can I speed up DNS propagation?**
You can’t force other servers to drop their cache, but you can plan ahead: lower the TTL well before a change. Google and Cloudflare also offer web pages to purge their cached copy of a name.

**Are these servers really in different countries?**
The public DNS networks are global: each answers from its site nearest to you, with its own cache. The country rows ask Google Public DNS to answer as it would for users of each ISP network, using EDNS Client Subnet — accurate for CDN and GeoDNS answers, but served from Google’s cache near you.

**Why do different countries get different IP addresses?**
Sites on a CDN (Cloudflare, CloudFront, Akamai, Fastly) or with GeoDNS deliberately give visitors the address of a nearby server. That’s expected and not a propagation problem.

**Why does it say “Domain not found” for a domain I just registered?**
New domains can take from minutes to a few hours to appear, and servers that asked before it existed remember the “not found” answer for the zone’s negative-cache time (shown as TTL).

**What is sent, and to whom?**
Only the domain and record type, sent from your browser over encrypted DNS-over-HTTPS to the DNS services listed on the page. JustTools doesn’t receive or store your checks.

## EXIF Metadata Remover

URL: https://justtools.online/image-tools/exif-metadata-remover/
Category: Image Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-09-30

Remove EXIF metadata from photos: GPS location, camera, date and hidden data in JPG, PNG, WebP and HEIC — with no quality loss and no upload. Free.

### At a glance

- Removes **EXIF, XMP, IPTC**, comments, embedded thumbnails and other metadata from **JPG, PNG, WebP, HEIC and AVIF** photos.
- **No quality loss:** the image data is copied byte for byte, not re-compressed, so the photo looks exactly the same — and usually gets smaller.
- Shows what each photo revealed first: **GPS location** (with a map link), camera and serial number, date and time, author and software.
- Also removes hidden extras stored after the image, such as the **video of a motion photo** or depth and HDR data.
- Keeps the **colour profile** and the **rotation** by default, so colours stay accurate and phone photos stay upright; either can be switched off.
- Every cleaned file is checked again, and the whole job runs in your browser — photos are never uploaded.

### Features

- **See what’s hidden**: Before cleaning, each photo shows what it gives away: the exact spot it was taken, the phone model, its serial number, the time and more.
- **Location removed**: Phones save GPS coordinates in every photo. Share pictures of your home, kids or car without revealing where you live.
- **Zero quality loss**: Unlike tools that re-save the image, only the metadata is cut out. The pixels are untouched.
- **iPhone HEIC too**: HEIC and AVIF photos are cleaned in place and stay HEIC — no conversion needed.
- **Batch cleaning**: Drop a whole folder of photos, then download them all as one ZIP.
- **Private by design**: Everything happens on your device. Nothing is uploaded, stored or seen by anyone else.

### How to remove EXIF data from a photo

1. **Add your photos** — Drop JPG, PNG, WebP or HEIC photos onto the box, click to choose them, or paste an image.
2. **Check what they reveal** — Each photo lists what it contained — tap **Details** to see the location, camera and dates.
3. **Choose what to keep** — Leave **Keep colour profile** and **Keep rotation** on for photos that look exactly as before.
4. **Download** — Click the download button for one photo, or **Download all (ZIP)**.

### Guide

#### What EXIF metadata can reveal

| Metadata | What it gives away |
| --- | --- |
| GPS position | The exact place a photo was taken — often your home, school or workplace |
| Date and time | When you were there, to the second, with your time zone |
| Camera and serial number | The device you own; a serial number can link photos to you |
| Author, owner, copyright | Your name, if the camera or an app added it |
| Software | The apps used to edit the photo |
| Embedded thumbnail | A small copy of the original — sometimes before cropping |
| Motion-photo video | A few seconds of video around the moment, with sound |

#### Do social networks remove it?

Most large social networks strip location data from photos they show publicly, but many other routes don’t: **sending a photo as a document or file** in WhatsApp or Telegram, email attachments, cloud-drive links, online marketplaces, forums and your own website usually keep every byte of metadata.

The safe habit is to clean photos before they leave your device. You can also switch off location tagging in your phone’s camera settings — but that doesn’t fix photos you’ve already taken.

### FAQ

**Does removing EXIF data reduce image quality?**
No. The tool cuts out the metadata blocks and copies the image data unchanged — it doesn’t decode and re-save the picture. The file usually gets a little smaller.

**Why keep the colour profile and rotation?**
The colour profile (ICC) makes colours display correctly, especially iPhone photos in Display P3; it contains no personal data. The rotation flag keeps phone photos upright. Everything else is removed. Turn both off for the strictest result.

**Can I remove metadata from iPhone HEIC photos?**
Yes. HEIC and AVIF files are cleaned in place: the EXIF and XMP data is erased and the file stays a HEIC, with the photo untouched. The file size stays the same.

**How do I know the location was really removed?**
Each cleaned file is scanned again automatically, and you’ll see a warning if anything identifying remains. You can also drop the cleaned photo back in — it will show “No metadata found”.

**Are my photos uploaded?**
No. Photos are read and cleaned by your browser on your own device. Nothing is sent to JustTools or anyone else.

**Which formats are supported?**
JPG/JPEG, PNG, WebP, HEIC/HEIF and AVIF. GIF, TIFF and RAW files aren’t supported.

## Image Blur Tool

URL: https://justtools.online/image-tools/image-blur/
Category: Image Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-09-30

Blur faces, number plates, text or the background in any photo. Blur, pixelate or black out areas, then download it full size — free, private, no upload.

### At a glance

- Blurs **marked areas**, **everything except the marked areas** (background blur), or the **whole photo**.
- Three effects: smooth **Gaussian blur**, **pixelate** (mosaic) and a solid **black box** — with adjustable strength.
- Mark areas as **rectangles or ovals**; drag to move them, drag a corner to resize, and press Delete to remove one.
- The live preview matches the final image; the download is **full resolution** in the original format (JPG, PNG or WebP; HEIC becomes JPG).
- Location and camera data (EXIF) are not copied to the blurred image.
- Runs entirely in your browser — the photo is never uploaded.

### Features

- **Hide faces and plates**: Blur children’s faces, bystanders, car number plates and house numbers before posting photos online.
- **Censor screenshots**: Cover names, phone numbers, UPI IDs, OTPs and account details in chat or payment screenshots.
- **Background blur**: Mark the subject and choose “Everything else” for a portrait-style blurred background.
- **Blur, pixelate or black box**: Pick the look you want. For text that must stay secret, the black box can never be reversed.
- **Before and after**: Press and hold “Hold to see original” to compare with the untouched photo at any time.
- **Private and free**: No upload, no watermark, no sign-up, and full-size downloads.

### How to blur part of an image

1. **Open your photo** — Drop a JPG, PNG, WebP or HEIC photo onto the box, or paste a screenshot with Ctrl+V.
2. **Mark what to hide** — Drag over each face, plate or piece of text. Use **Oval** for faces. Move or resize areas by dragging.
3. **Choose the effect** — Pick **Blur**, **Pixelate** or **Black box** and set the strength. Choose **Everything else** to blur the background instead.
4. **Download** — Click **Download** to save the full-size blurred photo.

### Guide

#### Which effect should I use?

| Effect | Looks like | Best for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Blur | Soft and natural | Faces, backgrounds, bystanders |
| Pixelate | Mosaic squares | Number plates, logos, a TV-style censor look |
| Black box | Solid black shape | Text and numbers that must stay secret — OTPs, account and ID numbers |

#### Is blurred text really unreadable?

Not always. Light blur or small pixel blocks can leave enough of the shapes of letters and digits for software to guess them, especially for short numbers. For anything sensitive — Aadhaar, PAN, card or account numbers, passwords, OTPs — use **Black box**, or a strength of 60 or more so no detail remains.

For documents, a black box in [Redact PDF](https://justtools.online/pdf-tools/redact-pdf/) removes the text itself rather than only covering it.

### FAQ

**How do I blur a face in a photo?**
Open the photo, choose **Oval** as the area shape and drag over the face. Set the effect to **Blur** with a strength of 50 or more, then download.

**How do I blur the background of a photo?**
Mark the person or object you want to keep sharp, then choose **Everything else**. Everything outside the marked areas is blurred.

**Will the downloaded image be lower quality?**
The size stays exactly the same. JPG and WebP photos are saved at high quality (92); PNG stays lossless.

**Can someone un-blur my image?**
A strong blur or pixelation can’t be undone to reveal faces, but weakly blurred text can sometimes be guessed. Use Black box for secret text and numbers.

**Does it work on phones?**
Yes. Drag with your finger to mark areas. To scroll past the photo, switch the toggle above it to **Scroll page**.

**Is my photo uploaded?**
No. The photo is processed in your browser on your own device and never leaves it.

## Image Steganography Tool

URL: https://justtools.online/security-tools/image-steganography/
Category: Security Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-09-30

Hide a secret message or file inside an image, protected with a password, and reveal hidden messages from PNG images. Free and private — no upload.

### At a glance

- Hides a **message or a small file** in the lowest bit of the colour values of an image’s pixels — a change of at most 1 in 255 that the eye can’t see.
- With a password, the message is encrypted with **AES-256-GCM** (key from PBKDF2-SHA-256, 600,000 rounds) before it’s hidden, so it can’t be read or altered without the password.
- Any photo works as the cover (JPG, PNG, WebP, HEIC); the result is saved as a **PNG**, because lossy formats would destroy the hidden bits.
- Shows how much the image can hold — a 1,000 × 1,000 image holds about 370 KB — and checks the saved file reads back correctly.
- Messages are compressed first, so long text takes less room. Hindi, emoji and any language work.
- Runs entirely in your browser: images, messages and passwords are never uploaded.

### Features

- **Invisible**: The picture looks exactly the same. Only the tiniest bit of each colour value changes.
- **Password protected**: AES-256 encryption means that even someone who knows there’s a message can’t read it without the password.
- **Text or files**: Hide a note, a list of passwords, a key, or a small PDF or ZIP inside a photo.
- **Verified**: After saving, the tool reads the message back from the file to make sure it will work for the recipient.
- **Reveal in one step**: Drop the PNG in Reveal mode and enter the password — the message or file appears.
- **Private**: No server ever sees your image, message or password.

### How to hide a message in an image

1. **Choose a cover image** — In **Hide a message**, drop any photo. Larger images can hold more.
2. **Write the message** — Type your text, or switch to **A small file** and choose one.
3. **Add a password** — Recommended: without it, anyone using this tool can read the message.
4. **Download and send** — Click **Hide and download PNG**, then send the PNG as a file or document — not as a photo.

### Guide

#### Sending the image without losing the message

| How you send it | Hidden message |
| --- | --- |
| Email attachment, Google Drive, Dropbox, USB | Kept |
| WhatsApp or Telegram “Document” / “File” | Kept |
| WhatsApp, Instagram or Facebook as a photo | Destroyed (the image is re-compressed) |
| Screenshot of the image | Destroyed |
| Converting to JPG or resizing | Destroyed |

#### How it works

Each pixel has red, green and blue values from 0 to 255. The tool writes the message, bit by bit, into the lowest bit of those values — changing a colour from, say, 200 to 201. That is far below what the eye can notice, so the image looks untouched. A short header marks where the message starts and how long it is.

Steganography hides **that** a message exists; encryption protects **what** it says. With a password, you get both. Note that specialised analysis software can often detect that an image contains hidden data, even if it can’t read it — so always use a password for anything sensitive.

### FAQ

**Can anyone see that the image has a hidden message?**
Not by looking at it. Forensic tools can sometimes detect that the pixels were altered, which is why a password matters: detected or not, the message can’t be read without it.

**Why is the output a PNG?**
PNG is lossless, so every bit is saved exactly. JPG and WebP photos are compressed in a way that changes pixel values slightly — enough to wipe out a hidden message.

**How much can I hide?**
About 3 bits per pixel: roughly 370 KB in a 1,000 × 1,000 image, or 1.1 MB in a photo reduced to 2,000 × 1,500. Text is compressed first, so a page of text needs only a few kilobytes.

**I forgot the password. Can the message be recovered?**
No. The encryption has no back door, and JustTools never sees your password, so it can’t be reset.

**Can it read messages hidden with other steganography tools?**
No. Each tool uses its own format. Reveal mode reads messages hidden with this tool.

**Is steganography legal?**
Yes, hiding your own messages in your own images is legal in India and most countries. Using it to commit a crime is not.

## Image Watermark

URL: https://justtools.online/image-tools/image-watermark/
Category: Image Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-09-30

Watermark photos with your name, © text or logo in one go: choose position, size, angle and opacity, or repeat it across the image. Free, no upload.

### At a glance

- Adds a **text** watermark (any language, including Hindi, and emoji) or your **logo** (PNG with transparency, JPG, WebP or SVG) to photos.
- Place it **once** in any of nine positions, or **repeat it across the photo** at any angle — hardest to crop or remove.
- Size is relative to each photo, so a batch of large and small images gets a matching watermark.
- An optional **outline** keeps white or dark text readable on busy backgrounds.
- Watermark **many photos at once** and download them as a ZIP, in their original format (JPG, PNG or WebP; HEIC becomes JPG) at full size.
- Runs in your browser — photos and logos are never uploaded. Camera data (EXIF, GPS) is not copied to the watermarked files.

### Features

- **Live preview**: Every change shows immediately on your photo. Click any photo in the list to preview it.
- **Your logo**: Upload a transparent PNG or SVG logo and set its width as a share of the photo.
- **Hard to remove**: A repeated, rotated watermark across the whole image can’t simply be cropped out.
- **Batch processing**: Drop a folder of photos, set the watermark once, and download them all.
- **Full quality**: Photos keep their size and are saved at high quality — no resizing, no compression surprises.
- **Private**: Unlike most watermark sites, nothing is uploaded to a server.

### How to add a watermark to photos

1. **Add photos** — Drop one or more photos onto the box, or click to choose them.
2. **Write or upload the watermark** — Type your text — try the **© Your Name** preset — or switch to **Logo / image** and choose your logo.
3. **Style and place it** — Set the size, colour, opacity and rotation, and choose a corner or **Repeat across photo**.
4. **Download** — Download photos one by one, or all at once with **Download all (ZIP)**.

### Guide

#### Good watermark settings

| Use | Watermark | Layout | Opacity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Photography portfolio | © Your Name, white with outline | Once, bottom-right, 4–6% | 60–80% |
| Products for online selling | Shop logo | Once, centre or corner | 30–60% |
| Proofs sent to clients | PROOF or SAMPLE | Repeat across photo, 30–45° | 20–35% |
| ID copies for KYC | For KYC only · date | Repeat across photo | 25–35% |

#### Protecting photos you post online

A small corner watermark tells people who took the photo and is easy to live with — but it can be cropped out. If your images are being copied, use a larger, semi-transparent watermark across the subject, or repeat it across the whole photo.

For documents such as Aadhaar or PAN copies, add the purpose and date (“For KYC only · 30 Sep 2026”) across the image so a copy can’t be reused elsewhere. For PDFs, use [PDF Watermark](https://justtools.online/pdf-tools/pdf-watermark/).

### FAQ

**Can I watermark many photos at once?**
Yes. Add as many photos as you like; the same watermark is applied to all of them, scaled to each photo’s size, and you can download them together as a ZIP.

**Will my photos lose quality?**
They keep their full size. JPG and WebP photos are saved at high quality (92), and PNG stays lossless.

**Can I use my logo as a watermark?**
Yes. Choose Logo / image and upload a PNG with a transparent background (or JPG, WebP or SVG). Set its width and opacity.

**Can a watermark be removed?**
A small corner mark can be cropped or edited out. A large, rotated watermark repeated across the photo is much harder to remove without ruining the image.

**Are my photos uploaded?**
No. Photos and your logo are processed in your browser on your own device.

**Can I write the watermark in Hindi?**
Yes. The text is drawn by your browser, so Hindi, other Indian languages and emoji all work.

## JSON to CSV Converter

URL: https://justtools.online/developer-tools/json-to-csv/
Category: Developer Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-09-30

Convert JSON to CSV for Excel or Google Sheets: nested objects become columns, lists are kept and big numbers stay exact. Also CSV to JSON. No upload.

### At a glance

- Converts a JSON **array of objects** into CSV rows, with every key as a column — even keys that only some objects have.
- Finds the rows inside API responses like `{"data": {"users": [...]}}` automatically, and reads **JSON Lines** (NDJSON).
- **Nested objects** become `parent.child` columns; lists of values are joined in one cell (or written as JSON).
- Numbers are copied digit for digit, so long IDs like 12345678901234567890 and prices like 1.10 aren’t rounded.
- Comma, semicolon, tab or pipe delimiters, RFC 4180 quoting, and an optional UTF-8 BOM so **Excel** shows Hindi, ₹ and accents correctly.
- Also converts **CSV to JSON**, detecting the delimiter, turning numbers and true/false into JSON types (leading zeros stay text) and `a.b` columns back into nested objects.
- Runs in your browser — your data is never uploaded.

### Features

- **Table preview**: See the result as a spreadsheet-style table before downloading, or switch to the raw CSV text.
- **Handles messy JSON**: Objects with different keys, nested objects, lists and wrapper objects are all turned into a proper rectangular table.
- **Excel and Sheets ready**: The download opens correctly in Excel, Google Sheets and Numbers, including Indian languages and the ₹ sign.
- **Formula-safe option**: Optionally stop cells that start with =, +, - or @ from running as spreadsheet formulas (CSV injection).
- **Both directions**: Switch to CSV → JSON to turn a spreadsheet export back into clean, nested JSON for an API or config.
- **Exact error messages**: Invalid JSON is reported with the line and column of the mistake.

### How to convert JSON to CSV

1. **Add your JSON** — Paste JSON into the left box, click **Open file**, or try the **Sample**.
2. **Check the table** — The CSV appears as a table straight away. Nested objects become columns like **address.city**.
3. **Adjust the options** — Pick the **delimiter**, and open **Options** to flatten, join lists or make the file Excel-ready.
4. **Download** — Click **Download** for a .csv file, or **Copy** to paste into a spreadsheet.

### Guide

#### How JSON becomes a table

| JSON | CSV |
| --- | --- |
| [{"name": "Asha", "age": 31}] | Columns name, age — one row per object |
| {"address": {"city": "Pune"}} | Column address.city |
| {"skills": ["SQL", "Excel"]} | One cell: SQL; Excel (or ["SQL","Excel"]) |
| {"data": [ … ]} | Rows are taken from the data array |
| null | Empty cell |
| "Mehta, Jr." | "Mehta, Jr." — quoted because of the comma |

#### Opening CSV files in Excel

Keep **Excel-ready (UTF-8 BOM)** switched on: without it, Excel on Windows may show Hindi text or the ₹ sign as garbled characters. If your Excel uses a comma as the decimal separator (common in Europe), choose the **semicolon** delimiter.

Excel drops leading zeros from numbers like phone numbers and PIN codes when it opens a CSV. The data in the file is correct — to keep the zeros, import it with **Data → From Text/CSV** and set that column to Text.

### FAQ

**Can it convert nested JSON to CSV?**
Yes. Nested objects become columns named with dots, such as address.city. Lists of simple values are joined into one cell, and lists of objects are written as JSON text in the cell.

**What if my objects have different keys?**
Every key found in any object becomes a column, in the order first seen. Objects without a key get an empty cell there.

**Is my data uploaded anywhere?**
No. The conversion runs entirely in your browser, so API responses, customer lists and exports never leave your device.

**How large a file can it handle?**
Files of several megabytes convert in a second or two. Very large files are limited only by your device’s memory; the table preview shows the first 200 rows.

**Why do my Hindi or ₹ characters look wrong in Excel?**
Excel needs a byte order mark to detect UTF-8. Keep “Excel-ready (UTF-8 BOM)” switched on in Options and download again.

**Can I convert CSV back to JSON?**
Yes — choose CSV → JSON. The delimiter is detected automatically, numbers and true/false become JSON values, and columns like address.city become nested objects.

## Passport Size Photo Maker

URL: https://justtools.online/image-tools/passport-photo-maker/
Category: Image Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-09-30

Make passport size photos online: India passport, PAN card, visa, US, UK and more. Face guide, print sheets for 4×6 or A4, and KB limits for forms.

### At a glance

- Sizes for **India passport (35 × 45 mm)**, **India visa / OCI (2 × 2 in)**, **PAN card (25 × 35 mm)**, **stamp size (20 × 25 mm)**, and passports or visas for the **USA, UK, Schengen, Canada, Australia and China**.
- A **head guide** shows where the top of the hair and the chin should be for each document; on supported browsers the face is found and placed automatically.
- Download a single photo at **300 DPI**, a **print sheet** for 4 × 6 in photo paper, 5 × 7 in, A4 or Letter (as PDF or JPG, with cut lines), or a file **under a KB limit** for online forms.
- The print sheet fits the most photos — for example **8 passport photos on a 4 × 6 in** print, or 6 of 2 × 2 in.
- Straighten, zoom, and adjust brightness and contrast; empty edges are filled with white, light grey or light blue.
- Works in your browser — your photo is never uploaded.

### Features

- **Right size, every time**: Choose the document and the frame, head size and output pixels are set for you.
- **Print at home or a shop**: Print a 4 × 6 in sheet at any photo studio or kiosk for far less than a new passport photo session, or use the A4 PDF at home.
- **For exam forms**: Set the size limit — 20, 50 or 100 KB — and the width in pixels for SSC, UPSC, IBPS, university and job applications.
- **Face guide**: An oval, a chin line and a band for the top of the head make it easy to meet the rules.
- **Exact print size**: The PDF sheet is made at the paper’s real size, so each photo prints at exactly 35 × 45 mm (or your size) at 100%.
- **Private**: Your face photo stays on your device — nothing is uploaded or stored.

### How to make a passport size photo

1. **Choose the photo size** — Pick the document, such as **India passport** or **PAN card**.
2. **Add your photo** — Use a photo taken facing the camera, in front of a plain light wall, in good light.
3. **Line up your face** — Drag and zoom so the head fits the oval: top of the hair in the shaded band, chin on the line.
4. **Download** — Choose **Photo**, **Print sheet** (PDF or JPG) or **Online form** with a KB limit, and download.

### Guide

#### Common photo sizes

| Document | Size | Head (chin to top of hair) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| India passport | 35 × 45 mm (3.5 × 4.5 cm) | about 31–36 mm (most of the height) |
| India visa / OCI | 2 × 2 in (51 × 51 mm) | 25–35 mm |
| PAN card | 25 × 35 mm (2.5 × 3.5 cm) | most of the height |
| Stamp size | 20 × 25 mm | most of the height |
| USA passport / visa | 2 × 2 in (51 × 51 mm) | 25–35 mm (1–1⅜ in) |
| UK passport | 35 × 45 mm | 29–34 mm |
| Schengen visa | 35 × 45 mm | 32–36 mm |
| Canada passport | 50 × 70 mm | 31–36 mm |

#### Tips for an accepted photo

Stand about a metre in front of a **plain white or very light wall**, facing a window or soft light so there are no shadows on your face or behind you. Look straight at the camera with a neutral expression and your mouth closed, eyes open and clearly visible. Avoid glasses and caps; religious headwear is usually allowed if the whole face is visible.

Ask someone else to take the photo from about 1.5 metres away at eye level — selfies distort the face. Use a recent photo (taken within the last six months), and always check the latest rules of the office you are applying to.

### FAQ

**What is the passport photo size in India?**
35 × 45 mm (3.5 cm wide, 4.5 cm tall) with a plain white background, the face covering most of the photo, taken from the front. Choose “India passport” and the tool sets this for you.

**What is the PAN card photo size?**
25 × 35 mm (2.5 × 3.5 cm), in colour with a white background. Choose “PAN card”, then download a single photo or a print sheet.

**How do I reduce a photo to 20 KB or 50 KB for an online form?**
Choose Online form, set the maximum size (such as 50 KB) and the width in pixels your form asks for, and download. The tool picks the highest quality that fits the limit.

**How many passport photos fit on a 4 × 6 photo print?**
Eight 35 × 45 mm photos fit on a 4 × 6 in (10 × 15 cm) print, with small gaps to cut along. Six 2 × 2 in photos fit on the same print.

**Can it change the background to white?**
Not automatically. Take the photo against a plain white or light wall; any empty edges around the photo are filled with white, light grey or light blue.

**Is my photo uploaded?**
No. Everything is done in your browser, so your photo never leaves your device.

## Password Strength Checker

URL: https://justtools.online/security-tools/password-strength-checker/
Category: Security Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-09-30

Check how strong a password is: time to crack, common words and patterns it hides, tips to improve it, and a safe data-breach check. Fully private.

### At a glance

- Uses **zxcvbn**, the password-strength estimator developed at Dropbox, which models how real attackers guess instead of just counting symbols.
- Recognises **tens of thousands of common passwords**, English words, first names and surnames, plus common **Indian names and words** such as Rahul, Priya, Sairam or Jaishreeram.
- Spots **keyboard patterns** (qwerty), **sequences** (1234, abcd), repeats, **dates and years**, and look-alike swaps like P@ssw0rd.
- Shows the time to crack in four realistic situations, from a rate-limited login page to a stolen database cracked on GPUs.
- The optional **data-breach check** uses Have I Been Pwned’s k-anonymity API: only the first 5 characters of the password’s SHA-1 hash are sent, never the password.
- Everything else runs in your browser; the password is never stored or sent anywhere.

### Features

- **Realistic, not naive**: “P@ssw0rd123” ticks every box on most sites — here it’s rated weak, because attackers try exactly those swaps first.
- **Time to crack**: From a login page that blocks repeated tries to a leaked database attacked with graphics cards.
- **What gives it away**: See each part an attacker would recognise: a common password, a name, a year, a keyboard walk.
- **Has it leaked?**: Compare against hundreds of millions of passwords exposed in data breaches, without revealing yours.
- **Clear advice**: Specific tips to make it stronger — and a link to generate a truly random one.
- **Private**: Nothing you type is saved or sent. Works offline once loaded (except the optional breach check).

### How to check password strength

1. **Type the password** — Type or paste it into the box. Use the eye button to show or hide it.
2. **Read the rating** — The meter shows **Very weak** to **Very strong**, with the estimated number of guesses needed.
3. **See why** — Check the time to crack, the checklist and **What an attacker would notice**.
4. **Check for leaks** — Click **Check now** to see if it has appeared in a data breach. If it has, stop using it.

### Guide

#### What makes a password strong

**Length and randomness beat complexity.** A random 4–5 word passphrase like “tiger-lamp-orbit-seven” is far stronger than “Rahul@1990”, and easier to remember. Names, birthdays, cricket players, cities and keyboard patterns are the first things cracking tools try — with or without @ for a and 0 for o.

Just as important: **never reuse a password.** When one site leaks, attackers try the same email and password everywhere else. Use a password manager to store a different random password for every account, and turn on two-factor authentication for email, banking and UPI apps.

#### Time to crack, explained

| Situation | Guesses per second | Needs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Login page with rate limiting | 100 per hour | Any password that isn’t very common |
| Login page without limits | 10 | At least a fair password |
| Leaked database, bcrypt or similar | 10,000 | A strong password |
| Leaked database, MD5 or similar, GPUs | 10 billion | A very strong, random password |

### FAQ

**Is it safe to type my password here?**
Yes. The strength check runs entirely in your browser, and the password is never stored or sent. If you prefer, test a password that follows the same pattern as yours instead of the real one.

**How does the data-breach check work without sending my password?**
Your browser computes the SHA-1 hash of the password and sends only its first five characters to Have I Been Pwned. The service returns every leaked hash starting with those characters (with random padding), and the match is found on your device. The password and its full hash never leave it.

**Why is my password with symbols rated weak?**
Because the rest of it is predictable. Attackers’ tools try common words with capitals, numbers, years and symbol swaps first, so “Password@123” falls in seconds. Randomness and length matter far more than symbols.

**How long should a password be?**
At least 12 characters for everyday accounts, and 15 or more — or a passphrase of four to five random words — for email, banking and your password manager.

**What does “Found in data breaches” mean?**
The exact password appears in lists of passwords leaked from hacked websites. Attackers try these lists first, so don’t use it anywhere, even if it looks strong.

**How is this different from the strength bar on websites?**
Most sites only check length and character types. This tool estimates the number of guesses a real attacker would need, recognising common passwords, names, dates and patterns.

## CSV to JSON Converter

URL: https://justtools.online/developer-tools/csv-to-json/
Category: Developer Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-09-30

Convert CSV or data pasted from Excel to JSON: auto-detected delimiter, real numbers and true/false, nested objects from dotted columns. Free, no upload.

### At a glance

- Turns each CSV row into a JSON object, using the **first row as keys** (or column1, column2… when there’s no header).
- Detects the delimiter automatically — **comma, semicolon, tab or pipe** — so cells copied from **Excel or Google Sheets** can be pasted directly.
- Converts **numbers, true/false and empty cells** into proper JSON values, while phone numbers, PIN codes with leading zeros and long IDs stay text.
- Columns named like **address.city** become nested objects.
- Four output shapes: **array of objects**, **array of arrays**, an object **keyed by the first column**, or **JSON Lines** — with 2 or 4 spaces, tabs or minified.
- Follows RFC 4180: quoted fields, commas and line breaks inside quotes, and doubled quotes all work. Runs in your browser; data is never uploaded.

### Features

- **Straight from Excel**: Select cells in Excel or Google Sheets, copy, and paste here — tab-separated data is recognised automatically.
- **Proper JSON types**: Numbers become numbers and true/false become booleans — without breaking IDs like 007 or 16-digit card numbers.
- **Nested objects**: user.name and user.email columns become {"user": {"name": …, "email": …}}.
- **The shape you need**: Objects for APIs, arrays for charts, keyed objects for lookups, or JSON Lines for big-data tools.
- **Handles messy files**: Missing header names, duplicate columns and rows with extra or missing fields are handled and reported.
- **Private**: Customer lists and exports stay on your device — nothing is uploaded.

### How to convert CSV to JSON

1. **Add your CSV** — Paste CSV, paste cells copied from Excel or Google Sheets, or click **Open file** to load a .csv file.
2. **Check the options** — Open **Options** to choose the output shape, indentation, and whether to convert numbers and nest dotted columns.
3. **Review the JSON** — The JSON appears as you type, with a count of rows and columns and notes about any irregular rows.
4. **Copy or download** — Click **Copy**, or **Download** a .json (or .jsonl) file.

### Guide

#### Output shapes

| Shape | Looks like | Good for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Objects | [{"id": 1, "name": "Asha"}, …] | APIs, JavaScript, most uses |
| Arrays | [["id", "name"], [1, "Asha"], …] | Charts, compact data, keeping column order |
| Keyed | {"1": {"id": 1, "name": "Asha"}, …} | Looking rows up by ID |
| JSON Lines | {"id": 1, …} on each line | Streaming, logs, BigQuery and data pipelines |

#### How values are converted

With **Convert numbers & booleans** on, 42 and 3.14 become numbers, true and false become booleans, and empty cells become null. Values that only look like numbers stay text: anything with a leading zero (phone numbers, PIN codes like 012345, employee IDs like 007) and anything longer than 15 digits (card and account numbers), because JSON numbers would lose those digits.

Switch the option off to keep every value as text exactly as it appears in the CSV.

### FAQ

**Can I convert an Excel file to JSON?**
Yes. Open the sheet, select the cells (including the header row), copy, and paste them here. To use a file instead, save it from Excel as CSV UTF-8 and open that.

**Why are some numbers kept as text?**
Numbers with leading zeros or more than 15 digits would change if stored as JSON numbers, so they stay text. Turn off “Convert numbers & booleans” to keep everything as text.

**What if my CSV uses semicolons?**
The delimiter is detected automatically — commas, semicolons (common in Europe), tabs and pipes all work. You can also pick one yourself.

**Is my data uploaded?**
No. The conversion runs entirely in your browser; your file never leaves your device.

**How do I get nested JSON?**
Name the columns with dots, like address.city and address.pin, and keep “Nest dotted columns” on. They become {"address": {"city": …, "pin": …}}.

**Can I convert JSON back to CSV?**
Yes — switch to JSON → CSV, or use the JSON to CSV Converter, which also shows the result as a table.

## UUID Generator

URL: https://justtools.online/developer-tools/uuid-generator/
Category: Developer Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-09-30

Generate UUIDs (GUIDs) online: random v4, sortable v7, v1, and name-based v5 and v3 — one or 10,000 at a time. Also decode and validate any UUID.

### At a glance

- Generates **version 4** (random), **version 7** (Unix time, sortable), **version 1** (time-based), **version 5** (SHA-1) and **version 3** (MD5) UUIDs, plus the nil and max UUIDs — all following **RFC 9562**.
- Random bits come from your browser’s **cryptographically secure** generator (Web Crypto).
- Version 7 UUIDs generated together stay **in order** even within the same millisecond, which keeps database indexes fast.
- Version 1 UUIDs use a random node ID, so they **never reveal your device’s MAC address**.
- Generate up to **10,000** at once, uppercase or lowercase, with or without hyphens, in {braces}, "quotes" or as urn:uuid:, one per line or comma-separated.
- The decoder shows any UUID’s version, variant and — for v1, v6 and v7 — the date and time it was created.

### Features

- **The right version**: v4 for general IDs, v7 for database keys, v5 for repeatable IDs from names — each explained in one line.
- **Bulk generation**: Make 10, 100 or 10,000 UUIDs and copy them all or download a .txt file.
- **Any format**: Match your code or database: uppercase for .NET GUIDs, no hyphens for compact keys, quotes and commas for SQL.
- **Name-based UUIDs**: Turn domain names, URLs or any text into stable v5 or v3 UUIDs — one per line.
- **Decode & validate**: Paste a UUID — or a log line containing several — to check it and see when it was created.
- **Private and offline**: UUIDs are made on your device. Nothing is sent to a server or logged.

### How to generate a UUID

1. **Pick a version** — Keep **v4** for a random UUID, or choose **v7** for time-ordered IDs.
2. **Choose how many** — Enter a number or pick **10**, **100** or **1,000**.
3. **Set the format** — Turn on **Uppercase**, remove **Hyphens**, or wrap each UUID in braces, quotes or urn:uuid:.
4. **Copy** — Click **Copy** (or **Copy all**), or download the list as a text file.

### Guide

#### Which UUID version should I use?

| Version | Made from | Use it for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| v4 | 122 random bits | General-purpose unique IDs — the default choice |
| v7 | Unix time in ms + random bits | Database primary keys and anything you sort by creation time |
| v1 | Time + clock sequence + node | Older systems that expect time-based UUIDs |
| v5 | SHA-1 of a namespace and a name | The same ID every time for the same input |
| v3 | MD5 of a namespace and a name | Compatibility with systems that already use v3 |

#### Are UUIDs really unique?

A version 4 UUID has 122 random bits: about 5.3 × 10³⁶ possible values. You would need to generate a billion UUIDs every second for about 86 years before the chance of a single duplicate reached 50%. In practice, UUIDs from a good random source never collide.

UUIDs aren’t secrets, though: don’t use them as passwords or security tokens. And while v7 UUIDs are great database keys, they reveal the time they were created.

### FAQ

**What is the difference between a UUID and a GUID?**
None in practice. GUID (globally unique identifier) is Microsoft’s name for a UUID. Windows and .NET often show GUIDs in uppercase and in braces — switch on Uppercase and choose { } to match.

**Is UUID v7 better than v4?**
For database keys, usually yes: v7 UUIDs increase over time, so new rows go at the end of the index instead of random places, which keeps inserts fast. Use v4 when the creation time shouldn’t be visible.

**Are these UUIDs safe to use in production?**
Yes. They follow RFC 9562 and use your browser’s cryptographically secure random number generator — the same quality as crypto.randomUUID() or uuid libraries.

**How do I check whether a string is a valid UUID?**
Open Decode & validate and paste it. The tool accepts common formats — with or without hyphens, braces or urn:uuid: — and shows the version, variant and, for time-based versions, when it was created.

**Why does v5 give the same UUID every time?**
That’s the point of name-based UUIDs: the same namespace and name always produce the same UUID, so different systems can derive matching IDs without talking to each other.

**Can a UUID be decoded to get the time?**
For versions 1, 6 and 7, yes — the creation time is stored inside. Version 4 is purely random, and v3 and v5 are hashes, so they contain no time.

## UTM Builder

URL: https://justtools.online/seo-tools/utm-builder/
Category: SEO & Marketing Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-09-30

Build UTM campaign links for Google Analytics 4: presets for WhatsApp, Instagram, email and ads, the GA4 channel each lands in, and a QR code for it.

### At a glance

- Adds **utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign**, and optionally **utm_id, utm_term** and **utm_content** to any page URL — keeping its other parameters and #fragment.
- One-click presets for **WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook, YouTube, LinkedIn, X, Google Ads, Meta ads, email, SMS, push notifications and QR codes**.
- Shows which **GA4 default channel** the link will most likely count as — Organic Social, Paid Search, Email and so on — using Google’s published rules.
- Keeps values **consistent**: lowercase and underscores by default, because GA4 treats “Facebook” and “facebook” as different sources.
- Warns about missing values, capital letters and short links, and reads the UTM tags back out of any link you paste.
- Builds a separate link for **several channels at once** (copy all or download CSV), and hands any link to the QR Code Generator for posters and packaging.

### Features

- **Know what works**: See in Google Analytics whether WhatsApp, Instagram or your newsletter brought the visits and sales.
- **GA4 channel preview**: Avoid “Unassigned” traffic: the tool shows the channel group before you share the link.
- **Consistent naming**: Automatic lowercase and space handling keep your reports clean, campaign after campaign.
- **Many channels, one click**: Tick the places you’ll post — get a separate tagged link for each, ready to copy or save as CSV.
- **QR codes for print**: Send the tagged link straight to the QR Code Generator to track posters, flyers and packaging.
- **Private**: Links are built in your browser. Nothing is sent to a server or shortened through a third party.

### How to build a UTM link

1. **Paste the page URL** — Enter the address of the page the link should open, such as your sale page.
2. **Pick a preset** — Click **WhatsApp**, **Instagram post**, **Google Ads** or another preset to fill in source and medium.
3. **Name the campaign** — Enter a campaign name like **diwali_sale_2026**, and optionally content such as **story_1**.
4. **Copy and share** — Copy the link, open it to test, or make a QR code. Check the GA4 channel shown below it.

### Guide

#### UTM parameters explained

| Parameter | Answers | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| utm_source | Where did the visit come from? | whatsapp, instagram, google, newsletter |
| utm_medium | What kind of channel? | social, cpc, email, sms, referral |
| utm_campaign | Which campaign or promotion? | diwali_sale_2026 |
| utm_content | Which link, ad or post exactly? | story_2, banner_top, button_red |
| utm_term | Which paid keyword? | running_shoes |
| utm_id | Which campaign ID (for cost import)? | fb_2026_q4 |

#### Tips for clean campaign data

**Stick to one naming style.** Decide on lowercase with underscores and use it everywhere — “Instagram”, “instagram” and “IG” become three separate sources in GA4. Use the medium names GA4 recognises (social, cpc, email, sms, referral, affiliate, display) so visits land in the right channel instead of “Unassigned”.

**Never tag internal links.** Links from one page of your site to another should not have UTM tags: clicking one starts a new session and overwrites where the visitor really came from. Google Ads links are tagged automatically (gclid) when auto-tagging is on, so they don’t need manual UTMs.

### FAQ

**What is a UTM link?**
A normal link with extra parameters, such as ?utm_source=whatsapp&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=diwali_sale, that tell Google Analytics where a visitor came from. The page itself works exactly the same.

**Which UTM parameters are required?**
utm_source is the essential one — Google Analytics ignores the others without it. Always add utm_medium and utm_campaign too, so the visit is grouped into a channel and campaign.

**What UTM should I use for WhatsApp?**
utm_source=whatsapp and utm_medium=social, which GA4 groups as Organic Social. Add utm_content to tell apart a status update, a broadcast list and a group message.

**Why does my traffic show as “Unassigned” in GA4?**
The source and medium didn’t match any of GA4’s default channel rules — for example a made-up medium like “post” or “story”. Use standard mediums such as social, email or cpc. The tool shows the channel before you share.

**Are UTM parameters case-sensitive?**
Yes. GA4 treats Facebook and facebook as two different sources, so keep “Lowercase” switched on.

**Do UTM tags affect SEO?**
Not when used on links in campaigns, ads, emails and social posts. Don’t use them on your own internal links, and make sure pages have a canonical URL so tagged links aren’t indexed separately.

## URL Encoder / Decoder

URL: https://justtools.online/developer-tools/url-encoder-decoder/
Category: Developer Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-09-30

Encode or decode URLs and query strings online: %20, + and UTF-8 (Hindi, emoji) done right, errors pinpointed, and URL parameters shown in a table.

### At a glance

- Three encodings for three jobs: **parameter value** (encodeURIComponent), **whole URL** (encodeURI) and **form data** (application/x-www-form-urlencoded, spaces as +).
- Encodes text as **UTF-8**, so Hindi, other Indian scripts, ₹ and emoji become the %E0%A4… sequences every browser and server understands.
- The decoder turns %20 and + back into spaces and shows **exactly where** an invalid sequence like “50%off” or broken UTF-8 is.
- Spots **double encoding** (%2520) and decodes again with one click.
- Paste a full URL to see its host, path, fragment and every **query parameter decoded in a table** — edit, add or remove parameters and copy the updated URL.
- Optional strict RFC 3986 mode and line-by-line conversion. Everything runs in your browser.

### Features

- **Live, both ways**: Results update as you type. Switch between Encode and Decode and the result carries over.
- **Right encoding, explained**: Each mode says when to use it, so a URL doesn’t break because its slashes or ampersands were encoded.
- **Clear errors**: Instead of “URIError: malformed URI”, see which character is wrong and why.
- **Query parameter editor**: Read long tracking URLs at a glance, fix a value, remove a parameter, and get a correctly encoded URL back.
- **Batch mode**: Turn on Each line separately to encode or decode a whole list of values or URLs at once.
- **Private**: URLs with tokens or personal data never leave your device.

### How to encode or decode a URL

1. **Choose Encode or Decode** — Pick **Encode** to make text safe for a URL, or **Decode** to read an encoded link.
2. **Pick what you’re encoding** — Use **Parameter value** for a single value, **Whole URL** for a complete link, or **Form data** for form posts.
3. **Paste your text** — The result appears as you type. Problems are pointed out with the exact character.
4. **Copy or edit** — Copy the result, or edit the query parameters in the **URL parts** table and copy the updated URL.

### Guide

#### Which encoding should I use?

| You have | Use | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A value for ?q= or a path segment | Parameter value | chai & samosa → chai%20%26%20samosa |
| A complete URL with spaces or Hindi | Whole URL | https://x.in/a b → https://x.in/a%20b |
| Data for an HTML form or POST body | Form data | chai & samosa → chai+%26+samosa |

#### Common percent-encodings

| Character | Encoded | Character | Encoded |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| space | %20 (or + in forms) | & | %26 |
| / | %2F | = | %3D |
| ? | %3F | # | %23 |
| % | %25 | + | %2B |
| @ | %40 | ₹ | %E2%82%B9 |

### FAQ

**What is URL encoding?**
URLs may only contain a limited set of characters. URL (percent) encoding replaces any other character — spaces, &, non-English letters, emoji — with % followed by the hexadecimal value of each of its UTF-8 bytes, such as %20 for a space.

**Should a space be %20 or +?**
Both mean a space, in different places. %20 works everywhere in a URL; + means a space only in query strings and form data. When decoding, keep “+ means space” on for query strings and form data.

**What’s the difference between encodeURI and encodeURIComponent?**
encodeURI encodes a complete URL but leaves characters that structure it — : / ? & = # — alone. encodeURIComponent encodes those too, which is right for a single value you put inside a URL, but would break a whole URL.

**Why does decoding fail with “malformed URI”?**
The text contains a % that isn’t followed by two hexadecimal digits (like “50%off”), or bytes that aren’t valid UTF-8. The tool shows the exact character; encode a literal % as %25.

**What is double encoding?**
Encoding text that’s already encoded, so %20 becomes %2520. The tool notices when a decoded result still contains escapes and offers to decode it again.

**Is my URL sent anywhere?**
No. Encoding, decoding and parsing all happen in your browser.

## Fancy Font Generator

URL: https://justtools.online/text-tools/fancy-font-generator/
Category: Text Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-01

Turn text into stylish fonts to copy and paste: bold, italic, cursive, bubble, gothic and more for Instagram bios, WhatsApp, BGMI names and posts. Free.

### At a glance

- Converts your text into **28 styles**, including bold, italic, cursive (script), gothic (fraktur), double-struck, monospace, bubble, squares, small caps, upside down, strikethrough and glitch text.
- The “fonts” are really **Unicode characters**, so they stay styled wherever you paste them — Instagram and Facebook bios, WhatsApp, X, YouTube, Discord and game names.
- Letters that Unicode keeps elsewhere (like cursive ℬ, ℰ, ℋ) are filled in correctly, so no letter turns into a box.
- Also makes **decorated names** such as ꧁༺ 𝓝𝓪𝓶𝓮 ༻꧂ for profiles and gaming IDs.
- Pastes back to normal: the tool can turn fancy text into plain letters again.
- Hindi and other scripts pass through unchanged — the styles apply to English letters and digits.

### Features

- **Tap to copy**: Every style is shown with your own text. Tap one and it’s copied — ready to paste.
- **Works everywhere**: Unlike real fonts, these characters travel with the text into apps, bios, captions and comments.
- **Names and bios**: Decorated styles for Instagram bios, Free Fire and BGMI names, and WhatsApp statuses.
- **Strikethrough & underline**: Cross out or underline text in places that don’t support formatting.
- **Back to normal**: Paste stylised text to recover the plain letters for editing or searching.
- **Private**: Everything happens as you type, in your browser.

### How to make fancy text

1. **Type your text** — Enter a name, bio or message in the box.
2. **Browse the styles** — Scroll the list or filter by **Bold**, **Cursive & gothic**, **Bubble & boxes** and more.
3. **Copy** — Tap a style to copy it.
4. **Paste** — Paste it into your Instagram bio, WhatsApp, a game name field or a post.

### Guide

#### Where fancy text works

| Place | Works? | Tip |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Instagram bio, name and captions | Yes | Bios allow 150 characters; each fancy letter counts as one |
| WhatsApp messages and About | Yes | For plain bold or italic, WhatsApp also has *bold* and _italic_ |
| Facebook, X, Threads, YouTube comments | Yes | Keep it short — long styled posts are hard to read |
| Game names (BGMI, Free Fire) | Mostly | Games limit name length and some symbols; check the preview |
| Usernames and @handles | No | Handles only allow plain letters, numbers, . and _ |

#### A note on accessibility

Screen readers used by blind and low-vision people read these characters as mathematical symbols (“mathematical bold capital H…”) or skip them. Use fancy text for a name or a few decorative words, and keep important information — prices, dates, links, instructions — in normal text.

Search engines and in-app search also see different characters, so a name written in 𝓬𝓾𝓻𝓼𝓲𝓿𝓮 may not be found by people typing it normally.

### FAQ

**How does a fancy font generator work?**
It swaps each letter for a look-alike character from Unicode — the universal character set every phone and computer uses. For example, 𝐀 is “mathematical bold capital A”. Because they’re characters rather than a font, the style stays when you paste the text.

**Why do some letters show as boxes?**
The device you’re viewing on doesn’t have a font with that character — usually older phones. Bold, italic, cursive and bubble text work on almost all current devices; newer symbols may not.

**Can I use fancy text in my Instagram bio?**
Yes. Copy a style and paste it into Edit profile → Bio or Name. Each styled letter counts as one of the 150 bio characters.

**Can I make stylish names for BGMI or Free Fire?**
Yes — try the decorated styles. Games limit name length and may reject some symbols, so keep it short and check how it looks in the game.

**Does it work with Hindi?**
Unicode only has styled versions of the English alphabet and digits, so Hindi text stays as it is. You can mix both — the English parts get styled.

**How do I turn fancy text back to normal?**
Paste it into “Turn fancy text back into normal text” at the bottom of the tool, and copy the plain version.

## Base64 Encoder & Decoder

URL: https://justtools.online/developer-tools/base64-encoder-decoder/
Category: Developer Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-01

Encode text or files to Base64 and decode Base64 back — UTF-8, URL-safe Base64URL, data URLs for images, file type detection. Free, private, no upload.

### At a glance

- Encodes and decodes **Base64 (RFC 4648)** as you type, with text treated as **UTF-8** — Hindi, ₹ and emoji round-trip correctly.
- Supports **Base64URL** (- and _, as in JWTs), with or without = padding, and 76-character line wrapping for email (MIME).
- The decoder ignores spaces and line breaks, accepts missing padding and data: URLs, and says exactly which character is invalid.
- Decoded binary data is **recognised** — PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF, PDF, ZIP, MP3, MP4, fonts and more — with an image preview and a download button.
- Converts **any file to Base64** or a **data URL**, and gives ready-made <img> and CSS snippets for images.
- Runs entirely in your browser: nothing you encode or decode is uploaded.

### Features

- **Live both ways**: Switch between Encode and Decode and the result carries over — handy for checking a round trip.
- **Base64 to image or PDF**: Paste Base64 from an API or email source and get the actual file back, previewed and ready to save.
- **Image to data URL**: Drop an icon or logo to embed it directly in HTML, CSS or JSON.
- **Clear errors**: Invalid characters, misplaced padding and truncated input are explained instead of failing silently.
- **JWT friendly**: Decode the parts of a JSON Web Token — they’re Base64URL without padding.
- **Private**: Tokens, keys and files stay on your device.

### How to encode or decode Base64

1. **Choose text or file** — Use **Text** to convert text, or **File / image** to convert a file.
2. **Pick Encode or Decode** — Encode turns text into Base64; Decode turns Base64 back.
3. **Paste or drop** — Paste text or Base64, or drop a file. The result appears immediately.
4. **Copy or download** — Copy the result, or download the decoded file with the right extension.

### Guide

#### Base64 in a nutshell

Base64 writes any data — text, images, PDFs — using just 64 safe characters (A–Z, a–z, 0–9, + and /), so it can travel through systems made for text: JSON, XML, email, URLs and HTML. Every 3 bytes become 4 characters, so Base64 is about **33% larger** than the original.

**Base64 is not encryption.** Anyone can decode it instantly, so never use it to hide passwords or secrets. To protect data, encrypt it; to shorten it, compress it.

#### Standard vs URL-safe Base64

|  | Standard Base64 | Base64URL |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Characters 62 and 63 | + and / | - and _ |
| Padding | = at the end | Usually left out |
| Used in | Email attachments, data URLs, most APIs | URLs, file names, JWTs, WebAuthn |
| Example | Pz4/Pg== | Pz4_Pg |

### FAQ

**How do I convert Base64 to an image?**
Choose Text → Decode and paste the Base64 (with or without the data:image/…;base64, prefix). The tool recognises the image, shows a preview and lets you download it with the right extension.

**How do I convert an image to Base64?**
Choose File / image and drop the image. You get a data URL ready for an <img> tag or CSS, or plain Base64 if you switch to “Base64 only”.

**Why does my decoded text look garbled?**
The Base64 probably holds binary data (an image, a PDF, compressed data) rather than text — the tool then shows the file type instead. If it’s text in an old encoding other than UTF-8, some characters may not show correctly.

**Is Base64 secure?**
No. It’s an encoding, not encryption: anyone can decode it. Use it to transport data, not to protect it.

**What is the = at the end?**
Padding, which makes the length a multiple of 4. Base64URL often leaves it out; this decoder works either way.

**Is my data uploaded?**
No. Encoding and decoding happen entirely in your browser, including for files.

## Case Converter

URL: https://justtools.online/text-tools/case-converter/
Category: Text Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-01

Change text case online: UPPERCASE, lowercase, Title Case, Sentence case, and camelCase, snake_case or kebab-case for code. Smart rules, instant, free.

### At a glance

- Seven text cases: **Sentence case, lower case, UPPER CASE, Title Case, Capitalized Case, aLtErNaTiNg** and **iNVERSE**.
- Eight programming cases: **camelCase, PascalCase, snake_case, CONSTANT_CASE, kebab-case, Train-Case, dot.case** and **path/case** — one name per line.
- **Title Case** keeps articles and short words lowercase (“The Lord of the Rings”), but capitalises the first and last word and the word after a colon.
- **Sentence case** capitalises the start of every sentence and the word “I”, and fixes text typed with Caps Lock on.
- Keeps **acronyms and brand names** like NASA, GST and iPhone as written (can be switched off), and handles hyphens (Well-Known) and apostrophes (Don’t).
