- Splits programming names smartly: XMLHttpRequest becomes xml_http_request. Counts characters, words, sentences and lines as you type.

### Features

- **Fix Caps Lock text**: Paste text that was typed in capitals and turn it into normal sentences in one click.
- **Proper headlines**: Title Case that follows style-guide rules — for blog titles, YouTube titles, headings and book names.
- **For developers**: Convert variable, column, CSS class and URL names between camelCase, snake_case, kebab-case and more.
- **Line by line**: Paste a list of names and convert them all at once — each line stays a separate name.
- **Live counts**: See the number of characters, words, sentences and lines while you work.
- **Private**: Your text is converted in your browser and never sent anywhere.

### How to change text case

1. **Paste your text** — Type or paste text into the box, or try the **Sample**.
2. **Pick a case** — Click **UPPER CASE**, **Title Case**, **Sentence case**, **snake_case** or any other.
3. **Check the result** — The converted text appears below straight away.
4. **Copy** — Click **Copy**, download it as a .txt file, or **Replace my text** to keep working on it.

### Guide

#### Which case to use

| Case | Example | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sentence case | Tips for your first job interview | Most headings on the web, emails, UI text |
| Title Case | Tips for Your First Job Interview | Book, film and article titles, formal headings |
| UPPER CASE | SALE ENDS TODAY | Short labels and warnings (reads as shouting in messages) |
| camelCase | firstJobInterview | JavaScript and Java variables |
| snake_case | first_job_interview | Python, database columns, file names |
| kebab-case | first-job-interview | URLs, CSS classes, file names |
| CONSTANT_CASE | MAX_RETRY_COUNT | Constants and environment variables |

#### Title Case rules used here

Every word is capitalised except articles (a, an, the), short conjunctions (and, but, or, nor, for, so, yet) and short prepositions (as, at, by, in, of, off, on, per, to, up, via) — unless they are the first or last word, or come right after a colon. This matches the common ground of the Chicago and AP style guides for most headlines.

Hyphenated words get a capital on each part (Well-Known), words after apostrophes stay lowercase (Don’t, India’s), and words already written as acronyms or brands (NASA, iPhone) are left alone.

### FAQ

**How do I convert uppercase to lowercase?**
Paste your text and click “lower case” — or “Sentence case” to also capitalise the start of each sentence, which is usually what you want for text typed with Caps Lock on.

**What is the difference between Title Case and Capitalized Case?**
Capitalized Case capitalises every word. Title Case follows style-guide rules and keeps small words like “of”, “the” and “and” lowercase, as in “The Lord of the Rings”.

**Does it work with Hindi?**
Hindi and most Indian scripts don’t have upper and lower case, so they stay unchanged. English words mixed in are converted.

**Can I convert a list of variable names?**
Yes. Put one name per line and choose a programming case. userAccountId, user-account-id and User Account ID all become user_account_id in snake_case.

**Why wasn’t NASA changed to Nasa?**
Words already written in capitals or mixed case are treated as acronyms and brand names and kept as written. Turn off “Keep acronyms and brand names” to change them too. Text written entirely in capitals is always converted.

**Is my text saved?**
No. The conversion runs in your browser and nothing is stored or sent.

Write Markdown with a live preview: GitHub tables, task lists, alerts and highlighted code. Export to HTML or PDF — free, private, runs in your browser.

### How to preview Markdown

### Guide

#### Markdown cheat sheet

| You type | You get |
| --- | --- |
| # Heading, ## Subheading | Headings (levels 1–6) |
| **bold**, _italic_, ~~strike~~ | Bold, italic, strikethrough |
| [text](https://example.com) | A link |
| ![alt text](image.png) | An image |
| - item, 1. item | Bulleted and numbered lists |
| - [ ] task, - [x] done | Task list with checkboxes |
| `code`, ``` for blocks | Inline code and code blocks (add a language: ```js) |
| > quote, > [!NOTE] | Quote, or a GitHub alert box |
| | a | b |, | --- | :-: | | Table (colons set the alignment) |
| --- | Horizontal divider |

#### Line breaks in Markdown

In README files and most Markdown documents, a single line break is ignored and lines join into one paragraph — leave an empty line to start a new paragraph, or end a line with two spaces to force a break. GitHub comments and issues are different: every line break shows. Switch on **Line breaks as typed** to preview that behaviour.

### FAQ

**What is Markdown?**
A simple way to format text with ordinary characters — **bold**, # headings, - lists — that converts to HTML. It’s used for README files, documentation, notes apps, forums and chat apps.

**Does the preview match GitHub?**
It follows GitHub Flavored Markdown and GitHub’s styles, including tables, task lists, alerts and code highlighting. Very new or GitHub-only features such as Mermaid diagrams, math and @mentions aren’t rendered.

**How do I convert Markdown to PDF?**
Click Print / PDF and choose “Save as PDF” as the printer. The PDF uses a clean, light document style.

**Is my text saved or uploaded?**
It isn’t uploaded anywhere. With “Save draft in this browser” on, the text is kept in this browser’s local storage so it survives a refresh; switch it off to clear it.

**Can I use HTML inside Markdown?**
Yes, common HTML such as <details>, <kbd> and <sup> works. Scripts, forms, iframes and inline styles are removed for safety, as on GitHub.

**Can I open a .md file?**
Yes. Click Open and choose a .md or .markdown file; it loads straight into the editor.

## Compare PDFs

URL: https://justtools.online/pdf-tools/compare-pdf/
Category: PDF Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-05

Compare two PDFs online and see what changed: added and removed words highlighted, plus a page-by-page visual diff. Free and private — nothing is uploaded.

### At a glance

- **Text changes** compares the two PDFs word by word: added words are green, removed words are red and struck through.
- A summary shows the number of changes, words added and removed, how much text is unchanged and **which pages** changed.
- **Show only changes** folds unchanged text away, and you can jump from one change to the next.
- **Visual** compares pages pixel by pixel to catch changes in layout, images, stamps, signatures and scanned pages, in **Side by side** or **Overlay** view.
- Every page pair is checked quickly so pages that look different are marked; pages can be paired by hand when one was added or removed.
- Save the text comparison as a self-contained **HTML report** to share or keep.
- Runs entirely in your browser with PDF.js — neither file is uploaded.

### Features

- **Review contracts**: See exactly what the other side changed in a rent agreement, offer letter or vendor contract before you sign it.
- **Word-level detail**: A changed amount, date or name is highlighted on its own, not the whole paragraph, so small edits don’t slip past.
- **Catch visual edits**: The Visual view finds changes the text can’t show — a moved logo, a different stamp, a new signature or edits in a scanned page.
- **Jump between changes**: Step through a long document change by change, with the page number of each one.
- **Shareable report**: Download the highlighted differences as one HTML file that opens in any browser.
- **Private**: Confidential drafts stay on your device. No upload, no sign-up and no limits.

### How to compare two PDF files

1. **Add both PDFs** — Drop the **Original** in the first box and the **Changed** version in the second — or drop both at once.
2. **Read the text changes** — Green words were added and red ones removed. Use the arrows to go from one change to the next.
3. **Check the pages** — Open **Visual** to see the pages side by side or overlaid, with changed areas tinted.
4. **Save a report** — Click **Download report** to keep the highlighted text differences as an HTML file.

### Guide

#### Text or visual comparison?

|  | Text changes | Visual |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Finds | Added, removed and replaced words | Anything that looks different |
| Works on scanned PDFs | No — needs selectable text | Yes |
| Ignores reflowed text | Yes — compares words, not positions | No — moved text shows as changed |
| Best for | Contracts, reports, policies | Drawings, forms, letterheads, scans |

#### Good to know

The text comparison looks at words, not fonts or colours, so a change only to bold, size or colour shows up in the **Visual** view instead.

If a page was inserted, later pages in the Visual view are paired with the wrong page. Choose the matching pages from the **Original** and **Changed** lists to line them up again; the text comparison isn’t affected.

Need to fix the order of pages before comparing? Use the [PDF Page Organizer](https://justtools.online/pdf-tools/pdf-page-organizer/).

### FAQ

**How do I compare two PDF files for differences?**
Add the original and the changed PDF here. The text differences appear straight away — green for added, red for removed — and the Visual tab shows what changed on each page.

**Can it compare scanned PDFs?**
Yes, with the **Visual** comparison, which compares the pages as images. The word-by-word comparison needs PDFs with selectable text.

**Does it work with Hindi and other languages?**
Yes, as long as the PDF has selectable text. Words are compared in any language; some older PDFs with Hindi text store it in a way that can’t be read back, and then the Visual view works best.

**Can I compare PDFs with a different number of pages?**
Yes. The text comparison follows the words across pages, and in the Visual view you can pair any page of the original with any page of the changed PDF.

**Are my files uploaded?**
No. Both PDFs are read and compared in your browser, so confidential documents never leave your device.

**Is there a file size or page limit?**
No fixed limit. Very large PDFs depend on your device’s memory; documents of a few hundred pages work on most computers.

## PDF Page Organizer

URL: https://justtools.online/pdf-tools/pdf-page-organizer/

Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-05

Rearrange PDF pages online: drag to reorder, rotate, delete, duplicate, add blank pages or pages from other PDFs. Free, private, no upload, with undo.

### At a glance

- **Drag pages** by their handle to reorder them; selected pages move together. Works with a mouse or touch.
- **Select** one or many pages to rotate, duplicate, move to the start or end, delete, or **Extract** them into a new PDF.
- Insert **blank pages** (the size of the pages around them) and pages from **other PDFs**, including password-protected ones.

- Runs entirely in your browser with pdf-lib and PDF.js — files are never uploaded.

### Features

- **See every page**: Thumbnails of all pages, with a size slider, so you can spot the out-of-place scan or the blank page straight away.
- **Drag and drop**: Move one page or a whole selection to where it belongs; the list scrolls as you drag.
- **Combine documents**: Add pages from another PDF and slot them in — like inserting a signed page back into an agreement.
- **Clean up scans**: Rotate sideways pages, delete blank ones, and reverse a stack that was scanned last page first.
- **Undo anything**: Try things out freely: every move, rotation and deletion can be undone or redone.
- **Private**: Your files stay on your device. No upload, no sign-up and no watermark.

### How to rearrange PDF pages

1. **Open the PDF** — Drop the PDF onto the box. Enter its password if it has one.
2. **Reorder** — Drag pages by their handle, or select pages and use **Move to start** or **Move to end**.
3. **Edit pages** — Rotate, **Duplicate** or **Delete** selected pages, and add a **Blank page** or pages with **Add PDF**.
4. **Save** — Click **Save PDF** to download the organised document, or **Extract** to save only the selected pages.

### Guide

#### Which page tool do I need?

| You want to… | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Reorder, delete, duplicate or insert pages | PDF Page Organizer |
| Join whole PDFs one after another | [Merge PDF](https://justtools.online/pdf-tools/merge-pdf/) |
| Split a PDF into several files | [Split PDF](https://justtools.online/pdf-tools/split-pdf/) |
| Only rotate pages | [Rotate PDF](https://justtools.online/pdf-tools/rotate-pdf/) |
| Number the pages afterwards | [Add Page Numbers](https://justtools.online/pdf-tools/add-page-numbers/) |

### FAQ

**How do I rearrange the pages of a PDF?**
Open the PDF here, drag each page by its handle to its new place, then click **Save PDF**. You can also select pages and move them to the start or end in one go.

**How do I delete pages from a PDF?**
Tap the pages to select them and click **Delete**. If you change your mind, click **Undo**.

**Can I add pages from another PDF?**
Yes. Click **Add PDF** and choose the file; its pages are added after the selected page, or at the end, and each source gets a letter badge so you can tell them apart.

**Will the quality change?**
No. Pages are copied, not redrawn, so text, images and links on the page look exactly as before.

**Are bookmarks kept?**
No. The document is rebuilt in the new order, so the old bookmarks (outline) aren’t carried over. Page content always is.

**Are my files uploaded?**
No. Everything happens in your browser, and your PDFs never leave your device.

## Add Page Numbers to PDF

URL: https://justtools.online/pdf-tools/add-page-numbers/
Category: PDF Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-05

Add page numbers to a PDF online: 1, Page 1 of 10, Roman numerals or your own format, in any corner. Skip the cover, number from any page. Free, no upload.

### At a glance

- Formats: **1**, **Page 1**, **1 of 10**, **Page 1 of 10**, **– 1 –**, **Roman numerals** (i, ii, iii) or a **custom format** such as “Exhibit A – {n:4}”.
- Six positions — top or bottom, left, centre or right — with a **Double-sided** option that swaps left and right on alternate pages for printed booklets.
- **Start on page** skips a cover or index, and **First number** sets the number printed there; the last page can be left without a number.
- Fonts: sans (Helvetica), serif (Times) or mono (Courier), regular or bold, any size, colour and distance from the edge.
- Numbers are added as real text, so the PDF stays sharp and searchable; text in other scripts, such as Hindi, is added as a crisp image.
- Rotated and mixed-size pages are numbered the right way up, in the same place on every page.
- Bookmarks, links and form fields are kept. Runs entirely in your browser with pdf-lib — the file is never uploaded.

### Features

- **Every common format**: Plain numbers, “Page 1 of 10”, dashes or Roman numerals for a preface — or build your own with {n}, {total} and zero-padded {n:4}.
- **Skip the cover**: Start numbering on page 2 or 3 and choose the first number, so a title page and contents don’t throw the count off.
- **Ready for print**: Double-sided mode puts numbers on the outer edge of facing pages, like a printed book or bound report.
- **See it first**: Preview the number on every page — position, size and colour — before anything is saved.
- **Court and office bundles**: Number a bundle, annexure or set of exhibits with a custom label like “Annexure P-{n}” or simple Bates-style numbering such as “DOC-{n:6}”.
- **Private**: Your document stays on your device. No upload, no sign-up and no watermark.

### How to add page numbers to a PDF

1. **Open the PDF** — Drop the PDF onto the box. Enter its password if it has one.
2. **Choose a format** — Pick a **Format** such as “Page 1 of 10”, or **Custom format** to write your own.
3. **Place the numbers** — Choose a **Position**, then set **Start on page** and **First number** if the first pages shouldn’t be numbered.
4. **Style and download** — Adjust the font, size, colour and margin, check the preview, then click **Number pages**.

### Guide

#### Custom formats

**{total}** is the last number printed, so it stays correct when you skip a cover or start from a number other than 1.

| You type | Page 1 shows | Page 12 of 40 shows |
| --- | --- | --- |
| {n} | 1 | 12 |
| Page {n} of {total} | Page 1 of 40 | Page 12 of 40 |
| {n:4} | 0001 | 0012 |
| Annexure P-{n} | Annexure P-1 | Annexure P-12 |
| {roman} | i | xii |
| Report 2026 · {n} | Report 2026 · 1 | Report 2026 · 12 |

#### Tips

Putting a book together? Number the preface in Roman numerals and the main text from 1: [split the PDF](https://justtools.online/pdf-tools/split-pdf/), number each part, then [merge them](https://justtools.online/pdf-tools/merge-pdf/) back together.

Need pages in a different order first? Use the [PDF Page Organizer](https://justtools.online/pdf-tools/pdf-page-organizer/) before numbering, so the numbers follow the final order.

### FAQ

**How do I add page numbers to a PDF for free?**
Open the PDF here, choose a format and position, and click **Number pages**. It’s free, with no sign-up or watermark, and the file never leaves your device.

**Can I start numbering from page 2 or 3?**
Yes. Set **Start on page** to the first page that should have a number, and **First number** to the number it should show — for example page 3 numbered as 1.

**Can I add “Page X of Y”?**
Yes. Choose **Page 1 of 10** or **1 of 10**. Y is the last number printed, so it is right even when you skip pages.

**Will the numbers be searchable?**
Yes, for English and other Latin-script text — the numbers are real text in a standard PDF font. Labels in scripts such as Hindi are added as a high-resolution image.

**Will it work on scanned or rotated pages?**
Yes. Numbers are placed on the page as you see it, so landscape, rotated and scanned pages all get them the right way up.

**Is my file uploaded?**
No. The numbers are added in your browser, so confidential documents stay on your device.

## Crop PDF

URL: https://justtools.online/pdf-tools/crop-pdf/
Category: PDF Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-05

Crop PDF pages online: drag a box or auto-detect white margins, then crop one page, some or all. Free, private, no upload — text stays sharp and selectable.

### At a glance

- Drag the **crop box** on the page preview, or type exact margins in **millimetres** for the top, bottom, left and right.
- **Auto-detect margins** finds the empty white border around the content, checking up to 24 of the pages you are cropping, spread through the document.
- Crop **all pages**, **this page**, or a list such as “1, 3-5, even”.
- Cropping is lossless: text stays selectable and images keep their quality, because the pages aren’t redrawn.
- Cropping **hides** the area outside the box — that content is still in the file. Use Redact PDF to remove information for good.
- Rotated and landscape pages are cropped as you see them. Bookmarks, links and form fields are kept.
- Runs entirely in your browser with pdf-lib and PDF.js — the file is never uploaded.

### Features

- **Trim white margins**: Make slides, papers and e-books easier to read on a phone or tablet by cutting away wide empty borders.
- **Auto-detect**: One click finds where the content starts and ends on your pages, with a little padding so nothing is clipped.
- **Exact sizes**: Drag the box for a quick crop, or type margins in millimetres when you need a precise result.
- **Any pages**: Crop the whole document, only the page you’re looking at, or chosen pages like “2-4” or “odd”.
- **No quality loss**: Pages aren’t turned into images, so text stays sharp and searchable and the file size barely changes.
- **Private**: Your PDF stays on your device. No upload, no sign-up and no watermark.

### How to crop a PDF

1. **Open the PDF** — Drop the PDF onto the box. Enter its password if it has one.
2. **Set the crop** — Drag the edges of the crop box, type margins in mm, or click **Auto-detect margins**.
3. **Choose the pages** — Pick **All**, **This page** or **Choose** and type pages such as “1, 3-5”.
4. **Crop and download** — Click **Crop pages**. The cropped PDF downloads straight away.

### Guide

#### Crop, resize or redact?

| You want to… | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Cut away margins or keep part of a page | Crop PDF |
| Hide something for good — a name, number or signature | [Redact PDF](https://justtools.online/pdf-tools/redact-pdf/) |
| Make the file smaller | [Compress PDF](https://justtools.online/pdf-tools/compress-pdf/) |
| Turn sideways pages the right way | [Rotate PDF](https://justtools.online/pdf-tools/rotate-pdf/) |

#### Is cropped content really gone?

No. Like Adobe Acrobat and most PDF editors, cropping sets the visible area of each page; the content outside it is hidden but still in the file, and can be shown again in a PDF editor. That makes cropping reversible, but not safe for hiding sensitive information.

To remove an account number, address or signature permanently, use [Redact PDF](https://justtools.online/pdf-tools/redact-pdf/) instead.

### FAQ

**How do I crop a PDF for free?**
Open the PDF here, drag the crop box or click **Auto-detect margins**, choose the pages and click **Crop**. It’s free and nothing is uploaded.

**Can I crop just one page?**
Yes. Go to the page and choose **This page**, or choose **Choose** and type the page numbers you want, such as “4” or “2-6”.

**Does cropping reduce quality?**
No. The pages aren’t redrawn or turned into images, so text and pictures look exactly as before.

**Does cropping make the file smaller?**
Not noticeably — the hidden content is still in the file. To make it smaller, use Compress PDF.

**Can I undo a crop?**
In a PDF editor, yes, because the content is only hidden. Keep your original file as well, just in case.

**Is my PDF uploaded?**
No. Cropping happens in your browser and the file never leaves your device.

## Sign PDF

URL: https://justtools.online/pdf-tools/sign-pdf/
Category: PDF Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-05

Sign a PDF online for free: draw, type or upload your signature, add initials and the date, and place them on any page. Private — nothing is uploaded.

### At a glance

- Create a signature three ways: **Draw** it, **Type** your name in one of four handwriting styles, or **Upload** a photo of your signature on paper.
- Uploaded photos can have the **paper removed**, leaving clean black or blue ink on a transparent background.
- Add **initials**, **today’s date** and short **text** such as your name or “Approved”, and put a signature **on every page** with one switch.
- Drag to place and resize each signature; it is added to the PDF exactly where you see it, the right way up on rotated pages.
- This adds an **image-based electronic signature**. It is not a certificate-based digital signature (DSC) or Aadhaar eSign.
- Signatures can be **remembered on this device** if you choose; otherwise they are forgotten when you close the page.
- Runs entirely in your browser with pdf-lib and PDF.js — your document and signature are never uploaded.

### Features

- **Draw, type or upload**: Sign with a finger on your phone, a mouse or a pen — or type your name in a signature style, or scan the one you use on paper.
- **Clean scans**: Photograph your signature on white paper and the tool removes the background, so it sits naturally on the page.
- **Initials and dates**: Add initials to every page of an agreement and today’s date beside your signature, without printing anything.
- **Exact placement**: Drag each mark onto the signature line and resize it; what you see in the preview is what’s saved.
- **Works on phones**: Open the PDF from WhatsApp or email, sign with your finger and share it back — no app or account needed.
- **Private**: Your signature never leaves your device. No upload, no sign-up and no watermark.

### How to sign a PDF online

1. **Open the PDF** — Drop the PDF onto the box. Enter its password if it has one.
2. **Create your signature** — Choose **Draw**, **Type** or **Upload**, then click **Use this**. Switch to **Initials** to add those too.
3. **Place it** — Go to the right page, drag the signature onto the line and resize it. Add the date or text if needed.
4. **Download** — Click **Sign and download** to save the signed PDF.

### Guide

#### Is a signature added this way legally valid?

This tool adds a picture of your signature to the page — an **electronic signature** in the everyday sense, like signing a printout and scanning it. Many businesses, landlords, schools and HR teams accept it for routine documents such as offer letters, rental agreements, forms and invoices.

It is **not** a certificate-based digital signature. In India, documents that legally require an electronic signature under the IT Act — for example many government filings, tenders and company returns — need a **Digital Signature Certificate (DSC)** or **Aadhaar eSign**, which this tool does not provide. If you are unsure, ask the person or office who will receive the document.

#### Tips for a good signature

For an uploaded signature, sign with a dark pen on plain white paper, photograph it in good light from directly above, and keep **Remove the paper** on.

Sign last: make any other changes first — for example [add page numbers](https://justtools.online/pdf-tools/add-page-numbers/) or [rearrange pages](https://justtools.online/pdf-tools/pdf-page-organizer/) — then sign. To stop anyone moving or editing filled form fields afterwards, [flatten the PDF](https://justtools.online/pdf-tools/flatten-pdf/).

### FAQ

**How do I sign a PDF for free?**
Open the PDF here, draw, type or upload your signature, drag it into place and click **Sign and download**. It’s free, with no sign-up or watermark.

**Can I sign a PDF on my phone?**
Yes. Open this page on your phone, choose the PDF, and draw your signature with your finger. The signed PDF downloads to your phone, ready to share.

**Is this a digital signature (DSC) or Aadhaar eSign?**
No. It places an image of your signature on the page. Documents that legally need a certificate-based digital signature require a DSC or Aadhaar eSign from a licensed provider.

**Can I add my signature to every page?**
Yes. Select the placed signature or initials and turn on **On every page**. It appears in the same spot on all pages.

**Is my signature stored or uploaded?**
No. It is never uploaded. It stays in this browser tab, and is saved on your device only if you turn on **Remember on this device**.

**Can someone remove my signature from the PDF?**
Someone with a PDF editor could. To make the page harder to change, flatten the PDF or turn it into images after signing, and keep a copy of what you sent.

## JSON to XML Converter

URL: https://justtools.online/developer-tools/json-to-xml/
Category: Developer Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-05

Convert JSON to XML online: attributes, text, arrays and nested data, with a root element, CDATA and pretty or minified output. Free and private, no upload.

### At a glance

- Keys starting with **@** become attributes and **#text** becomes element text — the same convention as the XML to JSON converter, so data round-trips.
- Arrays can **repeat the element** (`<tag>a</tag><tag>b</tag>`) or **wrap each item** (`<tags><item>a</item>…</tags>`), and nested arrays always produce valid XML.
- Data without a single root is wrapped in a **root element** you can name; top-level arrays get one item element per entry.
- Keys that aren’t valid XML names are fixed (“first name” → `first_name`, “2nd” → `_2nd`) and listed, and characters XML can’t hold are removed and reported.
- Options for the XML declaration, **CDATA** sections, self-closing empty elements and 2-space, 4-space, tab or minified output.
- Accepts relaxed JSON (comments, trailing commas, single quotes) and points to the exact line and column of real errors. Big numbers keep every digit.
- Runs entirely in your browser — the JSON is never uploaded.

### Features

- **Attributes and text**: Write `{"price": {"@currency": "INR", "#text": "799"}}` and get `<price currency="INR">799</price>` — exactly what most XML APIs expect.
- **Your array style**: Repeat the element for each entry, or wrap entries in item elements — whichever the receiving system wants.
- **Always valid XML**: Invalid names are fixed, special characters escaped, mixed content kept on one line and empty arrays handled, with a note for every change.
- **Round-trips**: Switch to XML → JSON at any time: the result converts straight back, so you can edit data as JSON and send it as XML.
- **Exact numbers**: IDs and amounts like 12345678901234567890 or 1.50 are written exactly as in the JSON, never rounded.
- **Private**: API payloads and configs stay on your device. No upload, no sign-up.

### How to convert JSON to XML

1. **Paste the JSON** — Paste JSON into the left box, open a .json file, or try the **Sample**.
2. **Set the options** — Open **Options** to choose the root and item element names, how arrays are written, CDATA and the XML declaration.
3. **Check the result** — The XML appears as you type, with notes about anything that was renamed, wrapped or removed.
4. **Copy or download** — Click **Copy**, or **Download** to save an .xml file.

### Guide

#### How JSON maps to XML

| JSON | XML |
| --- | --- |
| `{"user": {"name": "Asha"}}` | `<user><name>Asha</name></user>` |
| `{"user": {"@id": "7"}}` | `<user id="7"/>` |
| `{"price": {"@currency": "INR", "#text": 799}}` | `<price currency="INR">799</price>` |
| `{"list": {"tag": ["a", "b"]}}` | `<list><tag>a</tag><tag>b</tag></list>` (or wrapped: `<list><tag><item>a</item><item>b</item></tag></list>`) |
| `{"note": null}` | `<note/>` |
| `[1, 2]` | `<root><item>1</item><item>2</item></root>` |

#### Good to know

XML has no data types, so numbers, booleans and null all become text: `true` is written as `<paid>true</paid>`. An empty array can’t be shown with repeated elements, so it is left out (with a note) unless you choose **Wrap items**.

Converting the other way? Use the [XML to JSON converter](https://justtools.online/developer-tools/xml-to-json/). To check or tidy JSON first, try the [JSON Formatter](https://justtools.online/developer-tools/json-formatter/).

### FAQ

**How do I convert JSON to XML?**
Paste your JSON into the box. The XML appears on the right straight away — copy it or download it as an .xml file.

**How do I make an XML attribute from JSON?**
Start the key with @. For example `{"book": {"@id": "42", "title": "Gitanjali"}}` becomes `<book id="42"><title>Gitanjali</title></book>`. You can change the prefix under Options.

**How are JSON arrays converted?**
By default each entry repeats the element: `"tag": ["a","b"]` gives two `<tag>` elements. Choose **Wrap items** to get `<tag><item>a</item><item>b</item></tag>` instead, and set the item element’s name.

**Why was my data wrapped in <root>?**
An XML document must have exactly one top-level element. If your JSON has several top-level keys, or is an array, it’s wrapped in a root element — you can rename it under Options.

**Can it convert invalid JSON?**
It accepts common slips — comments, trailing commas, single quotes and unquoted keys — and tells you what it fixed. For real errors it shows the line and column so you can correct them.

**Is my JSON uploaded?**
No. The conversion runs in your browser, so API responses, keys and customer data never leave your device.

## Cron Expression Generator

URL: https://justtools.online/developer-tools/cron-expression-generator/
Category: Developer Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-05

Build and explain cron expressions in plain English with next run times. Supports Linux crontab, Quartz, Spring and AWS EventBridge, and converts between them.

### At a glance

- Four formats: **Unix / Linux cron** (crontab, Kubernetes, GitHub Actions), **Quartz** (with seconds and year), **Spring @Scheduled** and **AWS EventBridge**.
- Explains any expression in **plain English** — e.g. `30 9 * * 1-5` is “At 9:30 AM, Monday through Friday” — in 12- or 24-hour time.
- Shows the **next 10 run times** in your time zone or UTC, including L, W and # rules, leap years and the Unix “either day” rule.
- **Converts** a schedule between formats, rewriting day-of-week numbers (Sunday is 0 in Unix and Spring but 1 in Quartz and AWS), `?` and seconds — or explains why it can’t.
- Errors point to the exact field (“Hour: 24 is out of range (0–23)”), and an expression in the wrong format is recognised and you’re offered a switch.
- Presets and a simple builder for every few minutes or hours, daily, weekly, monthly and yearly schedules, plus ready-to-paste crontab, GitHub Actions, Kubernetes, Spring and AWS snippets.
- Warns about schedules that never run (30 February) or skip months, and about day-of-month + day-of-week combinations that run more often than expected.

### Features

- **Plain-English check**: Paste the expression from a crontab, YAML file or code review and read what it actually does before it ships.
- **Real next runs**: See the next ten dates and times — “in 3 h 15 min” — so a schedule that’s off by a day or an hour is obvious.
- **Every scheduler**: Unix cron, Quartz, Spring and AWS each have their own rules. Pick the one you use and the syntax is checked for it.
- **Convert between them**: Moving a job from crontab to Spring or EventBridge? Get the equivalent expression with day numbers and “?” fixed.
- **Build without memorising**: Choose “Every week”, tick Mon–Fri and pick a time — the expression is written for you.
- **Share a schedule**: Copy a link that opens the tool with your expression and format, for a ticket or code review.

### How to create a cron expression

1. **Pick the format** — Choose **Unix**, **Quartz**, **Spring** or **AWS** — the one your scheduler uses.
2. **Build or paste** — Click a preset, use **Build a schedule**, or paste an expression and edit any field.
3. **Check it** — Read the plain-English description and the **Next runs**; switch between your time zone and UTC.
4. **Copy it** — Copy the expression or a ready-made snippet for crontab, GitHub Actions, Kubernetes, Spring or AWS.

### Guide

#### Cron syntax at a glance

`*` any value · `,` list (1,15) · `-` range (9-17) · `/` step (*/15) · `?` no value · `L` last · `W` nearest weekday · `#` nth weekday (FRI#3).

| Field | Unix | Quartz / Spring | AWS |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Second | — | 0–59 | — |
| Minute | 0–59 | 0–59 | 0–59 |
| Hour | 0–23 | 0–23 | 0–23 |
| Day of month | 1–31 | 1–31, L, W, ? | 1–31, L, W, ? |
| Month | 1–12 or JAN–DEC | 1–12 or JAN–DEC | 1–12 or JAN–DEC |
| Day of week | 0–7 (0 and 7 = Sun) | Quartz 1–7 (1 = Sun) · Spring 0–7, L, # | 1–7 (1 = Sun), L, #, ? |
| Year | — | Quartz only, optional | 1970–2199 |

#### Common cron expressions

| Schedule | Unix cron | Quartz |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Every 5 minutes | `*/5 * * * *` | `0 */5 * * * ?` |
| Every hour | `0 * * * *` | `0 0 * * * ?` |
| Every day at midnight | `0 0 * * *` | `0 0 0 * * ?` |
| Weekdays at 9:30 AM | `30 9 * * 1-5` | `0 30 9 ? * MON-FRI` |
| Every Sunday at 6 PM | `0 18 * * 0` | `0 0 18 ? * SUN` |
| 1st of every month | `0 0 1 * *` | `0 0 0 1 * ?` |
| Last day of the month | not possible | `0 0 0 L * ?` |

#### Things that often go wrong

**Time zones:** cron uses the server’s time zone, GitHub Actions always uses UTC, and EventBridge rules run in UTC. Check the next runs in UTC if your job runs at the “wrong” hour.

**Both day fields in Unix cron:** `0 0 1 * 1` runs on the 1st **and** every Monday, not only on Mondays that are the 1st.

**Day numbers:** Monday is 1 in Unix and Spring but 2 in Quartz and AWS. Using names like MON avoids mistakes.

### FAQ

**How do I run a cron job every 5 minutes?**
Use `*/5 * * * *` in Unix cron. In Quartz it’s `0 */5 * * * ?`, in Spring `0 */5 * * * *` and in AWS `*/5 * * * ? *`.

**What does * * * * * mean?**
Every minute. The five fields are minute, hour, day of month, month and day of week; * means “every”.

**What is the difference between Unix cron and Quartz cron?**
Quartz adds a seconds field at the start (and an optional year), numbers days of the week 1–7 starting with Sunday, needs a “?” in either day-of-month or day-of-week, and supports L, W and #. The tool converts between them.

**How do I schedule a job on the last day of the month?**
Use L in day-of-month in Quartz, Spring or AWS, e.g. `0 0 0 L * ?`. Standard Unix cron has no last-day option; a common workaround is to run daily on days 28–31 and check the date in the script.

**Why does my GitHub Actions schedule run at a different time?**
GitHub Actions cron is always in UTC (and may start a few minutes late when busy). India is UTC+5:30, so 9:00 AM IST is `30 3 * * *`. Switch Next runs to UTC to check.

**Can cron run every 30 seconds?**
Not standard Unix cron — its smallest unit is a minute. Quartz and Spring have a seconds field: `*/30 * * * * ?` (Quartz) or `*/30 * * * * *` (Spring).

## CSS to Tailwind Converter

URL: https://justtools.online/developer-tools/css-to-tailwind/
Category: Developer Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-05

Convert CSS to Tailwind classes online: hover, media queries, dark mode and gradients become variants, colours match the palette. Tailwind v4 and v3, free.

### At a glance

- Outputs **Tailwind v4** classes by default, or **v3** — scales, colour names and syntax differ (for example `p-3.25` and `shadow-sm` in v4 vs `p-[13px]` and `shadow` in v3).
- `:hover`, `:focus`, `::before`, `:first-child`, `[aria-expanded="true"]`, `@media (min-width: 768px)`, dark mode and `@supports` become **variants** like `hover:`, `before:`, `first:`, `aria-expanded:`, `md:`, `dark:` and `supports-[…]:`.
- `.card:hover .title` becomes `group-hover:` (adding `group` to `.card`) and `input:checked + label` becomes `peer-checked:`.
- Colours in hex, rgb(), hsl() or OKLCH are matched to the **Tailwind palette** (v3 hex and v4 colours), with opacity like `bg-black/50`; an option picks the nearest palette colour.
- Shorthands are merged into Tailwind shortcuts: `px-4`, `truncate`, `size-10`, `line-clamp-3`, gradients as `bg-linear-to-r from-… to-…`.
- Anything without an exact class becomes an **arbitrary value** (`p-[13px]`, `[-webkit-text-stroke:1px]`), highlighted so you can review it; close-but-not-identical matches are marked.
- The converter is tested against the real Tailwind v4 compiler, so the classes it writes exist. Runs in your browser — your CSS isn’t uploaded.

### Features

- **Whole stylesheets**: Paste rules, media queries and nested CSS together — classes are grouped by element, with each breakpoint and state in one class list.
- **Exact, not guessed**: 13px stays 13px. Values are only replaced by a Tailwind step when it is exactly the same; otherwise you get an arbitrary value.
- **Honest approximations**: Where Tailwind is close but different — like CSS “ease” vs ease-in-out — the class is marked and the difference explained.
- **Palette matching**: Recognises Tailwind colours from design files, including v4’s OKLCH values, and keeps opacity as /50 modifiers.
- **See where it came from**: Hover a class, or open “How each class was made”, to see the CSS declaration behind it.
- **Ready to paste**: Copy the classes, a class="" attribute or a JSX className for each selector, with your project’s prefix if it uses one.

### How to convert CSS to Tailwind

1. **Paste your CSS** — Paste a rule, a whole stylesheet or a few declarations into the CSS box — or try the **Sample**.
2. **Choose the version** — Pick **Tailwind v4** or **v3**, and set a prefix or nearest-colour matching if you need them.
3. **Review** — Classes appear for each selector. Amber classes are arbitrary values; underlined ones are close, not identical.
4. **Copy** — Copy the classes, a class attribute or a JSX className and paste them into your HTML or components.

### Guide

#### Examples

| CSS | Tailwind v4 |
| --- | --- |
| `display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px` | `flex items-center gap-2` |
| `padding: 12px 24px` | `py-3 px-6` |
| `margin: 0 auto; max-width: 768px` | `my-0 mx-auto max-w-3xl` |
| `color: #1e293b; background: rgba(0,0,0,.5)` | `text-slate-800 bg-black/50` |
| `border: 1px solid #e5e7eb; border-radius: 8px` | `border border-gray-200 rounded-lg` |
| `overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap` | `truncate` |
| `.btn:hover { background: #1d4ed8 }` | `hover:bg-blue-700` |
| `@media (min-width: 768px) { .a { padding: 32px } }` | `md:p-8` |
| `padding: 13px` | `p-3.25` (v4) · `p-[13px]` (v3) |

#### Tips

Keep **@keyframes** and **@font-face** in your CSS (or in your Tailwind theme) — the converter lists them as skipped and you can use `animate-[…]` and `font-[…]` to refer to them.

In Tailwind v4, `dark:` follows the system setting unless you set up class-based dark mode. Tailwind’s preflight already makes borders solid, so `border-solid` is left out.

### FAQ

**How do I convert CSS to Tailwind?**
Paste your CSS into the box. The tool shows the Tailwind classes for each selector straight away, including hover states and breakpoints — copy them into your HTML.

**Does it support Tailwind v4?**
Yes — v4 is the default. Switch to v3 for older projects; the classes follow each version’s scales and syntax (v4 `p-4!` vs v3 `!p-4` for important, for example).

**Why are some classes like p-[13px]?**
They are arbitrary values: Tailwind has no class for exactly that value (in v3) or it’s not on any scale. They work as-is; you can also switch them to the nearest scale value by hand.

**Will hex colours become Tailwind colour names?**
When they match a Tailwind palette colour exactly — v3 hex values and v4’s colours both count — yes, e.g. #1e293b → slate-800. Turn on **Nearest colours** to use the closest palette colour for the rest.

**Does it convert media queries and :hover?**
Yes. Min-width queries at 640, 768, 1024, 1280 and 1536px become sm:, md:, lg:, xl: and 2xl:; others become min-[…]: or max-[…]:. :hover, :focus, ::before, :first-child, dark mode and more become variants.

**Is my CSS uploaded?**
No. The conversion runs entirely in your browser.

## Hash Generator

URL: https://justtools.online/developer-tools/hash-generator/
Category: Developer Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-05

Generate MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-512, SHA-3, BLAKE3, CRC32 and HMAC hashes of text or files, and verify checksums. Free, fast and private — no upload.

### At a glance

- 17 algorithms: **MD5, SHA-1, SHA-224, SHA-256, SHA-384, SHA-512, SHA3-256, SHA3-512, Keccak-256, BLAKE2b, BLAKE3, RIPEMD-160, CRC32, CRC32C, Adler-32, xxHash64** and **XXH3**.
- **Files of any size** are read in 2 MB pieces and hashed with every chosen algorithm in one pass, with progress and speed shown.
- **HMAC** with a secret key (text, hex or Base64) for API and webhook signatures, e.g. HMAC-SHA256.
- **Compare** with a hash you were given — hex, Base64, `sha256=…` or SRI format — or paste a whole **SHA256SUMS** list to check several files by name.
- **Each line** mode hashes a list one value at a time (with optional trimming and lowercasing, as ad platforms require for emails) and exports a CSV.
- Output as lowercase hex, uppercase hex or Base64; text input as UTF-8, hex or Base64 bytes.
- Runs entirely in your browser with WebAssembly — nothing you hash is uploaded. Results are checked against the published test vectors.

### Features

- **Verify downloads**: Drop an ISO, installer or APK and paste the checksum from the download page — the tool tells you instantly whether it matches.
- **Many algorithms at once**: See MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256 and SHA-512 side by side, or add SHA-3, BLAKE3 and checksums — the file is read only once.
- **Webhook signatures**: Recreate the HMAC-SHA256 of a payload with your secret to debug Razorpay, Stripe, GitHub or Shopify webhooks.
- **Hash a list**: Normalise and hash a column of emails or phone numbers line by line, then download value and hash as CSV.
- **Find the algorithm**: No match? The tool suggests which algorithms produce a hash of that length and adds them with one click.
- **Private**: Passwords, keys and files never leave your device. No upload, no sign-up and no size limit.

### How to generate a hash

1. **Choose what to hash** — Pick **Text**, **Each line** or **Files**, and select the algorithms you need.
2. **Add your data** — Type or paste text, or drop one or more files. Turn on **HMAC** and enter a key for a keyed hash.
3. **Copy the result** — Hashes appear instantly. Choose hex, HEX or Base64 and click the copy button next to any hash.
4. **Verify (optional)** — Paste the expected hash or checksum list into **Compare with a hash** to see whether it matches.

### Guide

#### Which hash should I use?

| Use | Algorithm |
| --- | --- |
| Checking a download, file integrity | SHA-256 (or whatever the publisher lists) |
| API / webhook signatures | HMAC-SHA256 |
| Ethereum addresses and signatures | Keccak-256 (not SHA3-256) |
| Fast deduplication or cache keys | BLAKE3, xxHash64 or XXH3 |
| ZIP, PNG and gzip checksums | CRC32 |
| Old systems that only accept it | MD5 or SHA-1 — never for security |
| Storing passwords | None of these — use bcrypt, scrypt or Argon2 with a salt |

#### Checking a file from the command line

To compare with what this tool shows: on Windows run `certutil -hashfile file.iso SHA256` (or `Get-FileHash file.iso` in PowerShell), on macOS `shasum -a 256 file.iso`, and on Linux `sha256sum file.iso`.

Hashing text in a terminal? `echo "hello" | sha256sum` includes a line break at the end — use `echo -n` (or `printf`) to match the tool, which hashes exactly what is in the box.

### FAQ

**How do I generate a SHA-256 hash?**
Type or paste your text into the box — the SHA-256 hash appears instantly along with MD5, SHA-1 and SHA-512. For a file, choose **Files** and drop it in.

**How do I verify a file’s checksum?**
Choose **Files**, drop the file, and paste the checksum from the download page into **Compare with a hash**. A green “Match” means the file is exactly what the publisher released.

**Why doesn’t my hash match?**
Hashes change with every byte. The usual causes are a trailing space or line break, different text encoding, uppercase vs lowercase input, or the wrong algorithm. The tool warns about trailing spaces and suggests algorithms that match the length of your hash.

**Can I reverse or decrypt a hash?**
No. Hashes are one-way: you can’t get the original text back. Sites that “decrypt” MD5 only look the hash up in tables of common passwords.

**Is MD5 still safe to use?**
Not for security — collisions can be made deliberately. It is fine for spotting accidental corruption or where a system requires it. Use SHA-256 or newer for anything security-related.

**Is there a file size limit?**
No. Files are read in small pieces, so even multi-gigabyte files work; the speed depends on your device.

**Is my data uploaded?**
No. All hashing happens in your browser with WebAssembly. Your text, files and secret keys never leave your device.

## Age Calculator

URL: https://justtools.online/calculators/age-calculator/
Category: Calculators
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-05

Calculate your exact age in years, months and days, the next birthday countdown and age on any date. Check exam age limits as on a cut-off date. Free.

### At a glance

- Gives your **exact age in years, months and days**, plus your age in total months, weeks, days, hours, minutes and seconds — live, to the second, with an optional time of birth.
- Shows your **next birthday**: the date, weekday, the age you’ll turn and a countdown, and the **day of the week you were born**.
- Calculates **age on any date** — past or future — not just today.
- **Exam age limit** mode checks your age **as on a cut-off date** (like “1 August”) against a minimum and maximum age, with OBC, SC/ST and PwBD relaxation, and shows the allowed range of birth dates.
- Upper limits can follow the UPSC/SSC wording (“must not have attained 32”) or count completed years; both are shown exactly, day by day.
- **Age difference** mode compares two dates of birth in years, months and days.
- Month lengths and leap years are handled exactly; someone born on 29 February has their birthday on 28 February in other years. Runs in your browser — your date of birth isn’t sent anywhere.

### Features

- **Exact to the day**: Counts calendar months the way birthdays work, so 31 January to 28 February is one month — no 30-day approximations.
- **Exam-ready**: Enter the “age as on” date and limits from a UPSC, SSC, banking or state exam notification and see at once whether you qualify.
- **Birthday countdown**: See how many months and days until your next birthday, the weekday it falls on and the age you’ll turn.
- **Fun milestones**: Find out when you’ll be 10,000 days old, 1,000 weeks or a billion seconds — and how many seconds old you are right now.
- **Any date**: Work out an age on a past or future date: at admission, retirement, a policy date or a wedding.
- **Private**: Calculated on your device. Your date of birth is never uploaded or stored.

### How to calculate your age

1. **Enter your date of birth** — Pick the date in the **Date of birth** box. Add your time of birth for exact hours and seconds (optional).
2. **Choose the date** — The age is worked out for today; change **Age on** to calculate it for any other date.
3. **Read the result** — See your age in years, months and days, your next birthday, and your age in months, weeks, days, hours and seconds.
4. **Check an exam limit (optional)** — Open **Exam age limit**, enter the cut-off date and the minimum and maximum age, and choose any relaxation.

### Guide

#### How exam age limits are worked out

Notifications give an age range and a date, such as “21 to 32 years as on 1 August 2026”. You must have **reached the minimum age** on that date. For the upper limit, UPSC and SSC say you **must not have attained** the maximum age — so with a limit of 32 you must still be 31 on the cut-off date.

That is why such notices list birth dates instead: for 21–32 as on 1 August 2026, a candidate must be born **not earlier than 2 August 1994 and not later than 1 August 2005**. The calculator shows this range for any limits you enter, including relaxation.

| Category | Usual upper age relaxation (central government) |
| --- | --- |
| OBC (non-creamy layer) | 3 years |
| SC / ST | 5 years |
| Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD) | 10 years (13 for OBC, 15 for SC/ST) |
| Ex-servicemen, J&K domicile and others | Varies — see the notification |

#### Good to know

Age in months and days depends on month lengths, so two people with the same number of days alive can have slightly different “years, months and days”. This calculator counts whole calendar months first, then the remaining days — the same way you count birthdays.

Planning finances by age? The [EMI calculator](https://justtools.online/calculators/emi-calculator/) shows a loan’s monthly payments, and the [BMI calculator](https://justtools.online/calculators/bmi-calculator/) uses your age to explain results for children and teens.

### FAQ

**How do I calculate my exact age?**
Enter your date of birth. The calculator counts the completed years and months since then, and the days left over — for example 26 years, 8 months and 20 days — and shows the same age in total days, weeks and hours.

**How do I calculate my age on a specific date?**
Change the **Age on** date to the date you need, such as an exam cut-off or admission date. The age is worked out for the start of that day.

**Am I eligible for an exam with an age limit “as on 1 August”?**
Open **Exam age limit**, enter your date of birth, 1 August of the exam year, and the minimum and maximum ages from the notification. Add your category’s relaxation. The calculator says whether you’re within the limit and shows the allowed birth dates. The notification is always final.

**What does “must not have attained 32 years” mean?**
You must not have had your 32nd birthday on or before the cut-off date. If you turn 32 on the cut-off date itself, you are not eligible; if you turn 32 the day after, you are.

**How is the age of someone born on 29 February calculated?**
In years without 29 February, this calculator counts the birthday on 28 February, so the person turns a year older then. Some countries use 1 March for legal purposes.

**Is my date of birth saved?**
No. Everything is calculated in your browser and nothing is sent or stored.

## SVG to PNG, JPG & WebP Converter

URL: https://justtools.online/image-tools/svg-to-png/
Category: Image Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-05

Convert SVG to PNG, JPG or WebP online at any size — 1x, 2x, 3x or exact pixels — with a transparent or coloured background. Batch convert, free, no upload.

### At a glance

- Converts SVG (and compressed .svgz) to **PNG**, **JPG** or **WebP**; you can also paste SVG code.
- Choose a **scale** (0.5×, 1×, 2×, 3×, 4×, 8× — several at once for @1x/@2x/@3x assets) or an exact **width or height** in pixels.
- The SVG is **redrawn as a vector at every size**, so a 24 px icon exported at 1024 px stays perfectly sharp.
- Background: **transparent** (PNG and WebP), white, black or any colour; JPG transparency becomes white.
- Works out the size from width/height (in px, pt, mm, cm or in) or the viewBox, and adds a viewBox when missing so scaling works.
- Warns about things browsers don’t draw in images: linked outside images, web fonts and external symbols.
- Batch convert many files and download them as a ZIP. Runs in your browser — nothing is uploaded.

### Features

- **Sharp at any size**: Not an upscale of a small picture: the vector itself is rendered at the size you pick, up to the browser’s 16-megapixel limit.
- **App and web assets**: Export @1x, @2x and @3x PNGs in one go for iOS, Android and high-DPI websites.
- **Exact pixel sizes**: Need a 512×512 icon or a 1200-pixel-wide image? Set the width or height and the other side follows the proportions.
- **Transparent or solid**: Keep transparency for logos, or put them on white, black or your brand colour.
- **Paste code**: Copied an icon’s SVG code from a design tool or icon set? Paste it and download the image.
- **Private**: Your files stay on your device. No upload, no sign-up and no watermark.

### How to convert SVG to PNG

1. **Add your SVG** — Drop one or more SVG files, or open **Or paste SVG code** and paste the code.
2. **Choose the format** — Pick **PNG**, **JPG** or **WebP** and the background.
3. **Set the size** — Tick one or more **scales**, or choose **Width** or **Height** and enter the pixels.
4. **Download** — Click a size to download it, or **Download all (ZIP)** for every image.

### Guide

#### Which format should I choose?

| Format | Transparency | Best for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PNG | Yes | Logos, icons, diagrams — exact colours and crisp edges |
| WebP | Yes | Websites — smaller files than PNG |
| JPG | No (white background) | Complex illustrations and where PNG isn’t accepted |

#### If the image looks different from the SVG

Browsers don’t load anything from outside the file when an SVG is turned into an image. Pictures linked by URL, web fonts loaded with @import and symbols from another SVG file are left out — embed them in the SVG to include them. Text uses fonts installed on your device; convert text to outlines in your design tool for an exact match.

Need smaller files afterwards? Try the [Image Compressor](https://justtools.online/image-tools/image-compressor/), or resize further with the [Image Resizer](https://justtools.online/image-tools/image-resizer/).

### FAQ

**How do I convert SVG to PNG?**
Drop the SVG file on this page, choose PNG and a size, and download. You can convert several files and sizes at once.

**How do I convert SVG to a high-resolution PNG?**
Choose a larger scale such as 4× or 8×, or set an exact width like 2048 px. Because the SVG is redrawn as a vector at that size, the PNG stays sharp.

**Will the PNG have a transparent background?**
Yes, with **Transparent** selected (the default for PNG and WebP). JPG can’t be transparent, so transparent areas become white or the colour you choose.

**Why is some text or an image missing?**
Browsers don’t load outside files when converting: linked images, web fonts and external symbols. The tool warns you when an SVG uses them. Embed images and convert text to outlines to fix it.

**What is the largest size I can export?**
Up to about 16 megapixels (for example 4000×4000), which is the most phones and browsers can draw at once. Larger sizes are scaled down to fit, and the tool tells you.

**Are my files uploaded?**
No. Everything happens in your browser, so your logos and designs never leave your device.

## PPK to PEM Converter

URL: https://justtools.online/security-tools/ppk-to-pem/
Category: Security Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-05

Convert a PuTTY .ppk private key to PEM or OpenSSH format online, with or without a passphrase. Supports PPK v2 and v3, RSA, ECDSA and Ed25519. No upload.

### At a glance

- Reads **PuTTY PPK version 2 and 3** files, including passphrase-protected ones (Argon2 for v3, as PuTTY 0.75 and later write them).
- Converts to **PEM** (BEGIN RSA / EC / DSA PRIVATE KEY), **OpenSSH** (BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY), **PKCS#8** or another **PPK** version.
- Supports **RSA, ECDSA (P-256, P-384, P-521), Ed25519** and DSA keys.
- Checks the key file’s MAC, so a wrong passphrase or a damaged file is reported instead of producing a broken key.
- Can add a new passphrase to the converted key, and shows the **SHA256 fingerprint** and public key line (for authorized_keys).
- Tested against keys made by PuTTYgen and checked with OpenSSH’s ssh-keygen and OpenSSL.
- Runs entirely in your browser — the private key is never uploaded.

### Features

- **Without PuTTYgen**: Convert on any computer or phone — no need to install PuTTY or use the command line on a Mac or Linux machine.
- **Passphrases handled**: Unlock an encrypted .ppk with its passphrase, and choose whether the new key has one.
- **Every format**: PEM for AWS and older tools, OpenSSH for modern ssh and Git, PKCS#8 for code libraries.
- **Verify before you use it**: Compare the SHA256 fingerprint with the one your server or PuTTYgen shows.
- **Public key too**: Copy the matching public key line for ~/.ssh/authorized_keys or download it as .pub.
- **Private**: Your key is converted in this browser tab and never sent anywhere.

### How to convert a PPK file to PEM

1. **Open the .ppk file** — Click **Open a key file** and choose your .ppk, or paste its text.
2. **Unlock it** — If the key has a passphrase, enter it and click **Unlock**.
3. **Choose the format** — Pick **PEM** (or **OpenSSH** / **PKCS#8**) and optionally a new passphrase.
4. **Download** — Click **Convert**, then **Download**. On macOS/Linux run `chmod 600` on the file before using it.

### Guide

#### PEM or OpenSSH — which do I need?

Ed25519 keys have no traditional PEM form, so choosing PEM gives the standard PKCS#8 “BEGIN PRIVATE KEY” format instead.

| Use | Choose |
| --- | --- |
| ssh on macOS/Linux, Git, VS Code Remote | OpenSSH (or PEM — both work) |
| AWS EC2 .pem files, older tools, Paramiko | PEM |
| Java, Node.js, Python cryptography libraries | PKCS#8 |
| An older PuTTY or WinSCP that rejects new keys | PPK v2 |

#### Using the converted key

Save it in `~/.ssh` (for example `~/.ssh/id_rsa`) and run `chmod 600 ~/.ssh/id_rsa` — ssh refuses keys that other users can read. Then connect with `ssh -i ~/.ssh/id_rsa user@server`.

Need it the other way round? Use the [PEM to PPK converter](https://justtools.online/security-tools/pem-to-ppk/).

### FAQ

**How do I convert a PPK file to PEM?**
Open the .ppk file here, enter its passphrase if it has one, choose PEM and click Convert. Download the new key — no PuTTYgen needed.

**Does it work with PuTTY’s new PPK version 3 files?**
Yes. PPK v3 (PuTTY 0.75 and later), including keys protected with Argon2 passphrases, and older v2 files are both supported.

**Is it safe to convert a private key online?**
The conversion runs in your browser and the key is never uploaded, so it’s as private as converting on your own computer. Still, use only sites you trust with keys, and delete spare copies afterwards.

**What if I forgot the passphrase?**
It can’t be recovered — the passphrase is what decrypts the key. You’ll need to create a new key pair and add its public key to your servers.

**Why does ssh say “bad permissions” or “unprotected private key”?**
The key file is readable by other users. Run `chmod 600` on it (or remove other users’ access on Windows), then try again.

**Can I convert DSA keys?**
Yes, but OpenSSH 9.8 and later no longer accept DSA (ssh-dss) keys. Create a new Ed25519 key for new servers.

## PEM to PPK Converter

URL: https://justtools.online/security-tools/pem-to-ppk/
Category: Security Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-05

Convert a PEM or OpenSSH private key (id_rsa, AWS .pem) to a PuTTY .ppk file online — PPK v3 or v2, with an optional passphrase. Free, private, no upload.

### At a glance

- Reads **OpenSSH** keys (BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY), traditional **PEM** (BEGIN RSA / EC / DSA PRIVATE KEY) and **PKCS#8**, encrypted or not.
- Unlocks passphrase-protected keys: OpenSSH’s bcrypt + AES, and PEM/PKCS#8 encrypted with AES or 3DES (as older OpenSSL and PuTTYgen exports are).
- Writes **PPK v3** (PuTTY 0.75+, WinSCP 5.19+) or **PPK v2** for older PuTTY versions, with an optional passphrase.
- Supports **RSA, ECDSA (P-256, P-384, P-521), Ed25519** and DSA keys, and keeps the key comment.
- Shows the key type, size and **SHA256 fingerprint**, and the public key line for authorized_keys.
- Output is tested against PuTTY’s format and read back by an independent PPK reader.
- Runs entirely in your browser — the private key is never uploaded.

### Features

- **AWS keys in PuTTY**: Downloaded an EC2 key pair as .pem? Convert it to .ppk to connect with PuTTY or WinSCP on Windows.
- **No PuTTYgen needed**: Works in any browser, on any computer — handy on a work laptop where you can’t install software.
- **Old and new PuTTY**: Choose PPK v3 for current PuTTY, or v2 for older PuTTY, WinSCP and tools that don’t read v3 yet.
- **Keep it protected**: Add a passphrase to the .ppk so the key is encrypted on disk.
- **Check the fingerprint**: The SHA256 fingerprint matches what ssh-keygen and PuTTYgen show, so you can confirm it’s the right key.
- **Private**: Your key is converted in this browser tab and never sent anywhere.

### How to convert a PEM file to PPK

1. **Open the key** — Click **Open a key file** and choose your .pem or id_rsa file, or paste the key text.
2. **Unlock it** — If the key has a passphrase, enter it and click **Unlock**.
3. **Choose PPK** — Pick **PPK v3** (or **PPK v2** for older PuTTY), set the comment and optionally a passphrase.
4. **Download** — Click **Convert** and **Download** the .ppk file.

### Guide

#### Using the .ppk file

**PuTTY:** Connection → SSH → Auth → Credentials → “Private key file for authentication”, then save the session.

**WinSCP:** Login → Advanced → SSH → Authentication → Private key file. **FileZilla:** Settings → Connection → SFTP → Add key file.

Going the other way? Use the [PPK to PEM converter](https://justtools.online/security-tools/ppk-to-pem/).

#### PPK v3 or v2?

|  | PPK v3 | PPK v2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Works with | PuTTY 0.75 and later, WinSCP 5.19+, current FileZilla | All PuTTY versions and older tools |
| Passphrase protection | Argon2 (much harder to crack) | Older SHA-1 based scheme |
| Choose when | Your tools are up to date | A tool says the key format is unsupported |

### FAQ

**How do I convert a PEM file to PPK?**
Open the .pem file here, enter its passphrase if it has one, choose PPK v3 and click Convert. Then download the .ppk — no PuTTYgen needed.

**Can I convert an AWS EC2 .pem key to .ppk?**
Yes. AWS key pairs download as PEM files; convert them to .ppk here and load them in PuTTY or WinSCP. Connect as the instance’s user, such as ec2-user or ubuntu.

**Does it support new OpenSSH keys (BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY)?**
Yes, including passphrase-protected ones. Unlocking takes a second or two because OpenSSH deliberately makes passphrase checks slow.

**PuTTY says “unsupported key format” — what now?**
Your PuTTY is probably older than 0.75. Convert again choosing **PPK v2**, or update PuTTY.

**Is it safe to convert a private key online?**
The conversion happens in your browser and the key is never uploaded. Use only tools you trust with private keys, and delete spare copies afterwards.

**Which key types are supported?**
RSA, ECDSA (P-256, P-384, P-521), Ed25519 and DSA. Ed448 and security-key (sk-) keys aren’t supported by PuTTY’s format here.

## QR Code Scanner

URL: https://justtools.online/qr-tools/qr-code-scanner/
Category: QR & Barcode Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-05

Scan QR codes online with your camera or from a photo or screenshot. Shows links safely, UPI payments, Wi-Fi passwords and contacts. Free, private, no app.

### At a glance

- Scans with your **camera** (phone or laptop) or from an **image or screenshot** — drop a file or paste with Ctrl+V; several codes in one image are all read.
- Shows what a code does before you act: **links** with warnings (http, IP addresses, look-alike domains, shorteners, app downloads), **UPI** payee and amount, **Wi-Fi** name and password, **contacts**, events, email, SMS and locations.
- Saves contacts (.vcf) and events (.ics), copies Wi-Fi passwords and UPI IDs, and opens links only when you click.
- Reads QR codes, Micro QR and rMQR, including inverted (light-on-dark) and rotated codes.
- Keeps a list of everything scanned this session, which you can copy or download as CSV.
- Decoding uses ZXing in WebAssembly on your device — camera frames and images are never uploaded or recorded.

### Features

- **Scan on a laptop**: Got a QR code in an email, PDF or screenshot? Paste or drop the image — no phone needed.
- **Check before you pay**: UPI codes show the payee’s name, UPI ID and amount, with a reminder that you never scan a code to receive money.
- **Safer links**: See the real website first, with warnings for unencrypted pages, shorteners, look-alike addresses and app downloads.
- **Wi-Fi in a tap**: Read the network name and password from a Wi-Fi QR code and copy the password.
- **Many codes at once**: Keep scanning to read a stack of codes, then copy them all or export a CSV.
- **Private**: Nothing is uploaded or recorded. The camera turns off when you stop or leave the page.

### How to scan a QR code online

1. **Choose the source** — Use **Camera**, or **Image or screenshot** for a picture on your device.
2. **Scan** — Click **Start camera** and allow access, then hold the code inside the frame — or drop/paste the image.
3. **Check what it contains** — Read the link, payment or details shown, including any warnings.
4. **Use it** — Open the link, copy the text, save the contact or event — only when you choose.

### Guide

#### Staying safe with QR codes

A QR code is just text, so anyone can print one — scammers stick fake codes over real ones on parking meters, posters and shop counters. Always check the website address before entering passwords or card details, and be careful with links from shorteners or bare IP addresses.

For **UPI** payments, check that the name your UPI app shows matches who you want to pay. You never need to scan a QR code or enter your UPI PIN to **receive** money — that’s a common fraud.

#### If a code won’t scan

Move closer so the code fills most of the frame, hold steady, and add light — on phones, tap **Light** for the torch. For images, use a sharp, straight photo or a screenshot rather than a photo of a screen.

Need to make a code instead? Use the [QR Code Generator](https://justtools.online/qr-tools/qr-code-generator/). For product barcodes, use the [Barcode Scanner](https://justtools.online/qr-tools/barcode-scanner/).

### FAQ

**How do I scan a QR code on my laptop?**
Open this page, click **Start camera** and hold the code up to your webcam — or take a screenshot of the code and paste it with Ctrl+V.

**Can I scan a QR code from an image or screenshot?**
Yes. Choose **Image or screenshot**, then drop the file or paste it. Every code in the image is read.

**Is it safe to scan unknown QR codes?**
Scanning here is safe — nothing opens until you click. The scanner shows the real destination and warns about common tricks, but always check the address before entering passwords or paying.

**Why isn’t the camera working?**
Your browser may have blocked camera access for this site — allow it in the site settings — or another app may be using the camera. You can always scan a photo instead.

**Are the camera images saved or uploaded?**
No. Frames are decoded on your device and discarded immediately; nothing is recorded or sent anywhere.

**Does it read UPI and Wi-Fi QR codes?**
Yes. UPI codes show the payee, UPI ID and amount; Wi-Fi codes show the network name, security type and password.

## Barcode Scanner

URL: https://justtools.online/qr-tools/barcode-scanner/
Category: QR & Barcode Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-05

Scan barcodes online with your camera or from a photo: EAN-13, UPC, Code 128, Code 39, ISBN, DataMatrix and PDF417. Batch scan to CSV. Free, no app needed.

### At a glance

- Reads **1D barcodes** — EAN-13, EAN-8, UPC-A, UPC-E, ISBN, Code 128, Code 39, Code 93, Codabar, ITF and GS1 DataBar — and **2D codes**: DataMatrix, PDF417, Aztec, MaxiCode and QR.
- Scans with your **camera** or from an **image or screenshot** (drop or paste); several barcodes in one picture are all read.
- For product codes, checks the **check digit**, converts UPC-E ↔ UPC-A and ISBN-13 → ISBN-10, and names the **GS1 prefix** (e.g. 890 = GS1 India).
- Decodes **GS1 data** in DataMatrix and Code 128 labels — GTIN, batch, expiry date, serial number, weight — as found on medicines and shipping cartons.
- **Keep scanning** mode reads item after item, counts repeats and exports a **CSV** for stock-taking.
- Decoding uses ZXing in WebAssembly on your device — nothing is uploaded or recorded.

### Features

- **Stock-taking**: Scan shelf after shelf with Keep scanning on; repeats are counted, and the list downloads as CSV for Excel.
- **Check a product code**: See whether the check digit is right and which GS1 office issued the number — and look the product up.
- **Medicine and logistics labels**: Read GS1 DataMatrix codes on medicine packs to see the GTIN, batch number and expiry date.
- **Books**: Scan a book’s barcode for its ISBN-13 and ISBN-10 and find it on Open Library.
- **From photos**: No camera handy? Drop a photo or paste a screenshot of the barcode.
- **Private**: Nothing is uploaded or recorded. The camera turns off when you stop or leave the page.

### How to scan a barcode online

1. **Pick the codes** — Leave **All codes**, or choose **Products (EAN/UPC)** for faster scanning of retail barcodes.
2. **Scan** — Click **Start camera**, allow access and hold the barcode across the frame — or switch to **Image or screenshot**.
3. **Read the result** — See the number, type, check-digit result and any product or GS1 details.
4. **Scan more** — Turn on **Keep scanning** to scan item after item, then download the list as CSV.

### Guide

#### What the GS1 prefix tells you

The first digits of an EAN-13 show which national GS1 office gave the company its barcode numbers — 890 for GS1 India, 400–440 for Germany, 690–699 for China. They **don’t** prove where the product was made: a company registered in India can make goods anywhere, and vice versa.

Codes starting with 20–29 are shops’ own numbers (loose produce, weighed items), and 978/979 are books.

#### Tips for a quick scan

Hold the barcode across the frame, not too close, so the lines are sharp; add light or tap **Light** on phones. Shiny or curved packs scan better at a slight angle.

Need to print barcodes? Use the [Barcode Generator](https://justtools.online/qr-tools/barcode-generator/). For QR codes, the [QR Code Scanner](https://justtools.online/qr-tools/qr-code-scanner/) shows links and payments in detail.

### FAQ

**How do I scan a barcode online?**
Click **Start camera**, allow camera access and hold the barcode in the frame. Or choose **Image or screenshot** and drop a picture of it.

**Which barcode types can it read?**
EAN-13, EAN-8, UPC-A, UPC-E, ISBN, Code 128, Code 39, Code 93, Codabar, ITF, GS1 DataBar, DataMatrix, PDF417, Aztec, MaxiCode and QR codes.

**Can I scan many barcodes and export them to Excel?**
Yes. Turn on **Keep scanning**, scan each item, then click **CSV**. Scanning the same barcode again increases its count.

**Does 890 at the start mean “Made in India”?**
No. It means the company got its barcode numbers from GS1 India. The country of manufacture is printed separately on the pack.

**Can it read the barcode on medicine strips?**
Yes — GS1 DataMatrix codes on medicines are decoded into the product number (GTIN), batch, expiry date and serial number.

**Is anything uploaded?**
No. Barcodes are decoded on your device; camera frames and images are never stored or sent anywhere.

#### Is the wheel really random?

Yes. The winner is chosen with your browser’s cryptographically secure random number generator, using a method that gives every name exactly the same chance; the wheel then spins to that name. Animation speed or where you click makes no difference.

Hundreds. With very many names the labels get small, but the pick works the same; use full screen for the clearest view.

## CSV to Interactive Chart

URL: https://justtools.online/developer-tools/csv-to-chart/

Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.

Turn CSV or Excel data into an interactive bar, line, area, pie or scatter chart online. Group and sum rows, hover for values, download PNG or SVG. No upload.

- Reads CSV, TSV and cells copied from **Excel or Google Sheets**, and detects number, date and text columns automatically.

- **Straight from a spreadsheet**: Copy a range in Excel or Google Sheets and paste it — tab-separated cells work just like CSV.

- **Indian number formats**: Lakh-style grouping (1,23,456), rupee signs and percentages are read as numbers, not text.

### How to make a chart from a CSV file
