2. **Pick the columns** — Choose the **Categories / X axis** column and the **Values to plot**.
3. **Shape the chart** — Choose a chart type; combine repeated rows, sort, or show the top few categories.
4. **Download** — Add a title if you like and download the chart as **PNG** or **SVG**.

### Guide

#### Which chart should I use?

| To show | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Change over time (months, years, dates) | Line or area |
| Comparing categories (regions, products) | Column, or bar for long names |
| Parts of a whole (share of sales) | Pie or donut — up to about 8 slices |
| The relationship between two numbers | Scatter |
| Totals and how they’re made up | Stacked column or area |

#### Tips

Long lists of categories are hard to read: use **Top 10 + Other**, or a bar chart, which has room for long names. If a column of numbers is treated as text, check for notes or units mixed into the cells.

Need the data in another shape first? The [CSV to JSON converter](https://justtools.online/developer-tools/csv-to-json/) and [JSON to CSV converter](https://justtools.online/developer-tools/json-to-csv/) help.

### FAQ

**How do I make a graph from a CSV file?**
Paste the CSV or open the file, choose which column goes along the axis and which numbers to plot, and pick a chart type. The chart appears instantly and can be downloaded as PNG or SVG.

**Can I paste data from Excel?**
Yes. Select the cells in Excel or Google Sheets, copy, and paste them into the data box — the columns are detected automatically.

**How do I total rows for the same category?**
Set **Combine rows** to Sum (or Average, Count, Min or Max). Rows with the same category are merged into one bar or slice.

**Why is my number column not available?**
At least 80% of a column’s cells must be numbers. Remove units or notes typed into the cells (like “approx.”), or use Count rows to chart how often each value appears.

**Can I download the chart?**
Yes, as a high-resolution PNG for documents and slides, or as an SVG that stays sharp at any size. The charted numbers download as CSV too.

**Is my data uploaded?**
No. The chart is made in your browser, so sales figures, survey results and other data never leave your device.

## Website SEO Checker

URL: https://justtools.online/seo-tools/website-seo-checker/
Category: SEO & Marketing Tools
Processing: Contacts an external service to work (see the page).
Last updated: 2026-10-06

Free website SEO checker: audit any page’s title, meta description, headings, canonical, robots.txt, schema, Open Graph and AI crawler access, with fixes.

### At a glance

- Runs **35+ on-page SEO checks** in nine areas — search appearance, crawling and indexing, content, images, links, social sharing, structured data, mobile and technical, and AI search visibility — and scores the page out of 100.
- Checks the **title and meta description** against what Google and Bing show (about 600 px for a title, 50–160 characters for a description) and previews the Google result and the WhatsApp or Facebook link preview.
- Reads **robots.txt** the way Googlebot does (RFC 9309 longest-match rules) and shows which search engines and **AI crawlers** — OAI-SearchBot, GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended and more — may crawl the page.
- Finds **noindex**, canonical and hreflang mistakes, mixed content, render-blocking scripts, images without alt text or size, empty or vague link text, and invalid or incomplete **JSON-LD structured data**.
- Spots pages whose text only appears after **JavaScript** runs — blank to most AI crawlers — and can render React, Vue or Angular pages first.
- Puts the most important problems first, gives each one a fix, and exports the report as **Markdown** for a developer or client.
- Your browser fetches the page itself when the site allows it; otherwise only the address is sent to **Jina Reader**, which fetches it. Pasted HTML never leaves your device.

### Features

- **Score with priorities**: One score out of 100, a score for each area, and a “Fix these first” list ordered by impact.
- **Search and link previews**: See your Google result and your WhatsApp, Facebook and LinkedIn preview before you publish, with the title width in pixels.
- **AI search visibility**: Check whether ChatGPT search, Claude, Perplexity and Gemini crawlers may read the page, and whether snippet rules stop AI answers from quoting it.
- **robots.txt like Googlebot**: The same rules search engines use: the most specific user-agent group, the longest matching path, Allow winning ties.
- **Structured data check**: Finds JSON-LD syntax errors and lists the properties Google needs for rich results such as Product, Article, Breadcrumb and Event.
- **Any page, even private ones**: Check live pages by address, or paste the HTML of pages behind a login, on localhost or protected from bots.

### How to check a website’s SEO

1. **Enter the page address** — Type or paste the URL of any page, such as **example.com/blog/post**. For sites built with React or Vue, switch on **Run JavaScript first**.
2. **Run the check** — Click **Check SEO**. The page, its robots.txt and llms.txt are fetched and analysed in a few seconds.
3. **Fix the top issues** — Start with **Fix these first**: problems are ordered by impact, each with a plain-English fix.
4. **Check again and share** — After fixing, click **Check again**. Copy the report as Markdown for your developer or client, or share the result link.

### Guide

#### What the SEO checker looks at

| Area | What is checked | Why it matters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Search appearance | Title, meta description, favicon | They make up your result in Google and Bing, and decide whether people click. |
| Crawling & indexing | HTTP status, robots meta tag, robots.txt, sitemap, canonical, HTTPS, URL, hreflang | A single noindex or Disallow keeps the page out of search results entirely. |
| Content | H1, heading order, word count, the page’s most used words | Search engines and AI answers need enough clear, on-topic text. |
| Images | Alt text, width and height, file formats, lazy loading | Alt text ranks images; missing sizes make the page jump as it loads. |
| Links | Internal links, link text, nofollow, links crawlers can’t follow | Links are how crawlers discover pages and learn what they are about. |
| Social sharing | Open Graph and X (Twitter) card tags | Without og:image, links shared on WhatsApp and Facebook show no picture. |
| Structured data | JSON-LD syntax, schema types, required properties | Makes the page eligible for rich results and easier for AI to understand. |
| Mobile & technical | Viewport, language, encoding, doctype, HTML size, render-blocking scripts, mixed content | Google indexes the mobile version, and slow or broken pages rank lower. |
| AI search visibility | AI crawler access, snippet controls, JavaScript-only content, llms.txt | Decides whether ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and AI Overviews can cite you. |

#### How the score works

Every check has a weight by how much it affects search: the title, meta description and H1 count most, a missing X card least. A passed check earns its full weight, a warning half, a failure nothing; notes marked with an “i” are advice and don’t count. Each area gets its own score, so you can see at a glance whether the trouble is content, indexing or technical.

**If search engines can’t index the page at all** — an error status, a noindex tag or a robots.txt block — the score is capped at 30, because nothing else matters until that is fixed. A high score means the page is technically ready to rank; how well it ranks still depends on the quality of the content, links from other sites and the competition.

#### SEO for AI search (GEO)

ChatGPT search, Claude, Perplexity and Google’s AI Overviews answer questions by reading web pages and citing them. To be one of those sources, a page has to be **crawlable by their bots** (OAI-SearchBot, Claude-SearchBot, PerplexityBot, and Googlebot for AI Overviews), **quotable** (no nosnippet or tiny max-snippet), and **readable without JavaScript**, because most AI crawlers don’t run it.

Blocking training crawlers such as GPTBot, ClaudeBot, CCBot or Google-Extended is a separate choice: it keeps your content out of model training but doesn’t remove you from search or from AI answers. The checker lists both kinds separately so you can decide. Clear headings, direct answers, FAQs and structured data help AI tools understand and quote a page; llms.txt is an optional extra that Google doesn’t use.

### FAQ

**Is the Website SEO Checker free?**
Yes — free, with no sign-up and no daily limit. The page-fetching service allows about 20 checks a minute from one network, which is plenty for normal use.

**What is sent when I check a page?**
Only the page address. Your browser first requests the page directly; if the site doesn’t allow that, the address is sent to Jina Reader (r.jina.ai), which fetches the page, robots.txt and llms.txt for you. We don’t store the addresses you check. Pasted HTML is analysed in your browser and never sent anywhere.

**How long should a title tag and meta description be?**
Keep titles to about 50–60 characters — Google cuts them at roughly 600 pixels — and meta descriptions to 120–160 characters. Bing Webmaster Tools reports descriptions shorter than about 25 or longer than 160 characters as an error.

**My page scores 100. Why doesn’t it rank?**
The checker covers on-page and technical SEO — what you control on the page. Rankings also depend on how useful the content is compared with competing pages, links from other websites, and real-user page speed. Use [Google Search Console](https://search.google.com/search-console) to see the searches you appear for.

**Should I block GPTBot and other AI crawlers?**
It depends on what you want. Blocking training crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, CCBot, Google-Extended) keeps your content out of AI training without hurting search. Blocking AI search crawlers (OAI-SearchBot, Claude-SearchBot, PerplexityBot) means those assistants can’t cite or link to you.

**Why can’t the checker fetch my page?**
Some sites block automated requests with Cloudflare or similar bot protection, and pages behind a login or on localhost aren’t reachable from outside. Open the page, press Ctrl+U to view its source, copy everything and use **Paste HTML** instead.

**Does it check page speed and Core Web Vitals?**
It flags the common causes it can see in the HTML — render-blocking scripts, images without width and height, very large pages and missing lazy loading. For measured loading times use Google PageSpeed Insights.

**Does it work for single-page apps built with React, Vue or Angular?**
Yes. By default it checks the HTML your server sends, which is what most AI crawlers see; if the page is an empty app shell it says so. Switch on **Run JavaScript first** to check the page as it looks after rendering, the way Google sees it.

## IP Subnet Calculator

URL: https://justtools.online/network-tools/ip-subnet-calculator/
Category: Internet & Network Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-06

Free IP subnet calculator for IPv4 and IPv6: network, broadcast, host range, mask and wildcard from any CIDR, plus subnetting, VLSM and route summarisation.

### At a glance

- Works out the **network address, broadcast address, first and last usable host**, total and usable addresses, **subnet mask, wildcard mask** and binary form of any IPv4 or IPv6 block.
- Accepts CIDR (192.168.1.10/24), an address with a mask (10.0.0.1 255.255.240.0), a Cisco wildcard mask, or IPv6 in any notation, and writes IPv6 the RFC 5952 way.
- Names the address type — **private (RFC 1918), CGNAT (100.64.0.0/10)**, loopback, link-local, multicast, documentation, unique local or global unicast — and the classful class.
- **Splits** a network into equal subnets by count, hosts or prefix, plans **VLSM** (largest subnet first) and **summarises** lists of networks or ranges into the fewest CIDR blocks.
- Handles the edge cases exams ask about: /31 point-to-point links (RFC 3021), /32 hosts, /0, and IPv6 counts too big for ordinary numbers.
- Gives the reverse DNS zone (in-addr.arpa / ip6.arpa), checks whether an address is inside the network, and exports subnet tables as CSV. Everything is calculated in your browser.

### Features

- **Every subnet value**: Network, broadcast, host range, mask, wildcard, hex, binary and reverse DNS — copy them all in one click.
- **IPv4 and IPv6**: One calculator for both, with BigInt maths so even a /32 IPv6 allocation is counted exactly.
- **Subnetting made easy**: Split a network by the number of subnets or hosts you need, and see every resulting subnet in a table.
- **VLSM planner**: List your LANs and how many devices each has; get the smallest fitting subnet for each, with room to grow shown.
- **Route summarisation**: Merge networks, single addresses and ranges into the fewest CIDR blocks, or find the one supernet that covers them.
- **Exam-ready**: Binary view with network bits highlighted, class and the /31 and /32 rules — handy for CCNA and university networking.

### How to calculate a subnet

1. **Enter an address** — Type an IP with its prefix, such as **192.168.1.10/24**, or pick the subnet mask from the list.
2. **Read the results** — See the **network address**, **broadcast address**, usable host range and number of hosts instantly.
3. **Split or plan** — Switch to **Split network** to divide it into subnets, or **VLSM** to size subnets for each LAN.
4. **Export** — Copy the details or download the subnet table as CSV for your documentation.

### Guide

#### IPv4 subnet mask cheat sheet

| Prefix | Subnet mask | Wildcard | Addresses | Usable hosts |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| /8 | 255.0.0.0 | 0.255.255.255 | 16,777,216 | 16,777,214 |
| /16 | 255.255.0.0 | 0.0.255.255 | 65,536 | 65,534 |
| /20 | 255.255.240.0 | 0.0.15.255 | 4,096 | 4,094 |
| /21 | 255.255.248.0 | 0.0.7.255 | 2,048 | 2,046 |
| /22 | 255.255.252.0 | 0.0.3.255 | 1,024 | 1,022 |
| /23 | 255.255.254.0 | 0.0.1.255 | 512 | 510 |
| /24 | 255.255.255.0 | 0.0.0.255 | 256 | 254 |
| /25 | 255.255.255.128 | 0.0.0.127 | 128 | 126 |
| /26 | 255.255.255.192 | 0.0.0.63 | 64 | 62 |
| /27 | 255.255.255.224 | 0.0.0.31 | 32 | 30 |
| /28 | 255.255.255.240 | 0.0.0.15 | 16 | 14 |
| /29 | 255.255.255.248 | 0.0.0.7 | 8 | 6 |
| /30 | 255.255.255.252 | 0.0.0.3 | 4 | 2 |
| /31 | 255.255.255.254 | 0.0.0.1 | 2 | 2 (point-to-point) |
| /32 | 255.255.255.255 | 0.0.0.0 | 1 | 1 (single host) |

#### Private and special IPv4 ranges

| Range | Use |
| --- | --- |
| 10.0.0.0/8 | Private network (RFC 1918) — large companies and data centres |
| 172.16.0.0/12 | Private network (RFC 1918) — 172.16.0.0 to 172.31.255.255 |
| 192.168.0.0/16 | Private network (RFC 1918) — home and office routers |
| 100.64.0.0/10 | Carrier-grade NAT — ISPs, especially mobile data, share public IPs |
| 169.254.0.0/16 | Link-local — self-assigned when DHCP fails |
| 127.0.0.0/8 | Loopback — the computer itself (localhost) |

#### How subnetting works

An IPv4 address has 32 bits. The prefix length — the number after the slash — says how many of them identify the network; the rest number the hosts inside it. A /24 leaves 8 host bits, so 2⁸ = 256 addresses. The first is the **network address** and the last the **broadcast address**, so 254 are usable for devices.

Every extra prefix bit halves the block: a /24 splits into two /25s, four /26s or eight /27s. **VLSM** (variable-length subnet masking) uses different sizes inside one network — a /25 for 100 office PCs, a /30 for a router link — to avoid wasting addresses. IPv6 LANs simply use /64 each; sites usually get a /48 or /56.

### FAQ

**How many usable hosts does a /24 have?**
254. A /24 has 256 addresses, but the first (network) and last (broadcast) can’t be given to devices. In general, usable hosts = 2^(32 − prefix) − 2, except /31 and /32.

**What is a wildcard mask?**
The inverse of the subnet mask: 0 bits must match and 1 bits can be anything. For 255.255.255.0 it is 0.0.0.255. Cisco access lists and OSPF network statements use wildcard masks.

**How do I find the network and broadcast address?**
The network address is the IP with all host bits set to 0 (a bitwise AND with the mask); the broadcast address has all host bits set to 1. For 192.168.1.10/24 they are 192.168.1.0 and 192.168.1.255.

**Can a /31 be used?**
Yes, on point-to-point links between two routers. RFC 3021 lets both addresses be used because a link with two ends needs no broadcast address.

**What subnet size should I use for an IPv6 LAN?**
A /64. Stateless address autoconfiguration (SLAAC) needs it, and a /64 still holds 18 quintillion addresses. Give each site a /48 or /56 to split into /64s.

**What is VLSM?**
Variable-length subnet masking: dividing one network into subnets of different sizes to match each LAN’s needs. Allocate the largest subnet first so every block stays aligned — the VLSM tab does this for you.

## Internet Speed Test

URL: https://justtools.online/network-tools/internet-speed-test/
Category: Internet & Network Tools
Processing: Contacts an external service to work (see the page).
Last updated: 2026-10-06

Free internet speed test: check download and upload speed, ping, jitter and bufferbloat on Wi-Fi, broadband or mobile data — no app, with a data saver mode.

### At a glance

- Measures **download and upload speed** in Mbps, **ping** (latency) and **jitter**, plus **loaded latency** — how much ping rises while the line is busy (bufferbloat).
- Tests against **Cloudflare’s global network** (speed.cloudflare.com), usually from a data centre in or near your city; the page shows which one.
- Leaves out connection set-up and server processing time, and reports the 90th-percentile speed of many transfers — the line’s real capacity rather than its slow start.
- File sizes grow only while transfers stay quick, and **Data saver** caps a run at about 39 MB for mobile data.
- Rates the connection for 4K streaming, video calls, online gaming, browsing and uploads, and shows which data centre answered, your country and your IP address.
- Keeps your last 20 results in this browser only. No app or account is needed, and JustTools never sees your results.

### Features

- **All the numbers that matter**: Download, upload, ping, jitter and loaded latency — not just one big number.
- **Live gauge**: Watch the speed as it is measured, from a quick ping to the full download and upload runs.
- **Bufferbloat grade**: See whether calls and games will lag while someone else downloads, graded A+ to F.
- **Mobile-data friendly**: Data saver mode keeps a test under about 39 MB, and you can stop at any moment.
- **What it’s good for**: Plain ratings for streaming, video calls, gaming, browsing and uploading files.
- **Your history**: Compare Wi-Fi with cable, or morning with evening — recent results stay in your browser.

### How to test your internet speed

1. **Close heavy apps** — Pause downloads, streaming and cloud backups on all devices so they don’t share the line during the test.
2. **Press Start** — Choose **Full test**, or **Data saver** on mobile data, and press **Start**. Ping is measured first.
3. **Wait for both runs** — Download and then upload are measured, which takes 15–30 seconds on most connections.
4. **Read the results** — Compare download and upload with your plan, check the ratings, and copy the results to share with your provider.

### Guide

#### What the results mean

| Result | What it measures | Good value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Download | How fast data reaches you — streaming, browsing, downloads | 25 Mbps+ for 4K; 100 Mbps+ for busy homes |
| Upload | How fast you send data — video calls, uploads, cloud backup | 5 Mbps+ for HD calls; 20 Mbps+ for creators |
| Ping | Round-trip time to the server, in milliseconds | Under 30 ms great, under 100 ms fine |
| Jitter | How much ping varies from one moment to the next | Under 10 ms for gaming, under 30 ms for calls |
| Loaded latency | Ping while the line is busy downloading or uploading | Within 30 ms of the idle ping (grade A) |

#### Why your speed may be lower than your plan

- **Wi-Fi**: walls, distance and older routers or phones cut speed. Test with a cable, or close to the router on 5 GHz, to see what the line delivers.
- **Other devices**: TVs, updates and backups on the same connection share the bandwidth during the test.
- **Peak hours**: evenings are busiest, especially on mobile networks and shared fibre.
- **VPNs and proxies** add distance and encryption overhead.
- **Very fast plans**: above roughly 1 Gbps, the browser and device can become the limit rather than the line.

### FAQ

**How accurate is this speed test?**
It uses the same method as Cloudflare’s own test: precise browser timings, server time removed, and the 90th-percentile speed of many transfers. Results from different test sites differ a little because they use different servers and methods.

**How much data does a speed test use?**
It depends on your speed: a full test uses up to a few hundred MB on a very fast line, less on slower ones. Data saver mode uses at most about 39 MB — the page shows the exact amount after each test.

**What is a good ping for gaming?**
Under 30 ms is excellent and under 60 ms is good for most online games; jitter should stay below about 10–20 ms. Above 100 ms you will notice lag in fast-paced games.

**What is the difference between Mbps and MB/s?**
Speeds are quoted in megabits per second (Mbps); file sizes in megabytes. One byte is 8 bits, so 100 Mbps downloads about 12.5 MB per second.

**Is the speed test private?**
The test connects your browser to Cloudflare’s speed test servers, which see your IP address like any website does. JustTools doesn’t receive or store your results; your history stays in your browser.

**Why is upload slower than download?**
Most home and mobile plans are asymmetric — designed to receive more than they send. Fibre plans are often symmetric, so similar upload and download speeds are normal there.

## JWT Debugger

URL: https://justtools.online/developer-tools/jwt-debugger/
Category: Developer Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-06

Decode any JWT and verify its signature in your browser: header, claims and expiry explained; HS256, RS256, ES256 and EdDSA with PEM or JWK keys. No upload.

### At a glance

- Decodes the **header and payload** of any JWT, explains standard and common claims (iss, sub, aud, exp, nbf, iat, scope, roles …) and shows times in UTC and your local time.
- Shows whether the token is **expired, not yet valid or still valid**, with a live countdown.
- **Verifies the signature** for HS256/384/512, RS256/384/512, PS256/384/512, ES256/384/512 and EdDSA (Ed25519) using your browser’s Web Crypto.
- Accepts keys as a shared secret (text, Base64, Base64URL or hex), **PEM** public or private keys, PKCS#1, X.509 certificates, a **JWK** or a whole **JWKS**, picking the key by kid.
- Warns about real security problems: alg “none”, keys or key URLs supplied by the token itself (jwk, jku, x5u), missing expiry, weak or well-known secrets and secrets placed in the payload.
- Runs entirely in your browser — tokens and keys are never uploaded or logged — and also decodes the header of encrypted JWE tokens.

### Features

- **Claims in plain English**: Every claim labelled — issuer, audience, scopes, roles — with dates converted and the time left until expiry.
- **Real signature check**: Verifies with Web Crypto, the same cryptography your browser uses for HTTPS, for every common JWS algorithm.
- **Any key format**: Secrets, PEM, PKCS#1, certificates, JWK or a JWKS from your identity provider — no conversion needed.
- **Security warnings**: Flags unsigned tokens, embedded keys, long lifetimes and weak secrets before they cause trouble.
- **Private by design**: Nothing leaves your device, so production tokens are safe to inspect.
- **Build tokens too**: Switch to Encode & sign to create a test token, then verify it here in one click.

### How to decode and verify a JWT

1. **Paste the token** — Paste the JWT — a “Bearer …” header value works too. The header, payload and claims appear instantly.
2. **Check the claims** — Read who issued the token, who it’s for and when it **expires**; warnings appear above the claims.
3. **Add the key** — Enter the **secret** for HS256, or paste the **public key**, certificate or JWKS for RS256, ES256 and EdDSA.
4. **Read the result** — “Signature verified” means the token is authentic and unchanged; otherwise check the key or the token.

### Guide

#### Anatomy of a JWT

| Part | Contains | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Header | The signing algorithm and token type, Base64URL-encoded JSON | {"alg":"RS256","typ":"JWT","kid":"key-1"} |
| Payload | The claims: who the token is about, for whom, and how long it lasts | {"sub":"42","aud":"api","exp":1767229200} |
| Signature | Proof that header and payload came from the key holder unchanged | Base64URL bytes of an HMAC, RSA, ECDSA or EdDSA signature |

#### Decoding is not verifying

Anyone can decode a JWT — the header and payload are only Base64URL-encoded, not encrypted. That is why tokens must never carry passwords or other secrets. **Verifying** checks the signature with the right key, which proves who created the token and that nobody changed a single character.

A server should verify the signature, then check **exp**, **nbf**, **iss** and **aud**, and accept only the algorithms it expects. Never trust the alg value or a key that arrives inside the token itself. Public keys for providers such as Auth0, Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Cognito and Firebase are published at a JWKS URL, usually ending in /.well-known/jwks.json.

### FAQ

**Is it safe to paste a production token here?**
Yes — decoding and verification run in your browser and nothing is sent to a server. Still, treat tokens like passwords: anyone holding a valid token can use it until it expires.

**Why does it say “Invalid signature”?**
The key doesn’t match the token, or the token was changed. Common causes: the wrong environment’s secret, a secret stored as Base64 but entered as text (switch the encoding), or a JWKS key with a different kid.

**Where do I find the public key to verify RS256 tokens?**
Identity providers publish them as a JWK set, usually at https://your-issuer/.well-known/jwks.json (OpenID Connect discovery lists the exact URL). Paste the whole JWKS — the key matching the token’s kid is used.

**Can it decrypt JWE tokens?**
No. Encrypted tokens (five parts) can only be read with the recipient’s private key; the debugger shows their header and says so.

**Why are exp and iat such large numbers?**
JWT times are seconds since 1 January 1970 UTC (Unix time). The debugger converts them to dates. Values in milliseconds are a common bug and are flagged.

## JWT Encoder

URL: https://justtools.online/developer-tools/jwt-encoder/
Category: Developer Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-06

Create and sign JWTs in your browser with HS256, RS256, PS256, ES256 or EdDSA: edit claims, set expiry, generate keys and a JWKS. Keys never leave your device.

### At a glance

- Signs JWTs with **HS256/384/512, RS256/384/512, PS256/384/512, ES256/384/512 and EdDSA (Ed25519)** using your browser’s Web Crypto API.
- Edits the header and payload as JSON, pointing to the line and column of any mistake; **alg** is kept in step with the algorithm you pick.
- Adds **iat, exp** (15 minutes to 30 days), **nbf** and a random **jti** in one click.
- Generates a **secure random secret** of the right length, or an RSA, EC or Ed25519 **key pair** with the public key as PEM, JWK and JWKS (kid = RFC 7638 thumbprint).
- Signs with keys in PEM (PKCS#8, PKCS#1 or SEC1) or JWK form, and warns when an HMAC secret is too short or a well-known example.
- One click opens the new token in the JWT Debugger to verify it. Everything runs locally; keys never leave your device.

### Features

- **Every JWS algorithm**: HMAC, RSA, RSA-PSS, ECDSA and EdDSA — tokens your backend libraries accept.
- **Claim shortcuts**: Issued-at, expiry, not-before and a unique ID added with one click, in seconds since 1970 as the standard requires.
- **Key generator**: Fresh 2048-bit RSA, P-256/384/521 or Ed25519 key pairs, with the public JWK and JWKS ready for your config.
- **Strong secrets**: Random HMAC secrets of the full hash length, so tokens can’t be cracked offline.
- **Verify instantly**: Send the token and key to the debugger to check the signature and claims.
- **Local only**: No server signs anything — safe for test keys, and nothing is logged.

### How to create a JWT

1. **Pick the algorithm** — Choose **HS256** for a shared secret, or **RS256**, **ES256** or **EdDSA** for a key pair.
2. **Write the claims** — Edit the payload JSON and use the buttons to add **iat** and an **exp** such as 1 hour.
3. **Add a key** — Paste your secret or private key, or click **Generate** for a new one.
4. **Copy the token** — The signed token updates as you type. Copy it, or open it in the debugger to verify.

### Guide

#### Which algorithm should I use?

| Algorithm | Key | Use it when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HS256 | One shared secret (32+ random bytes) | The same service creates and checks the tokens |
| RS256 | RSA key pair (2048-bit or more) | Others verify with your public key — the most widely supported choice |
| PS256 | RSA key pair | You want RSA with the more modern PSS padding |
| ES256 | EC P-256 key pair | Small, fast signatures with public-key verification |
| EdDSA | Ed25519 key pair | Modern, fast and hard to misuse, where your libraries support it |

#### Good practice for tokens

- Keep access tokens short-lived — minutes to an hour — and use refresh tokens for longer sessions.
- Always set **iss**, **aud** and **exp**, and have servers check them along with the signature.
- Put only what the receiver needs in the payload: it is readable by anyone who holds the token.
- Use a random secret at least as long as the hash (32 bytes for HS256) and never commit it to source control.

### FAQ

**Is it safe to sign tokens with my real keys here?**
Signing happens entirely in your browser and nothing is sent or stored. For production keys, the safest habit is still to sign on your own servers; this tool is ideal for test and development tokens.

**How long should a JWT secret be?**
At least as long as the hash: 32 random bytes for HS256, 48 for HS384 and 64 for HS512 (RFC 7518). “Generate secret” creates one of the right length.

**What format should the private key be in?**
PEM is easiest: “BEGIN PRIVATE KEY” (PKCS#8), “BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY” or “BEGIN EC PRIVATE KEY” all work, as does a private JWK. Passphrase-protected keys must be decrypted first.

**Why is exp a number like 1767229200?**
JWT dates are seconds since 1 January 1970 UTC. The expiry buttons calculate it for you from the current time.

**Can I create a token without a signature?**
No. Unsigned tokens (alg “none”) can be forged by anyone, and secure libraries reject them, so this tool always signs.

#### Tips for printing and using OMR sheets

- Use **red drop-out ink** if you will scan sheets with an OMR scanner that ignores red, or black for photocopying.
- Ask students to use a **black or blue ballpoint pen** and to fill each circle completely — the instructions box shows how.

### FAQ

**Is the OMR sheet generator free?**
Yes. Make, download and print as many sheets as you like, with no sign-up and no limit.

**Can I make an OMR sheet for 200 questions?**
Yes — up to 300. About 220 four-option questions fit on one A4 page with every field switched on, or 200 five-option questions if you turn off the instructions box. Longer sheets continue on a second page with a short header.

**Can these sheets be checked by a scanner or app?**
They follow the usual OMR layout with corner alignment marks, which many mobile OMR apps can read after you set up the template. Commercial OMR scanners need sheets printed to their own specifications, so test a few first.

**How do I add an answer key?**
Type the answers in the Answer key box — one letter per question (ABCDA…), or entries like “1-A, 2-C, 3-BD” for several correct options. A page with filled bubbles is added to the PDF.

**Can I write the exam title in Hindi?**
Not yet: the PDF uses the standard Helvetica font, which only covers Latin letters, so Hindi text is left out. Use English titles, or write the title by hand on the printed sheet.

## Sitemap Generator

URL: https://justtools.online/seo-tools/sitemap-generator/
Category: SEO & Marketing Tools
Processing: Contacts an external service to work (see the page).
Last updated: 2026-10-06

Free XML sitemap generator: crawl your site or paste URLs, skip noindex, redirected and robots.txt-blocked pages, add lastmod and images, ready for Google.

### At a glance

- **Crawls** a website from its home page, following links on the same host — up to 1,000 pages — or builds a sitemap from a **pasted list**, a CSV or an existing sitemap.
- Includes only **indexable pages**: it obeys robots.txt, and leaves out pages with noindex, a canonical pointing elsewhere, redirects and error statuses — listing each one with the reason.
- Adds **lastmod** from the page’s own date (article:modified_time, JSON-LD dateModified) or the server’s Last-Modified header, or a date you choose.
- Optionally adds **images** (Google image sitemap extension) and linked PDF files; changefreq and priority are optional because Google ignores them.
- Splits large sites into several files with a **sitemap index** at the protocol’s 50,000-URL / 50 MB limit, and also exports a plain-text list.
- Pages are fetched by your browser when the site allows it, otherwise through Jina Reader at about 18 pages a minute. Only page addresses are sent.

### Features

- **Crawls like Google**: Follows links, respects robots.txt and nofollow, and only keeps pages that can actually be indexed.
- **Clean by default**: No duplicates, no redirects, no noindex pages and no tracking parameters — the mistakes Search Console reports.
- **Honest lastmod**: Dates come from the pages themselves, so Google can trust them to spot updates.
- **Image sitemaps**: Add each page’s images to help them appear in Google Images.
- **Any size**: Sitemap index and numbered files are made automatically for very large sites.
- **From a list too**: Paste URLs or open a CSV or old sitemap to clean it up and rebuild it.

### How to create an XML sitemap

1. **Enter your website** — Type your home page address and choose how many pages to crawl, or switch to **From a list of URLs**.
2. **Let it crawl** — Pages are discovered through links; skipped pages are listed with the reason. You can stop at any time.
3. **Choose the details** — Pick where **lastmod** comes from and whether to add images; leave changefreq and priority out unless you need them.
4. **Upload and submit** — Download **sitemap.xml**, upload it to your site’s root, add it to robots.txt and submit it in Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools.

### Guide

#### What belongs in a sitemap

| Include | Leave out |
| --- | --- |
| Pages that return 200 and that you want in search results | Pages with noindex, or blocked in robots.txt |
| The canonical version of each page | Duplicates, ?ref= and other tracking variants |
| The final address after redirects | URLs that redirect or return 404 |
| Accurate lastmod dates | Dates that change on every build without a real update |

#### Do I need a sitemap?

Search engines find most pages by following links, but a sitemap helps them discover new and updated pages faster — especially on new sites with few backlinks, large sites, and pages that few other pages link to. Google reads **loc** and an accurate **lastmod**; it ignores changefreq and priority.

After uploading, list the sitemap in robots.txt (Sitemap: https://example.com/sitemap.xml) so every search engine finds it, and submit it once in Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools to see how many pages are indexed. Google no longer accepts sitemap “pings”; Bing and Yandex also support IndexNow for instant updates.

### FAQ

**Is the sitemap generator free?**
Yes, with no sign-up. Crawls are limited to 1,000 pages at a time; for bigger sites, crawl sections separately or use the URL list mode with an export from your CMS.

**Why is the crawl slow for my site?**
If your site doesn’t allow other websites to read its pages (most don’t), pages are fetched through Jina Reader, whose free service allows about 20 requests a minute — so 100 pages take around 6 minutes. Sites that allow it are crawled several pages at a time.

**Why were some pages left out?**
They can’t be indexed as they are: blocked by robots.txt, marked noindex, redirected, returning an error, or pointing to a different canonical URL. The “Pages left out” list shows the reason for each.

**Should I set changefreq and priority?**
Not for Google — it ignores both. They are optional and left out by default; an accurate lastmod is far more useful.

**How many URLs can one sitemap hold?**
50,000 URLs or 50 MB uncompressed. Larger sites need several sitemap files listed in a sitemap index, which the generator creates automatically.

## Robots.txt Generator

URL: https://justtools.online/seo-tools/robots-txt-generator/
Category: SEO & Marketing Tools
Processing: Contacts an external service to work (see the page).
Last updated: 2026-10-06

Create a robots.txt file free: block admin pages, AI training bots like GPTBot or SEO crawlers, add your sitemap, then test any URL against Google’s rules.

### At a glance

- Generates robots.txt from simple choices: default access, paths to block with exceptions, an optional Crawl-delay and your **sitemap** URLs.
- Lets you allow or block **26 named crawlers** in four groups — search engines, AI search assistants (OAI-SearchBot, Claude-SearchBot, PerplexityBot), **AI training bots** (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended, CCBot …) and SEO crawlers (AhrefsBot, SemrushBot …).
- Presets for WordPress, online shops, staging sites, and blocking AI training while staying in search and AI answers.
- **Validates** any robots.txt with line numbers: rules outside a group, unsupported noindex, misspellings, relative sitemaps, blocked CSS and JavaScript, and Google’s 500 KiB limit.
- **Tests a URL** against every crawler using Google’s matching rules (RFC 9309): the most specific user-agent group, the longest matching path, Allow winning ties — and shows the line that decided.
- Loads a site’s live robots.txt for checking — directly from your browser when the site allows it, otherwise through Jina Reader. Building and testing happen on your device.

### Features

- **Correct by construction**: Groups, paths and sitemap lines are written the way Google, Bing and AI crawlers expect, with full sitemap URLs.
- **AI crawler control**: Opt out of AI training without disappearing from ChatGPT, Claude or Perplexity search answers — or block AI completely.
- **Smart presets**: WordPress, online shop, staging and AI presets give a sensible starting point in one click.
- **Validator with line numbers**: Finds the mistakes that silently break robots.txt — and jumps to the line.
- **URL tester**: See which crawlers may fetch a page and which rule decides, before you upload the file.
- **Check any live site**: Load a website’s robots.txt to audit it, or to start editing your own.

### How to create a robots.txt file

1. **Pick a starting point** — Choose a preset such as **WordPress** or **Block AI training**, or start from **Allow everything**.
2. **Add your rules** — List paths to keep out of search (like /admin/), allow or block specific crawlers, and add your sitemap URL.
3. **Test it** — Click **Test a URL against this file** to check important pages are still crawlable.
4. **Upload** — Download robots.txt and upload it to your site’s root so it opens at example.com/robots.txt.

### Guide

#### robots.txt rules at a glance

| Line | Meaning | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| User-agent | Which crawler the following rules are for; * means all | User-agent: GPTBot |
| Disallow | Paths the crawler must not fetch | Disallow: /admin/ |
| Allow | An exception inside a disallowed path | Allow: /admin/help/ |
| * | Matches any characters | Disallow: /*?sort= |
| $ | Marks the end of the URL | Disallow: /*.pdf$ |
| Sitemap | Full URL of a sitemap, anywhere in the file | Sitemap: https://example.com/sitemap.xml |

#### What robots.txt can and can’t do

robots.txt controls **crawling**, not indexing. A blocked page can still appear in Google as a bare link if other sites link to it, and Google can’t see a noindex tag on a page it isn’t allowed to fetch. To keep a page out of search results, allow crawling and add **<meta name="robots" content="noindex">** instead.

It is also public and voluntary: well-behaved crawlers such as Googlebot, Bingbot, GPTBot and ClaudeBot obey it, but it is not access control. Never list secret paths in it, and protect private areas with a login.

### FAQ

**Where do I put robots.txt?**
In the root of your domain, so it opens at https://example.com/robots.txt. Each subdomain (blog.example.com) needs its own file, and it must be plain text returning HTTP 200.

**How do I block ChatGPT and other AI bots?**
Add a group for each crawler with Disallow: /. To stop training only, block GPTBot, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended, CCBot and similar; to also leave AI search answers, block OAI-SearchBot, Claude-SearchBot and PerplexityBot. The “Block AI training” and “Block all AI” presets do this for you.

**Will blocking Google-Extended remove my site from Google Search?**
No. Google-Extended only controls whether Gemini may use your content for training and grounding. Search, including AI Overviews, uses Googlebot.

**Does Google follow Crawl-delay?**
No. Bing and Yandex do; Google adjusts its crawl rate automatically. If Googlebot overloads your server, return 503 or 429 temporarily.

**Why does the validator say noindex isn’t supported?**
Google stopped honouring Noindex lines in robots.txt in September 2019. Use a robots meta tag or the X-Robots-Tag HTTP header on the page instead.

**Is blocking CSS and JavaScript a problem?**
Yes. Google renders pages like a browser; without your CSS and JavaScript it may see a broken page and rank it lower. Keep folders such as /wp-includes/ and /_next/ crawlable.

## Markdown to HTML Converter

URL: https://justtools.online/developer-tools/markdown-to-html/
Category: Developer Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-06

Convert Markdown to clean HTML online: GitHub tables, task lists and highlighted code, as a snippet or full page, minified or not. Batch files, no upload.

### At a glance

- Converts **GitHub Flavored Markdown** — tables with alignment, task lists, strikethrough, autolinks and GitHub alerts — to HTML as you type.
- Outputs an **HTML snippet**, a **full styled page** (GitHub-like CSS with light and dark themes) or a **plain full page**; title, description and language come from YAML front matter.
- **Syntax-highlights** code blocks in 20+ languages with highlight.js classes, or emits plain language-* classes for Prism.
- Options for heading IDs, # anchor links, external links in a new tab, GitHub-style line breaks, front matter and **minified** output.
- **Removes unsafe HTML** — scripts, event handlers and iframes — with DOMPurify, so the output is safe to publish.
- Converts **several .md files at once** and downloads them as a .zip. Everything runs in your browser; files are never uploaded.

### Features

- **Clean output**: Semantic HTML without inline styles — headings, lists, tables and code exactly as you wrote them.
- **Snippet or full page**: Paste a snippet into WordPress, Ghost or an email, or download a standalone styled page.
- **Highlighted code**: Code blocks come out with highlight.js markup and a matching theme in the styled page.
- **Safe to publish**: Raw HTML in the Markdown is sanitised, so copied content can’t carry scripts.
- **Batch conversion**: Drop a folder’s worth of .md files and get every page as .html in one zip.
- **Live preview**: Switch between the HTML source and the rendered result while you edit.

### How to convert Markdown to HTML

1. **Add your Markdown** — Paste or type it, or click **Open files** (or drop .md files) to convert several at once.
2. **Choose the output** — Pick **HTML snippet**, **Full page, styled** or **Full page, plain**, and set options such as heading IDs or minify.
3. **Check it** — Read the highlighted HTML, or switch to **Preview** to see how it looks.
4. **Copy or download** — Click **Copy HTML**, download the .html file, or download all files as a .zip.

### Guide

#### Markdown and the HTML it becomes

| Markdown | HTML |
| --- | --- |
| # Title | <h1 id="title">Title</h1> |
| **bold** and _italic_ | <strong>bold</strong> and <em>italic</em> |
| [link](https://example.com) | <a href="https://example.com">link</a> |
| - item | <ul><li>item</li></ul> |
| - [x] done | <li><input type="checkbox" checked disabled> done</li> |
| `code` | <code>code</code> |
| | a | b | table | <table> with <thead> and <tbody> |

#### Snippet or full page?

Use the **HTML snippet** when the HTML goes inside an existing page — a CMS editor, a blog template, a help centre or an email builder. They already have their own <head> and styles.

Use a **full page** for a standalone file you open, share or host on its own: documentation, release notes or a README turned into a web page. The styled version embeds the CSS, so it looks right without any other files.

### FAQ

**Is my Markdown uploaded?**
No. The conversion runs in your browser with the marked library, and nothing is sent to a server — so it’s safe for private documentation.

**Does it support GitHub Flavored Markdown?**
Yes: tables, task lists, strikethrough, autolinks and fenced code blocks, plus GitHub alerts (> [!NOTE], [!TIP], [!WARNING] …) and heading IDs that match GitHub’s.

**Can I keep raw HTML from my Markdown?**
Yes. Safe HTML such as <details>, <kbd> or <img> is kept. With “Remove unsafe HTML” on, scripts, iframes, forms and inline event handlers are stripped; switch it off only for content you trust.

**How do I style the HTML?**
Choose “Full page, styled” for a ready-made GitHub-like look, or use the snippet with your own CSS. Code blocks use highlight.js classes, so any highlight.js theme works.

**Can I convert many Markdown files at once?**
Yes. Open or drop several .md files; switch between them to check each one, then download all as HTML files in a .zip with the same options.

## Resume Builder

URL: https://justtools.online/career-tools/resume-builder/
Category: Career Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-06

Free resume builder with 4 ATS-friendly templates: fill in your details, see a live preview, and download a PDF or Word file. No sign-up and no watermark.

### At a glance

- **Four templates** — Classic, Modern (sidebar), Minimal and Compact — with your choice of colour, font (Inter, Lora or Poppins), text size, date format and A4 or US Letter paper.
- Downloads a **real-text PDF** that applicant tracking systems (ATS) can read, with clickable email, phone and profile links — and a **Word (.docx)** version recruiters can edit.
- Sections for summary, experience, education, projects, skills, certifications, awards, languages and interests, plus **personal details** and a **declaration** for Indian applications, and your own custom sections.
- A **resume check** flags missing contact details, weak bullet points, missing numbers, long bullets and length, and a **job description match** shows which keywords you are missing.
- Live preview of the exact PDF, page by page. Reorder and hide sections, add a photo, and copy a plain-text version for job portal forms.
- Everything stays in your browser and is saved on this device; export a .json file (or JSON Resume) to continue later or on another computer. Free, with no sign-up and no watermark.

### Features

- **ATS-friendly by design**: Real text, standard section names and clean layouts that resume-screening software reads correctly.
- **PDF and Word**: A pixel-perfect PDF for applying and an editable .docx when a recruiter asks for Word.
- **What you see is what you get**: The preview is the actual PDF, so spacing and page breaks are exactly as downloaded.
- **Built-in resume check**: Tips on action verbs, numbers, length and contact details — the things recruiters notice in seconds.
- **Match any job**: Paste a job ad to see which of its keywords your resume already covers and which to add.
- **Private**: No account and no upload: your resume is stored only in this browser until you download it.

### How to make a resume

1. **Fill in your details** — Start from the example or a blank page, and add your contact details, summary, experience, education and skills.
2. **Choose a design** — Open **Design** to pick a template, colour, font and size, and to reorder or hide sections.
3. **Check it** — Open **Check** for tips, and paste a job description to see which keywords are missing.
4. **Download** — Click **Download PDF** to apply, or **Word** for an editable copy. Use **Save data** to keep a copy you can edit later.

### Guide

#### Which sections to include

| Section | Freshers | Experienced |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Summary | 2–3 lines on your skills and the role you want | 2–4 lines on your experience and biggest strengths |
| Experience | Internships, part-time work, freelancing | Most recent first, 3–5 achievement bullets each |
| Projects | College and personal projects — put them high up | Optional; side projects that show relevant skills |
| Education | Near the top, with CGPA or percentage | Near the end; the score can be left out |
| Skills | Tools, languages and software you can really use | Grouped: languages, tools, methods |
| Certifications | Online courses and certificates | Professional certifications |
| Personal details & declaration | Often asked for in campus and government jobs | Usually left out for private-sector and overseas jobs |

#### How to write bullet points that get shortlisted

- Start with an action verb — **Led, Built, Reduced, Increased, Launched** — not “Responsible for”.
- Show the result with a number: “Cut report time from 3 days to 4 hours”, “Handled 120 customer calls a day”, “Saved ₹8 lakh a year”.
- Keep each bullet to one or two lines, and 3–5 bullets per job.
- Use the words from the job description for skills you really have — ATS software ranks resumes by matching them.
- Keep the resume to one page with under about five years of experience, and two pages at most.

### FAQ

**Is this resume builder really free?**
Yes. Every template, the PDF and Word downloads and the resume check are free, with no sign-up, no watermark and no limit on downloads or edits.

**Is my resume uploaded or stored on a server?**
No. The resume is created in your browser and saved only on this device. Nobody — including us — can see it. Clear it any time with Start blank.

**Are these resumes ATS-friendly?**
Yes. The PDF contains real, selectable text with standard section headings, which applicant tracking systems read correctly. Classic and Minimal are the safest choices for job portals; the two-column Modern template is fine for most modern systems.

**Should I add a photo, date of birth and declaration?**
In India they are common for government, PSU and campus applications. Leave them out for private-sector, MNC and overseas jobs, where recruiters prefer not to see them.

**Can I edit my resume later?**
Yes. It is saved automatically in this browser. To move it to another device, use More → Save data (.json) and open that file there. JSON Resume files from other tools can be opened too.

**What is the best resume format for freshers?**
One page: contact details, a two-line summary, education with CGPA, projects and internships with results, skills and certifications. The example resume shows the structure — replace it with your details.

**Can I write my resume in Hindi?**
Hindi text prints correctly in the PDF, but most companies and ATS software expect an English resume, and some systems read Hindi text imperfectly.

## Tic Tac Toe

URL: https://justtools.online/games/tic-tac-toe/
Category: Games
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-07

Play Tic Tac Toe online free against the computer — Easy, Medium or unbeatable Hard — or with a friend on one device. 3×3 to 6×6 boards. No sign-up.

### At a glance

- Play against the computer on **Easy**, **Medium** or **Hard**, or with a friend taking turns on the same phone, tablet or computer.
- On the classic 3×3 board, Hard plays perfectly and **never loses** — the best anyone can do against it is a draw.
- Bigger boards for a longer game: **4×4, 5×5 and 6×6**, with 3, 4 or 5 in a row to win.
- Classic Tic Tac Toe has **255,168 possible games**: X wins 131,184, O wins 77,904 and 46,080 end in a draw. With perfect play it is always a draw.
- Hints, undo, sound, full screen and keyboard play; scores are kept for each mode and board on your device. Free, with no download or sign-up.

### Features

- **Three difficulty levels**: Easy for young children, Medium for a fair fight, and a Hard opponent that never loses on 3×3.
- **Two players, one device**: Pass and play with a friend, with your own names and a running score.
- **Bigger boards**: Try 4×4, 5×5 or 6×6 with 3, 4 or 5 in a row — the computer thinks several moves ahead.
- **Learn as you play**: Ask for a hint to see the best move, or take a move back and try another idea.
- **Fair starts**: The first move swaps sides every round, so nobody always has the advantage.
- **Plays anywhere**: Works on phones, tablets and computers, with keyboard controls and screen reader announcements.

### How to play Tic Tac Toe

1. **Choose an opponent** — Pick **Computer** and a difficulty, and whether you play X or O — or pick **A friend** to play on the same device.
2. **Choose a board** — Keep the classic 3×3 board, or try 4×4, 5×5 or 6×6 and choose how many in a row it takes to win.
3. **Take turns** — Tap an empty square to place your mark. The first to complete a line across, down or diagonally wins; a full board with no line is a draw.
4. **Play again** — Press **Play again** for the next round — the score keeps adding up. Use **Hint** or **Undo** while you learn.

### Guide

#### The rules

Two players take turns placing their mark — X or O — in an empty square of a 3×3 grid. The first player to get three of their marks in a row, column or diagonal wins. If all nine squares fill up with no line, the game is a draw.

The game is also called **noughts and crosses** in Britain and **zero kata** in India. On bigger boards the idea is the same, but you need the number in a row shown under the board.

#### How to never lose at 3×3

- No first move wins by force: with best play from both sides, every opening ends in a draw.
- If your opponent starts in a **corner**, take the **centre** — every other reply loses against perfect play.
- If they start in the **centre**, take a **corner**. Answering on an edge loses.
- If they start on an **edge**, take the centre, a corner next to their mark, or the edge opposite it.
- On every turn, first look for a winning move, then block any two-in-a-row of theirs.
- Win with a **fork**: a move that makes two lines of two at once, so your opponent can only block one.

#### Tic Tac Toe by the numbers

| Classic 3×3 | Count |
| --- | --- |
| Possible games (until someone wins or the board fills) | 255,168 |
| … won by X (who moves first) | 131,184 |
| … won by O | 77,904 |
| … drawn | 46,080 |
| Positions that can occur in a game | 5,478 |
| Different positions, counting rotations and mirror images once | 765 |
| Result with perfect play | Draw |

### FAQ

**Can you beat the computer on Hard?**
Not on the 3×3 board: Hard plays perfectly, so the best possible result is a draw. On bigger boards it looks several moves ahead in about a second per move, so strong players can still win.

**How do I play with a friend?**
Choose **A friend** under Play against, add your names if you like, and take turns on the same phone or computer. Playing over the internet on two devices isn’t available.

**Who goes first?**
X moves first in a normal game. With **Take turns going first** switched on (the default), the first move swaps between the players every round, which keeps things fair.

**Is Tic Tac Toe always a draw?**
With perfect play by both players, yes — the classic 3×3 game always ends in a draw. Games are won when someone misses a block or falls for a fork.

**Is it free, and does it need the internet?**
It’s free with no download or sign-up. Once the page has loaded, the game runs entirely in your browser, so it keeps working if your connection drops.

**Are my scores saved?**
Yes, in this browser only, with a separate score for each mode, difficulty and board size. **Reset score** clears the one you are playing.

## Image Color Picker

URL: https://justtools.online/image-tools/image-color-picker/
Category: Image Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-07

Pick colours from any image: get HEX, RGB, HSL and CMYK codes with a zoom loupe, plus the image’s colour palette. Free, private — nothing is uploaded.

### At a glance

- Click any pixel to get its colour as **HEX, RGB, HSL, HSV and CMYK**, each with a copy button — transparent pixels also give RGBA and 8-digit HEX.
- A **magnifier** shows the 11 × 11 pixels around the pointer; sample a single pixel or the **average of 3×3, 5×5 or 9×9** pixels to smooth out noise.
- Shows the **nearest CSS colour name** and the **closest Tailwind CSS colour**, matched with the CIEDE2000 colour-difference formula.
- Builds the image’s **colour palette** — its 5, 8 or 12 main colours with how much of the image each covers — ready to copy as a HEX list or CSS variables.
- Checks **contrast** against white and black text (WCAG ratio and AA/AAA level). In Chrome and Edge on a computer you can also pick a colour from anywhere on your screen.
- Works with JPG, PNG, WebP, HEIC and pasted screenshots. The image never leaves your browser.

### Features

- **Pixel-exact**: A zoomed loupe and arrow-key nudging land on exactly the pixel you want, even in fine details.
- **Every format**: HEX, RGB, HSL, HSV, CMYK, a CSS name and a Tailwind class — copy whichever your project uses.
- **Instant palette**: The main colours of the whole image, worked out automatically and sorted by how much space they take.
- **Accessible colours**: See at once whether the colour is readable on white or on black, with WCAG contrast ratios.
- **Colour history**: Every colour you pick is kept in a row of swatches, so you can compare and copy them all.
- **Private**: Pixels are read in your browser — logos, designs and screenshots are never uploaded.

### How to pick a colour from an image

1. **Open the image** — Drop a photo, screenshot or logo on the page, browse for it, or paste a screenshot with Ctrl+V.
2. **Aim with the magnifier** — Move over the image to see the pixels up close. On a phone, drag your finger and lift it to pick.
3. **Click to pick** — Click the pixel you want. Its HEX, RGB, HSL, HSV and CMYK codes appear on the right.
4. **Copy the code** — Press the copy button next to any format, or use the palette and history to copy several colours at once.

### Guide

#### Colour code formats explained

| Format | Example | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HEX | #1E90FF | Websites (HTML and CSS), design apps, brand guides |
| RGB | rgb(30, 144, 255) | CSS, screens, video and most software |
| HSL | hsl(210, 100%, 56%) | CSS — easy to make lighter, darker or less saturated versions |
| HSV / HSB | hsv(210, 88%, 100%) | Colour pickers in Photoshop, Figma and other design tools |
| CMYK | cmyk(88%, 44%, 0%, 0%) | A starting point for print — check final print colours with your printer |

#### Tips for accurate colours

- Use a PNG or a high-quality original where you can: JPG compression and resizing blend neighbouring pixels.
- In photos, average **3×3 or 5×5** pixels — single pixels vary because of noise and texture.
- Pick from flat areas of a logo, not its edges, where colours blend into the background.
- Screenshots show colours as your screen displays them, which may differ slightly from the original design file.

### FAQ

**How do I find the HEX code of a colour in an image?**
Open the image here and click the colour. The HEX code (such as #1E90FF) appears at the top of the list with a copy button, together with RGB, HSL, HSV and CMYK.

**Is my image uploaded?**
No. The image is opened and read entirely in your browser, so it never leaves your device.

**Can I pick a colour from my screen, outside the image?**
Yes, in Chrome, Edge and other Chromium browsers on a computer: press **Pick from screen** and click anywhere. Other browsers don’t offer this yet — take a screenshot and paste it instead.

**How is the colour palette made?**
The tool groups similar pixels together (k-means clustering in the CIELAB colour space, which matches how people see colour differences) and shows each group’s average colour, largest first.

**Why does the colour look slightly different from my design file?**
JPG compression, resizing and screen colour profiles all shift colours a little. For brand colours, pick from the original PNG or SVG export, or average a few pixels.

**What does the contrast ratio mean?**
It is the WCAG measure of how readable text is: at least 4.5:1 for normal text (AA) and 7:1 for AAA. The two cards show the picked colour as text on white and on black.

## Image to Grayscale Converter

URL: https://justtools.online/image-tools/image-to-grayscale/
Category: Image Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-07

Convert images to grayscale or black and white online: pick the method, adjust contrast, add sepia, and download in bulk as JPG, PNG or WebP. Free, no upload.

### At a glance

- Converts to **shades of grey** or pure **black and white**, with a before-and-after slider to compare.
- Seven ways to turn colour into grey: **Luminance** (Rec. 709 in linear light, the default), **Rec. 601**, average, lightness, or a single red, green or blue channel.
- Black and white uses an **automatic threshold** (Otsu’s method) or your own, with optional **Floyd–Steinberg dithering** to keep shading in photos.
- Adjust **intensity** (partly desaturated looks), **brightness** and **contrast**, and add a **sepia** tone.
- Converts **many images at once** and downloads them as a ZIP — as JPG, PNG or WebP. Neutral grey PNGs are saved as true **8-bit greyscale (1-bit for black and white)**, so files are much smaller.
- Works with JPG, PNG, WebP and HEIC. Images are processed in your browser and location data is removed.

### Features

- **Natural-looking greys**: The default method keeps the brightness you see, so reds and blues don’t turn muddy or washed out.
- **Crisp black and white**: Perfect for scans, signatures and line art — or dither photos for a newspaper-print look.
- **Batch conversion**: Drop a whole folder of photos; every image uses the same settings and downloads together as a ZIP.
- **Before and after**: Drag the slider over the preview to compare the original with the converted image.
- **Small files**: True greyscale PNGs store one value per pixel instead of three, typically far smaller than colour PNGs.
- **Private**: No uploads: conversion happens on your own device, even for large photos.

### How to convert an image to grayscale

1. **Add your images** — Drop one or more photos on the page, browse for them, or paste with Ctrl+V.
2. **Choose grey or black & white** — Pick **Shades of grey** or **Black & white**, and a method if you want a different look.
3. **Fine-tune** — Adjust brightness, contrast and intensity, or add a sepia tone. Drag the slider on the preview to compare.
4. **Download** — Download each image, or **Download all (ZIP)** — as JPG, PNG or WebP.

### Guide

#### Which grayscale method should I use?

| Method | Formula | Best for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Luminance | 0.2126 R + 0.7152 G + 0.0722 B, in linear light | Photos — keeps the brightness people see |
| Rec. 601 | 0.299 R + 0.587 G + 0.114 B | Matching most other apps and older software |
| Average | (R + G + B) ÷ 3 | Quick, simple results |
| Lightness | (max + min) ÷ 2 | A soft, low-contrast look |
| Red channel | R | Dramatic skies and smooth skin, like a red filter on film |
| Green / blue channel | G or B | Foliage detail (green) or a moody, grainy look (blue) |

#### Grayscale or black and white?

**Grayscale** keeps up to 256 shades of grey, so a photo still shows every tone — this is what most people mean by a black-and-white photo.

**Black and white** (1-bit) uses only pure black and pure white. It suits scanned documents, signatures, stamps, logos and line drawings, and makes the smallest files. Turn on **dithering** to fake grey tones with dots when converting photos.

### FAQ

**How do I convert a photo to black and white?**
Drop the photo here: it is converted to grayscale straight away. Drag the slider to compare, adjust contrast if you like, then press the download button.

**Is grayscale the same as black and white?**
In everyday language, yes — a "black and white photo" is grayscale, with many shades of grey. Choose **Black & white** here for pure black and white only, for example for scanned documents.

**Are my photos uploaded?**
No. Everything happens in your browser, so your photos never leave your device.

**Can I convert several images at once?**
Yes. Add as many images as you want; they all use the same settings, and **Download all (ZIP)** saves them in one file.

**Why is the grayscale PNG smaller than the original?**
A colour PNG stores red, green and blue for every pixel. A greyscale PNG stores just one grey value (or a single bit for black and white), so the same picture takes far less space — with no loss of quality.

**Can I make a sepia photo?**
Yes. Choose **Sepia** under Tone for the warm brown look of old photographs; it works in both grey and black-and-white modes.

## Crop Image

URL: https://justtools.online/image-tools/crop-image/
Category: Image Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-07

Crop images online to any size or ratio: 1:1, 16:9, Instagram and YouTube sizes, circle crop, rotate, flip and straighten. Free, private and full quality.

### At a glance

- Crop freehand or to a fixed ratio — **1:1, 4:3, 3:2, 16:9, 4:5, 3:4, 2:3, 9:16**, the photo’s own ratio or a custom one.
- Ready-made sizes for **Instagram** (1080×1080, 1080×1350, stories 1080×1920), **YouTube thumbnails** (1280×720), X and LinkedIn headers, Facebook covers and profile pictures.
- Type exact **X, Y, width and height** in pixels, and optionally resize the result to any width and height.
- **Rotate** by 90°, **flip**, and **straighten** tilted photos by up to 45° — the crop automatically fits inside the photo so no empty corners show.
- **Circle crop** for profile pictures, with a transparent background in PNG and WebP.
- Saves at full resolution as JPG, PNG or WebP (HEIC opens too). The image is processed in your browser and never uploaded.

### Features

- **Precise control**: Drag eight handles, nudge with arrow keys, or type exact pixel values.
- **Social media sizes**: One click sets both the shape and the final pixel size for Instagram, YouTube, X, LinkedIn and Facebook.
- **Straighten and rotate**: Fix a tilted horizon and turn or mirror the photo before you crop.
- **Circle crop**: Round profile pictures with a transparent background, ready for any app.
- **Full quality**: The crop is taken from the original pixels, with careful resizing when you scale down.
- **Private**: No upload and no watermark — the photo stays on your device.

### How to crop an image

1. **Open the image** — Drop a photo on the page, browse for it, or paste with Ctrl+V.
2. **Choose a shape** — Pick an aspect ratio such as 1:1 or 16:9, a social media size, or keep it free. Choose **Circle** for round profile pictures.
3. **Adjust the crop** — Drag the corners and edges, move the box, or type exact values. Rotate, flip or straighten if needed.
4. **Download** — Check the preview and size, choose JPG, PNG or WebP, and press **Download**.

### Guide

#### Common image sizes

| Use | Size (pixels) | Ratio |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Instagram square post | 1080 × 1080 | 1:1 |
| Instagram portrait post | 1080 × 1350 | 4:5 |
| Instagram / WhatsApp story, Reels | 1080 × 1920 | 9:16 |
| YouTube thumbnail | 1280 × 720 | 16:9 |
| X (Twitter) header | 1500 × 500 | 3:1 |
| LinkedIn banner | 1584 × 396 | 4:1 |
| Facebook cover | 851 × 315 | ≈ 2.7:1 |

#### Cropping tips

- Use the **rule-of-thirds** grid: place eyes, horizons and key details on the lines rather than dead centre.
- Leave a little space in the direction a person is looking or moving.
- Crop before resizing — cropping a large original keeps more detail than cropping a small copy.
- For profile pictures, centre the face in a square crop: most apps show it as a circle.

### FAQ

**How do I crop an image to a specific size?**
Pick a ratio, then type the width and height under **Resize to** — or choose a social media size, which sets both. The crop box keeps the right shape while you move it.

**Does cropping reduce quality?**
No. The crop is cut from the original pixels at full resolution. Quality only changes if you resize the result or save as JPG/WebP — use quality 90 or higher, or PNG, to keep it pristine.

**How do I crop an image into a circle?**
Choose **Circle** under Shape. The square crop becomes a circle with a transparent outside when you save as PNG or WebP.

**Is my photo uploaded?**
No. Cropping happens entirely in your browser, so the photo never leaves your device.

**Can I straighten a crooked photo?**
Yes. Drag the **Straighten** slider until the horizon is level; the crop shrinks automatically so no empty corners appear.

**Which format should I download?**
JPG for photos (smallest files), PNG for screenshots, graphics and transparent circles, and WebP for websites. **Original** keeps JPG, PNG and WebP in their own format; HEIC and other formats are saved as WebP (or JPG).
