### How to make a favicon

1. **Choose the source** — Upload your logo (SVG is best), or type one or two letters, or pick an emoji.
2. **Style it** — Pick a background colour (or none), a shape and the padding. Check the 16 px preview and the dark browser tab.
3. **Add your site name** — Enter the name and theme colour used by phones when your site is added to the home screen.
4. **Download and install** — Download the ZIP, upload the files to your site’s root folder and paste the HTML into <head>.

### Guide

#### Which favicon files do you need?

| File | Size | Used by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| favicon.ico | 16, 32, 48 px | All browsers, bookmarks, and tools that ask for /favicon.ico |
| favicon.svg | Any size | Modern browsers — sharp on every screen |
| favicon-96x96.png | 96 × 96 | Browsers and Google Search, which wants a multiple of 48 px |
| apple-touch-icon.png | 180 × 180 | iPhone and iPad home screen and bookmarks |
| web-app-manifest-192x192.png | 192 × 192 | Android home screen |
| web-app-manifest-512x512.png | 512 × 512 | Android splash screen and installed web apps |
| maskable-icon-512x512.png | 512 × 512 | Android adaptive icons (circles, squircles and other shapes) |
| site.webmanifest | — | App name, colours and icons for “Add to home screen” |

#### Tips for a favicon that stands out

- Keep it simple: a symbol or one or two letters. Detailed logos turn into a blur at 16 pixels.
- Check the **dark tab** preview — a black logo on a transparent background disappears in dark mode. Add a background colour or a light outline.
- Use strong contrast between the letters and the background.
- Use an SVG logo if you have one: favicon.svg stays crisp on high-resolution screens.
- Browsers cache favicons for a long time. Open your site in a private window to see the new one.

### FAQ

**What size should a favicon be?**
Browsers use 16 × 16 and 32 × 32 pixels (48 × 48 on Windows), all stored in favicon.ico. Apple devices use a 180 × 180 icon, Android uses 192 × 192 and 512 × 512, and Google Search needs a size that is a multiple of 48 px. This tool makes all of them.

**How do I add a favicon to my website?**
Upload the files from the ZIP to the root folder of your site (where index.html is), then paste the HTML code from this page into the <head> of every page — or your site template.

**How do I add a favicon in WordPress?**
Go to **Appearance → Customize → Site Identity → Site Icon** (or **Settings → General** in newer versions) and upload web-app-manifest-512x512.png. WordPress creates the other sizes itself.

**Why don’t I see my new favicon?**
Browsers cache favicons aggressively. Open the site in a private window or clear the cache. Google Search updates its favicon when it next crawls your home page, which can take days or weeks.

**Do I still need favicon.ico?**
Yes. Many browsers, RSS readers and other tools still ask for /favicon.ico automatically. Modern browsers then prefer favicon.svg or the PNGs listed in your HTML.

**What is a maskable icon?**
Android crops app icons into circles, squircles or rounded squares. A maskable icon has a full background and keeps the logo inside a central safe zone, so nothing important is cut off whatever shape the phone uses.

**Is my logo uploaded?**
No. The icons are drawn in your browser and zipped on your device; nothing is sent anywhere.

## Unit Converter

URL: https://justtools.online/converters/unit-converter/
Category: Converters
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-07

Convert length, weight, area, volume, temperature, speed, data and 8 more quantities — including guntha, bigha, tola and lakh. Type “5 ft 10 in to cm”.

### At a glance

- **15 categories**: length, weight, temperature, area, volume, speed, time, data storage, pressure, energy, power, fuel economy, angle, frequency and lakh/crore numbers.
- Uses the **exact definitions**: 1 inch = 2.54 cm, 1 foot = 0.3048 m, 1 pound = 0.45359237 kg, 1 US gallon = 3.785411784 litres.
- **Indian units**: guntha, cent, ground, marla, kanal, gaj (square yard), bigha and katha (West Bengal), tola and quintal, lakh and crore.
- Type a conversion in plain words — **“5 ft 10 in to cm”**, “100 kmph in mph”, “1.5 ton to kW” (AC tonnage) — and get the answer instantly.
- See the value in **every unit** of a category at once, with the formula, adjustable precision and Indian (12,34,567) or international number grouping.

### Features

- **Type to convert**: Write conversions the way you say them, including feet-and-inches and °F to °C.
- **Exact factors**: Legal definitions of the inch, pound and gallon, so results match textbooks and spec sheets.
- **Land units of India**: Guntha, cent, ground, marla, kanal and gaj alongside acres, hectares and square feet.
- **All units at once**: One value shown in every unit of the category — copy any of them with a click.
- **Binary and decimal data**: GB and GiB, MB and MiB, megabits and megabytes — clearly separated.
- **Remembers your choice**: Your last category, units and number style are kept on this device.

### How to convert units

1. **Pick a category** — Choose length, weight, area or another quantity — or type a conversion in the box at the top.
2. **Enter a value** — Type the number and choose the units to convert from and to. Press ⇄ to swap them.
3. **Read and copy** — The answer appears instantly with its formula. Copy it, or see the value in every other unit below.

### Guide

#### Common conversions

| From | To | Multiply by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| inches | centimetres | 2.54 |
| feet | metres | 0.3048 |
| miles | kilometres | 1.609344 |
| pounds | kilograms | 0.45359237 |
| acres | square feet | 43,560 |
| hectares | acres | 2.47105 |
| square yards (gaj) | square feet | 9 |
| guntha | square feet | 1,089 |
| US gallons | litres | 3.785411784 |
| °C | °F | × 9/5, then + 32 |

#### Indian land measurement units

Land is still measured in local units in much of India. This converter uses these sizes: **1 guntha = 1,089 sq ft** (Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana), **1 cent = 435.6 sq ft** (1/100 acre, used in South India), **1 ground = 2,400 sq ft** (Tamil Nadu), **1 marla = 272.25 sq ft** and **1 kanal = 20 marla = 5,445 sq ft** (Punjab, Haryana), and **1 gaj = 1 sq yard = 9 sq ft**.

The **bigha** and **katha** differ from state to state, and even between districts. The converter uses the West Bengal and Assam sizes (1 bigha = 14,400 sq ft, 1 katha = 720 sq ft) — check the local value with your land records office before a sale.

### FAQ

**How many cm is 5 feet 10 inches?**
5 ft 10 in is 177.8 cm. Type “5 ft 10 in to cm” in the box at the top to convert any height.

**How do I convert Celsius to Fahrenheit?**
Multiply by 9/5 and add 32: 37 °C × 9/5 + 32 = 98.6 °F. To go back, subtract 32 and multiply by 5/9.

**How many square feet are in a guntha, acre or bigha?**
A guntha is 1,089 sq ft and an acre is 43,560 sq ft (40 guntha). A bigha differs by state; in West Bengal and Assam it is 14,400 sq ft.

**What is the difference between GB and GiB?**
A gigabyte (GB) is 1,000,000,000 bytes; a gibibyte (GiB) is 1,073,741,824 bytes (1024³). Drive makers use GB, while Windows shows sizes in GiB but labels them “GB” — which is why a 1 TB drive appears as about 931 GB.

**How do I convert lakh and crore to million?**
1 lakh = 100,000 and 1 crore = 10 million, so 10 lakh = 1 million and 100 crore = 1 billion. Choose the “Lakh & crore” category.

**What does an AC “ton” mean?**
It measures cooling power: 1 ton of refrigeration = 12,000 BTU per hour ≈ 3.517 kW of cooling. A 1.5 ton AC removes about 5.3 kW of heat — it is not its electricity use.

## Unix Timestamp Converter

URL: https://justtools.online/converters/unix-timestamp-converter/
Category: Converters
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-07

Convert Unix epoch time to a date in any time zone and back. Detects seconds, ms, µs and ns; also Excel, LDAP and WebKit times, and timestamps in logs.

### At a glance

- Shows the **current Unix time** live, in seconds and milliseconds, ready to copy.
- **Detects the unit** of a timestamp — seconds, milliseconds, microseconds or nanoseconds — and keeps nanosecond precision.
- Converts to **ISO 8601**, RFC 2822/HTTP date, a readable date and “3 days ago”, in **any IANA time zone**, with day of the year and ISO week.
- Turns a date and time in any zone back into epoch time, handling **daylight-saving** changes correctly.
- Also reads and writes **Excel serial dates**, **Windows FILETIME/LDAP**, **WebKit/Chrome** time, **Apple Cocoa** time and **Julian days**.
- Finds the 10- and 13-digit timestamps in **pasted logs or JSON** and adds the date next to each one.

### Features

- **Any unit**: Paste a 10, 13, 16 or 19-digit timestamp — the unit is detected for you.
- **Every time zone**: All IANA zones from your browser, with correct offsets for the date, including DST.
- **Both directions**: Epoch to date, and date to epoch — or paste any date text to inspect it.
- **Developer formats**: Excel, LDAP/Active Directory, Chrome history, Apple and Julian timestamps in one place.
- **Log decoder**: Make server logs readable by annotating or replacing every Unix timestamp.
- **Private**: Everything runs in your browser; nothing you paste is sent anywhere.

### How to convert a Unix timestamp

1. **Paste the timestamp** — Enter it under **Timestamp to date** — seconds, milliseconds or more are detected automatically.
2. **Choose a time zone** — Pick your zone, UTC or any other, to see the local date and time.
3. **Copy the format you need** — Copy ISO 8601, the readable date or any other format from the list.

### Guide

#### Get the current Unix time in code

| Language | Seconds | Milliseconds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| JavaScript | `Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000)` | `Date.now()` |
| Python | `int(time.time())` | `time.time_ns() // 1_000_000` |
| Java | `Instant.now().getEpochSecond()` | `System.currentTimeMillis()` |
| Go | `time.Now().Unix()` | `time.Now().UnixMilli()` |
| PHP | `time()` | `(int) (microtime(true) * 1000)` |
| C# | `DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.ToUnixTimeSeconds()` | `DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.ToUnixTimeMilliseconds()` |
| MySQL | `UNIX_TIMESTAMP()` | `ROUND(UNIX_TIMESTAMP(NOW(3)) * 1000)` |
| PostgreSQL | `extract(epoch from now())::bigint` | `(extract(epoch from now()) * 1000)::bigint` |
| Bash | `date +%s` | `date +%s%3N` |

#### Notable Unix times

| Timestamp | Date (UTC) | Why it matters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | 1 January 1970, 00:00:00 | The Unix epoch |
| 1,000,000,000 | 9 September 2001, 01:46:40 | The billionth second |
| 1,234,567,890 | 13 February 2009, 23:31:30 | A famous “counting” moment |
| 2,000,000,000 | 18 May 2033, 03:33:20 | Two billion seconds |
| 2,147,483,647 | 19 January 2038, 03:14:07 | Largest signed 32-bit time — the Year 2038 problem |

### FAQ

**What is Unix time (epoch time)?**
The number of seconds since 00:00:00 UTC on 1 January 1970, not counting leap seconds. It is the same everywhere in the world; time zones only change how it is displayed.

**Is my timestamp in seconds or milliseconds?**
Count the digits: today’s times have 10 digits in seconds and 13 in milliseconds (16 in microseconds, 19 in nanoseconds). The converter detects this automatically.

**What is the Year 2038 problem?**
Systems that store Unix time as a signed 32-bit number overflow after 2,147,483,647 — 03:14:07 UTC on 19 January 2038. Modern systems use 64-bit time, which lasts billions of years.

**How do I convert an Excel date to a timestamp?**
Choose “Excel / Sheets serial date” as the format and paste the number. Excel counts days from 30 December 1899, so 45292 is 1 January 2024.

**Does Unix time change with daylight saving?**
No. Unix time always counts UTC seconds. Daylight saving only changes the local time shown for it — which the converter applies for the zone you choose.

## Emoji & Kaomoji Picker

URL: https://justtools.online/text-tools/emoji-kaomoji-picker/
Category: Text Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-07

Search and copy every emoji, 200 kaomoji like ¯\_(ツ)_/¯ and 270+ text symbols with one click. Skin tones, recents and Unicode codes for developers.

### At a glance

- **Every emoji** up to Emoji 17, with names and keywords from the Unicode CLDR — search “party”, “india” or a shortcode like :joy:.
- **200 kaomoji** (Japanese text faces) in 19 moods — happy, love, shrug ¯\_(ツ)_/¯, table flip, cats, bears and more.
- **270+ text symbols**: arrows, stars, hearts, check marks, maths, currency (₹ € £), fractions, superscripts, keyboard keys and chess.
- Click to copy, or switch on **Collect into text** to build a message from several picks. Recently used items and your skin tone are remembered on this device.
- For developers: each emoji’s **code points**, HTML entity, CSS, JavaScript and Python escapes, URL encoding and UTF-8 bytes.
- Emoji your device can’t draw yet are hidden automatically, so you only see emoji that will show up.

- **Smart search**: Names, keywords and GitHub-style shortcodes — find 😂 by typing “laugh”, “joy” or :joy:.
- **Skin tones**: Pick a tone once and every hand and person emoji uses it.
- **Kaomoji for every mood**: From (◕‿◕) to (╯°□°）╯︵ ┻━┻, grouped and searchable.
- **Symbols that work anywhere**: Text symbols paste into names, bios, documents and code without images.
- **Compose messages**: Collect several emoji and symbols, then copy them all at once.
- **Unicode details**: Code points and escapes ready to paste into HTML, CSS, JavaScript or Python.

### How to copy an emoji or kaomoji

1. **Choose a tab** — Pick **Emoji**, **Kaomoji** or **Symbols**.
2. **Search or browse** — Type a word like “heart” or “shrug”, or jump to a category.
3. **Click to copy** — Click any item — it is copied to your clipboard. Paste it anywhere with Ctrl+V (or long-press on a phone).

### Guide

#### Popular kaomoji

| Kaomoji | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| ¯\_(ツ)_/¯ | Shrug — “whatever” or “I don’t know” |
| (╯°□°）╯︵ ┻━┻ | Table flip — frustration |
| ┬─┬ノ( º _ ºノ) | Putting the table back — calming down |
| ( ͡° ͜ʖ ͡°) | Lenny face — cheeky or suggestive |
| ಠ_ಠ | Look of disapproval |
| ʕ•ᴥ•ʔ | Bear |
| (づ｡◕‿‿◕｡)づ | Sending a hug |
| m(_ _)m | A deep bow — thanks or sorry |

#### Emoji in HTML and code

Emoji are ordinary Unicode characters, so you can paste them straight into UTF-8 web pages, documents and source code. Where you need plain ASCII, use the **HTML entity** (😀 is `&#x1F600;`), the **CSS escape** (`\1F600`, for `content`), or the **JavaScript escape** (`\u{1F600}`) shown for every emoji in the details panel.

Some emoji are sequences of several code points — skin tones, flags and family emoji join characters with modifiers or a zero-width joiner — which is why their codes list more than one value.

### FAQ

**How do I copy and paste an emoji?**
Click it — it is copied straight away. Then paste with Ctrl+V on a computer, or long-press and choose Paste on a phone.

**What is a kaomoji?**
A kaomoji is a Japanese-style face made from text characters, read the right way up — like (^_^) or ¯\_(ツ)_/¯. They work anywhere text does, without emoji support.

**Why do some emoji look different on another phone?**
Each system — Apple, Google, Samsung, Microsoft — draws emoji in its own style. The character is the same; only the picture differs. Very new emoji may show as a box on older systems.

**Why do flags look like letters on Windows?**
Windows doesn’t include flag emoji, so it shows the two letters that make up the flag (like IN for India). They still copy correctly and appear as flags on phones and Macs.

**Is anything I type sent anywhere?**
No. Search, copying and your recent items all stay in your browser.

## GST Invoice Generator

URL: https://justtools.online/business-tools/gst-invoice-generator/
Category: Business Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-07

Make GST tax invoices in your browser: CGST, SGST or IGST worked out, GSTIN check, HSN summary and a UPI QR code. Download a PDF — free, no sign-up.

### At a glance

- Makes **tax invoices**, **bills of supply**, **proforma invoices** and **quotations** as a ready-to-send A4 PDF with real, searchable text.
- Charges **CGST + SGST** when the place of supply is in your state and **IGST** when it isn’t — per item, rounded to the paisa, with an **HSN/SAC-wise tax summary**.
- **Checks GSTINs** (format, state code and check digit) and fills in the state and PAN from them.
- Adds a **UPI QR code** for the exact amount, your bank details, logo, signature, the amount in words and an optional **original, duplicate and triplicate** set.
- Handles **discounts**, **GST-inclusive prices**, round-off and numbering (INV-007 → INV-008). Long item lists continue onto more pages.

- **GSTIN check**: Typos in a GSTIN are caught by its check digit before the invoice goes out.
- **Get paid faster**: A UPI QR code for the invoice amount lets customers pay from any UPI app.
- **Looks professional**: Your logo, colours and signature on a clean layout with the totals in words.

### How to make a GST invoice

1. **Enter your business details** — Add your name, address, GSTIN, bank and UPI ID. They are saved for your next invoice.
2. **Add the customer** — Type the buyer’s details and GSTIN (if registered), or pick a saved customer. The place of supply sets CGST/SGST or IGST.
3. **Add items** — Enter each item with its HSN/SAC code, quantity, rate, discount and GST rate. Totals update as you type.
4. **Download the PDF** — Check the preview and press **Download PDF**. Use **Next invoice** to start the next one with the following number.

### Guide

#### What a GST tax invoice must show

- Your name, address and **GSTIN**, and a **unique invoice number** (up to 16 characters) and date.
- The buyer’s name and address, and their GSTIN if they are registered.
- The **place of supply** (state name and code), for supplies between states.
- For each item: description, **HSN or SAC code**, quantity and unit, value, discount and the **taxable value**.
- The GST rate and amount — **CGST and SGST**, or **IGST** — and the invoice total.
- Whether tax is payable on **reverse charge**, and the signature of the supplier or an authorised person.

#### CGST, SGST or IGST?

| Supply | Tax charged | Example at 18% |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Within the same state (intra-state) | CGST + SGST, half each | 9% CGST + 9% SGST |
| Within a union territory without a legislature | CGST + UTGST, half each | 9% CGST + 9% UTGST |
| To another state (inter-state) | IGST | 18% IGST |

### FAQ

**Is this GST invoice generator free?**
Yes — free, with no sign-up, no watermark and no limit on invoices.

**Does it work offline?**
Yes. Once the page has loaded, invoices are made entirely in your browser, so you can keep working without internet. Your details are saved on this device only.

**When is IGST charged instead of CGST and SGST?**
When the place of supply is in a different state from yours. Within your state, the GST rate is split equally into CGST and SGST. The invoice switches automatically when you choose the customer’s state.

**What is a bill of supply?**
An invoice without GST, issued by composition dealers or for exempt goods and services. Choose **Bill of Supply** and no tax is charged or shown.

**Can I add a UPI QR code to the invoice?**
Yes. Enter your UPI ID under Payment; the PDF gets a QR code for the exact invoice amount that any UPI app can scan.

**Is my data safe?**
Nothing is uploaded. Your business details, customers and invoices stay in this browser — download a backup file to move them to another device.

**Does it make e-invoices with an IRN?**
No. E-invoicing (IRN and QR from the government portal) is required only above a turnover limit and needs the IRP portal. This tool makes regular GST invoices.

## Salary Slip Generator

URL: https://justtools.online/business-tools/salary-slip-generator/
Category: Business Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-07

Make monthly salary slips as PDF: earnings, PF, ESI, professional tax and TDS worked out, loss of pay and net pay in words. Free, private, no sign-up.

### At a glance

- Makes a one-page **A4 payslip PDF** with your company logo, employee details, earnings, deductions and **net pay in figures and words**.
- Works out **employee PF** (12% of Basic + DA, with the optional ₹15,000 wage ceiling) and **ESI** (0.75% while the monthly gross is ₹21,000 or less, rounded up).
- Adds **professional tax**, **TDS** and any other deductions such as loans or advances.
- Handles **loss of pay**: earnings are paid for the days worked, with monthly and earned amounts shown side by side.
- Can show the **employer’s PF and ESI** and the month’s cost to company, and split a monthly gross into Basic, HRA and special allowance.
- Everything is saved only in this browser; press **Next month** to make the following payslip.

### Features

- **Statutory deductions**: PF and ESI follow the current rates and limits, so you don’t calculate them by hand.
- **Loss of pay**: Enter the paid days; every earning is pro-rated automatically.
- **Your branding**: Company logo, address and colours on a clean, printable layout.
- **Month to month**: Save the structure once and create next month’s payslip in a click.
- **Net pay in words**: Written the Indian way — lakh and crore, rupees and paise.
- **Private**: Salary details never leave your device; nothing is uploaded or stored online.

### How to make a salary slip

1. **Enter company and employee** — Add the company name and logo, then the employee’s name, ID, designation, PAN, UAN and bank.
2. **Set the salary** — Enter each earning for a full month — or type the monthly gross and press **Split**.
3. **Check deductions** — PF and ESI are worked out; add professional tax, TDS and any other deductions, and the paid days.
4. **Download** — Press **Download PDF**. Next month, press **Next month** and change only what’s different.

### Guide

#### How the deductions are calculated

| Deduction | Rule used |
| --- | --- |
| Provident fund (PF) | 12% of Basic + DA; with the wage ceiling, on at most ₹15,000 (₹1,800 a month) |
| Employer PF | Another 12%: 8.33% to the pension scheme (on up to ₹15,000) and the rest to PF |
| ESI (employee) | 0.75% of gross pay when the monthly gross is ₹21,000 or less, rounded up to the rupee |
| ESI (employer) | 3.25% of gross pay on the same condition |
| Professional tax | Set by each state, up to ₹2,500 a year — enter your state’s amount |
| TDS | Income tax deducted at source, as worked out for the employee’s regime |

#### Loss of pay

When an employee is paid for fewer days than the month has, each earning is reduced in proportion: **earned = monthly amount × paid days ÷ days in the month**. For example, ₹45,000 Basic with 27 of 30 days paid gives ₹40,500. PF and ESI are then worked out on the reduced pay.

### FAQ

**Is this salary slip generator free?**
Yes — free, without sign-up or watermark, for as many employees and months as you like.

**How is PF calculated on a payslip?**
The employee contributes 12% of Basic + DA. Most employers apply it on wages of at most ₹15,000, which caps it at ₹1,800 a month; switch the ceiling off to use the full Basic.

**When is ESI deducted?**
When the employee’s gross pay is ₹21,000 a month or less. The employee pays 0.75% and the employer 3.25%, both rounded up to the next rupee.

**Is a computer-generated payslip valid?**
Yes. Payslips from payroll software are routinely accepted without a signature; the PDF says it is computer-generated. Some banks or landlords may ask for a stamped copy or a salary certificate.

**Where is my data stored?**
Only in this browser. Download a backup file to keep the details or move them to another computer.

### FAQ

**Are all the bingo cards different?**
Yes. Every card in a set is checked against the others, so no two are alike. Each has its own number for checking claims.

**How do Tambola tickets work?**
Each ticket has 3 rows and 9 columns with 15 numbers — 5 in each row. The first column holds 1–9, the next 10–19 and so on up to 80–90. Six tickets make a strip that uses every number from 1 to 90 once.

**Can it call the numbers for me?**
Yes. Open **Call numbers** and press **Call next** — or switch on automatic calling. Each number is shown large and read aloud by your device’s voice, with traditional Tambola calls if you like.

**How do I check if a card has won?**
Under **Check a card**, type the number printed on the card. You will see the card with every called number marked and which prizes it has won.

**How many words do I need for word bingo?**
24 for a 5×5 card with a free centre (25 without), 16 for 4×4, and 8 for 3×3 with a free centre. Use more words than that so the cards differ more.

**Is it free to print?**
Yes — free, with no sign-up and no watermark, for as many cards as you need.

## Coin Flip

URL: https://justtools.online/games/coin-flip/
Category: Games
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-07

Flip a coin online: a fair 50/50 heads or tails toss with a 3D coin. Flip up to 10 coins, play best of 3, use custom sides and see your stats. Free.

### At a glance

- Every toss is a **fair 50/50** result from your browser’s cryptographic random number generator.
- A realistic **3D coin** in gold, silver or rupee style — with Heads/Tails, Yes/No, **Bat/Bowl for a cricket toss**, or your own two words or pictures.
- Flip **up to 10 coins** at once, or play a **best of 3, 5 or 7** series.
- **Statistics**: heads and tails counts and percentages, the current and longest streak, and quick runs of 10, 100 or 1,000 flips.
- Streaks are more common than people expect: in 100 flips there is a **54.6% chance** of six or more heads in a row somewhere.

### Features

- **Truly random**: Not a pattern or a timer — each result uses the same randomness that protects passwords and encryption.
- **Settle it fairly**: Best-of series for bigger decisions, so one lucky toss doesn’t decide everything.
- **Your own choices**: Put names, foods or photos on the two sides and let the coin choose.
- **See probability at work**: Run 1,000 flips in a click and watch the split settle near 50%.
- **Feels real**: A spinning 3D coin, a clink when it lands and a buzz on phones.
- **Works anywhere**: Phones, tablets and computers — press Space to flip on a keyboard.

### How to flip a coin online

1. **Choose the sides** — Keep Heads/Tails, pick Yes/No or Bat/Bowl, or type your own two options.
2. **Flip** — Press **Flip the coin** (or Space). The coin spins and lands on a random side.
3. **Read the result** — The result appears under the coin and is added to your statistics.

### Guide

#### Chances of streaks

| Event | Chance |
| --- | --- |
| Heads on one flip | 1 in 2 (50%) |
| Heads three times in a row | 1 in 8 (12.5%) |
| Heads five times in a row | 1 in 32 (3.1%) |
| Heads ten times in a row | 1 in 1,024 (0.1%) |
| Three heads in a row somewhere in 10 flips | 50.8% |
| Six heads in a row somewhere in 100 flips | 54.6% |

#### Is the next flip “due”?

No. A fair coin has no memory: after five heads in a row, the next flip is still exactly 50/50. Believing otherwise is called the **gambler’s fallacy**. What does happen is that over thousands of flips the *percentage* of heads drifts towards 50% — try the 1,000-flip button to see it.

### FAQ

**Is this coin flip really random?**
Yes. Each result comes from your browser’s cryptographic random number generator (crypto.getRandomValues), so heads and tails are equally likely and no flip depends on the one before.

**Can I use it for a cricket toss?**
Yes. Choose **Bat / Bowl** and let the coin decide — or keep Heads/Tails and have the captains call it.

**Is a real coin toss 50/50?**
Almost. A 2023 study by Bartoš and colleagues, with 350,757 real flips, found coins land on the side they started on slightly more often — about 50.8% of the time. This virtual coin has no starting side, so it is exactly 50/50.

**Can I flip more than one coin?**
Yes, up to 10 at once — the result shows how many landed heads and tails. For quick experiments, add 10, 100 or 1,000 flips to the statistics.

**What does best of 3 mean?**
The first side to win two flips wins (three for best of 5, four for best of 7). It makes a decision feel fairer than a single toss.

## ATS Resume Checker

URL: https://justtools.online/career-tools/ats-resume-checker/
Category: Career Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-07

Free ATS resume checker: see what applicant tracking systems read from your PDF or Word resume, get a score with clear fixes, and match it to any job.

### At a glance

- Reads your **PDF or Word (.docx)** resume the way ATS software does and shows the **text it extracts** and the **details it fills in** — name, email, phone, location, LinkedIn, experience, education and skills.
- **40+ checks** in four groups — readability, contact details, sections and dates, and content — with an **ATS score out of 100** and a plain-English fix for every problem.
- Finds what trips parsers up: **two-column layouts, layout tables, text boxes, headers and footers, icon fonts, spaced-out headings, scanned pages** and garbled text.
- **Job match**: paste a job description to see which **hard skills, soft skills and keywords** you’re missing, and whether you meet the job title, years of experience and degree it asks for.
- Recognises **350+ skills** in the spellings people use (Power BI / PowerBI, Node.js / NodeJS) and the headings Indian resumes use, such as Educational Qualifications and Positions of Responsibility.
- Private: your resume is read **in your browser** and never uploaded. Free, with no sign-up and no limit on checks.

### Features

- **See what the ATS sees**: The extracted text and parsed fields show exactly where a layout scrambles or hides your details.
- **Fixes, not just a score**: Every warning says why it matters and what to change, most important first.
- **Keyword match**: Skills and keywords from any job ad, counted in the job and in your resume.
- **Made for Indian resumes**: Understands Indian formats and flags Aadhaar or PAN numbers, date of birth and other personal details.
- **Checks the real file**: Text boxes, tables, headers and image-only pages only show up in the PDF or Word file itself — so that is what it reads.
- **Private**: No upload and no account: your resume never leaves your device.

### How to check your resume for ATS

1. **Add your resume** — Drop the PDF or Word file you send to employers, or paste the text.
2. **Read the score and fixes** — Start with critical problems and warnings — each one says what to change.
3. **Look at the ATS view** — See the text and details the ATS extracts. Jumbled lines mean the layout needs simplifying.
4. **Match a job** — Paste the job description to find missing skills and keywords, then add the ones you really have.

### Guide

#### What ATS software needs from a resume

| Check | Why it matters |
| --- | --- |
| Real, readable text | Scanned or image-only resumes come through empty. |
| A simple layout | Columns, tables and text boxes can mix up or hide text. |
| Standard headings | Experience, Education and Skills tell the ATS where each detail belongs. |
| Contact details in the page | Some ATS ignore Word headers and footers. |
| Dates on every role | They are used to work out your years of experience. |
| Keywords from the job | Recruiters search and rank candidates by skills and job titles. |

#### ATS myths

- **“An ATS rejects most resumes automatically.”** Most systems only reject through screening questions you answer while applying, such as location or notice period. Otherwise recruiters decide — but they find candidates by searching what the ATS extracted, so a resume it reads badly rarely comes up.
- **“You need a special ATS template.”** A clean, single-column PDF or Word file with standard headings works with every major ATS. Elaborate designs are what cause problems.
- **“Add as many keywords as you can.”** A person reads the resume after the search. Add only skills you really have, and show them in results.
- **“PDFs aren’t ATS-friendly.”** Modern ATS read text-based PDFs well. Scanned PDFs and image-heavy designs are the problem — this checker shows which kind yours is.

### FAQ

**What is an ATS score?**
There is no single official score — every ATS (Workday, Taleo, Greenhouse, Naukri RMS and others) works a little differently. This score measures what they all depend on: whether the text can be read, whether your details and sections are recognised, and how clearly your achievements are written.

**Is my resume uploaded anywhere?**
No. The file is opened and checked by your browser; nothing is sent to a server, and it is gone when you close the page.

**What is a good ATS score?**
75 or more means software reads your resume well and the content is solid; 90 or more is excellent. More important than the number: fix every critical problem and warning.

**Why is my job match low?**
The match compares your resume with the skills and keywords in that job ad. Add the ones you really have — in your skills and in bullets that show them in use — with the same spelling as the job. Don’t add skills you don’t have.

**Are two-column resumes bad for ATS?**
Modern systems often cope, but many read across the page and mix the columns together. If the ATS view shows jumbled lines, switch to one column — the free [Resume Builder](https://justtools.online/career-tools/resume-builder/) makes one.

**Should I send a PDF or a Word file?**
Either works. Send what the job asks for; otherwise a text-based PDF keeps your layout exactly. Use .docx when a portal or recruiter asks for Word, and avoid scanned PDFs, images and old .doc files.

### How to shorten a URL

2. **Choose options** — Pick spoo.me or da.gd, and add a password, click limit, expiry or UTM tags if you need them.

4. **Track clicks** — Open **Click stats** to see how many people opened a spoo.me link and where they came from.

### Guide

#### spoo.me or da.gd?

|  | spoo.me | da.gd |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Example | spoo.me/diwali-sale | da.gd/sale26 |
| Custom ending | 3–16 characters | Up to 10 characters |
| Password, click limit, expiry | Yes | No |
| Click statistics | Yes (public unless password-protected) | No |
| Open source | Yes | Yes |

#### Using short links safely

- **Check before you click.** A short link hides where it goes — paste it into **Check a link** to see the destination first.
- **Don’t shorten private links.** Anyone who has the short link can open it, so keep documents, payment and meeting links out of shorteners — or add a password.
- **Short links can’t be edited.** If the page moves you’ll need a new link, so double-check the long URL before you share it widely.
- **Prefer https:// pages.** Browsers warn visitors about pages that aren’t encrypted.

### FAQ

**Is this URL shortener free?**
Yes. Shortening, custom endings, QR codes, bulk shortening and click statistics are free, with no sign-up.

**How long do the short links last?**
They have no expiry date unless you set one or a click limit. The services can remove links that break their rules, such as spam, phishing or malware.

**Can I edit or delete a short link?**
No. Links made without an account can’t be changed or deleted, so check the long URL before you share it. Removing a link from your list here only hides it in this browser.

**Who can see my click statistics?**
spoo.me statistics are public to anyone who knows the short link. Set a password to protect both the link and its statistics.

**Why are the links not on justtools.online?**
JustTools runs entirely in your browser and has no server to store links, so it uses free, open-source shortening services that work straight from the browser.

**How can I tell if a short link is safe?**
Use **Check a link**. It follows the link on da.gd’s server and shows every redirect and the final address, with warnings for bare IP addresses, look-alike domains and unencrypted pages. It can’t prove a site is safe, so read the final domain name carefully.

## Typing Speed Test

URL: https://justtools.online/education-tools/typing-speed-test/
Category: Education Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-07

Free typing speed test in English and Hindi: check your WPM and accuracy, practise with passages, and take an exam-style test with full and half mistakes.

### At a glance

- Measures speed the standard way — **5 characters = 1 word** — and shows **WPM, raw speed, accuracy, consistency** and **key depressions per hour**.
- Tests of **15, 30, 60 or 120 seconds**, **10 to 100 words**, a full **passage** or **your own text**, with optional punctuation and numbers.
- **English and Hindi** (Devanagari): type Hindi with any Hindi keyboard — Inscript, Remington or phonetic — and each syllable is checked as one character.
- **Exam practice**: type a passage for 2, 5, 10 or 15 minutes in a plain box, then get **gross and net speed, error percentage, and full and half mistakes**, word by word.
- Results show a **speed chart**, the words you got wrong and the **characters you miss most**, and keep your **personal best** for each test on this device.
- Copy-paste is blocked in the typing box, so every result is real typing.

### Features

- **Live feedback**: Every character turns green or red as you type, with a caret that follows you.
- **Hindi typing test**: Practise Hindi passages and common words with your own Hindi keyboard layout.
- **Exam-style scoring**: Full and half mistakes, error rate and net speed, the way many government typing tests count them.
- **Know your weak keys**: See the words and characters you mistype most, and practise them.
- **Personal bests**: Each test type keeps its own best score and recent results.
- **Your own text**: Paste a paragraph from your syllabus or work and practise with it.

### How to take the typing test

1. **Choose a test** — Pick Time, Words, Passage, Exam practice or Custom, and English or Hindi.
2. **Start typing** — Click the text and type — the timer starts with your first key. Press space after each word.
3. **Read your result** — See your WPM, accuracy, speed chart and mistakes. Press **Next test** or Esc to go again.

### Guide

#### What is a good typing speed?

| Speed | Level |
| --- | --- |
| Under 20 WPM | Beginner — focus on accuracy and finger position |
| 20–35 WPM | Learning — enough for everyday use |
| 35–50 WPM | Average — what many office jobs expect |
| 50–70 WPM | Fast |
| 70 WPM and above | Very fast — professional typists and transcribers |

#### How the scores are worked out

- **WPM** = characters of correctly typed words (with their spaces) ÷ 5 ÷ minutes.
- **Raw speed** counts everything you typed, mistakes included.
- **Accuracy** = keys pressed correctly ÷ all keys pressed.
- **Key depressions per hour** = characters typed per minute × 60 — the measure many Indian recruitment typing tests quote.
- **Exam practice**: full mistakes are left-out, extra or wrong words; half mistakes are wrong capitals, punctuation, or words joined or split. Error rate = (full + half ÷ 2) ÷ words reached × 100.

### FAQ

**How is typing speed calculated?**
Speed is measured in words per minute, where one word is any 5 characters including spaces. Only words typed correctly count towards WPM; raw speed counts all your typing.

**Can I take a Hindi typing test?**
Yes. Choose हिंदी and type with your device’s Hindi keyboard — Inscript, Remington (with a Hindi font input tool) or phonetic. Common words and passages are available, and the exam practice mode works in Hindi too.

**What speed do government exams ask for?**
It depends on the exam and post, so always check the latest notification. For example, SSC CHSL has asked for 35 words per minute in English (about 10,500 key depressions per hour) and 30 words per minute in Hindi (about 9,000 key depressions per hour).

**How can I type faster?**
Keep your fingers on the home row, look at the screen instead of the keyboard and practise for 10–15 minutes every day. Aim for accuracy first — speed follows once you stop correcting mistakes.

**Are my results saved?**
Your recent results and personal bests are saved only in this browser. Nothing you type is sent anywhere.

- Copy the result as **SVG code**, a compact **data URI**, **CSS background**, **<img> tag**, **base64** or a **React (JSX) component**.

- **Ready-to-paste code**: Data URI, CSS, <img> and React component outputs with one-click copy.

### How to optimise an SVG

2. **Check the preview** — Compare the original and optimised image and the size saved.
3. **Adjust if needed** — Lower the precision for smaller files, or raise it if shapes change. Turn on **Keep IDs** if your CSS or scripts use them.
4. **Download or copy** — Download the file (or all files as a ZIP), or copy it as code, a data URI or a React component.

### Guide

#### Which options to use

| Situation | Setting |
| --- | --- |
| Icons for a website | Precision 2–3, Make responsive on |
| Logos and detailed illustrations | Precision 3–4; check the pixel comparison |
| SVG styled or animated with CSS/JS | Keep IDs on |
| SVG pasted into HTML | Remove xmlns on |
| SVG from an unknown source | Remove scripts on (the default) |
| Code you will edit by hand | Pretty print on |

### FAQ

**Does optimising change how my SVG looks?**
Usually not. The tool draws both versions and compares their pixels; if more than a tiny fraction differ, it tells you so you can raise the precision or turn off a step.

**Are my files uploaded?**
No. SVGO runs in your browser and the files never leave your device.

**What is SVGO?**
SVGO (SVG Optimizer) is the widely used open-source tool that removes unnecessary data from SVG files. This page runs it for you with clear options and previews.

**Should I use a data URI or base64?**
Use the URL-encoded data URI for CSS and HTML — it is usually smaller than base64 and compresses better. Use base64 only where a tool requires it.

**Why is the title kept?**
Screen readers read an SVG’s <title>, so it is kept by default. Switch on **Remove <title>** if the image is purely decorative.

## Sudoku

URL: https://justtools.online/games/sudoku/
Category: Games
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-07

Play free Sudoku online: easy to expert puzzles with one solution, notes, hints that explain the logic, a daily puzzle, printable PDFs and a solver.

### At a glance

- Four levels — **Easy, Medium, Hard and Expert** — graded by the techniques a person needs, from simple singles to **pairs, pointing pairs, X-Wing and XY-Wing**.
- Every puzzle is newly made, has **exactly one solution** and can be solved by **logic alone**, without guessing.
- **Hints explain the next step** — which digit goes where and why — and point out a wrong digit first if you have one.
- Pencil **notes**, automatic notes, undo, mistake highlighting, a timer with pause, and your **best time** for each level.

- **Print and play**: Make a PDF of new puzzles with answers for travel, classrooms or the newspaper habit.
- **Your game is kept**: Close the tab and carry on later; the game is saved in this browser.

### How to play Sudoku

1. **Know the rule** — Fill every row, every column and every 3×3 box with the digits 1 to 9, each exactly once.
2. **Pick a cell** — Tap a cell (or use the arrow keys) and tap a number — or type it.
3. **Use notes** — Switch on **Notes** to pencil in the digits a cell could be, or press **Auto notes**.
4. **Get unstuck** — Press **Hint** to see the next logical step and why it works.

### Guide

#### Sudoku techniques, from easy to expert

| Technique | Level | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Naked single | Easy | A cell where only one digit is still possible. |
| Hidden single | Easy | A digit that fits in only one cell of a row, column or box. |
| Pointing pair / box-line | Hard | A digit locked into one line of a box (or one box of a line) can be removed elsewhere. |
| Naked / hidden pair and triple | Hard | Two or three cells that share the same two or three digits rule those digits out of the rest of the unit. |
| X-Wing | Expert | A digit limited to the same two columns in two rows can be removed from the rest of those columns. |
| XY-Wing | Expert | Three two-digit cells that force a digit out of any cell that sees both ends. |

### FAQ

**Is this Sudoku free?**
Yes — unlimited puzzles, hints, the daily puzzle and printable PDFs, with no sign-up.

**Does every puzzle have one solution?**
Yes. Each puzzle is checked by a solver to have exactly one solution, and a second, human-style solver makes sure it can be finished by logic alone.

**What makes a Sudoku hard?**
Not the number of clues but the techniques needed. Easy and medium puzzles need only singles; hard ones need pairs or pointing pairs; expert ones need an X-Wing or XY-Wing.

**Can I solve a Sudoku from the newspaper?**
Yes. Open **Solve my puzzle**, type or paste the clues, and see the solution, whether it has exactly one solution and how hard it is — or play it here with hints.

**Is my game saved?**
Yes, in this browser: the game in progress, your settings and your best times. Nothing is uploaded.

## Pixel-Perfect Screen Ruler

URL: https://justtools.online/developer-tools/screen-ruler/
Category: Developer Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-08

Free online screen ruler: a real-size cm and inch ruler calibrated with a bank card, plus pixel-perfect measuring of screenshots with zoom and smart edges.

### At a glance

- A **real-size ruler** in **cm/mm, inches or pixels**, drawn pixel-perfect at your screen’s resolution — horizontal or vertical, and full screen for the longest ruler.
- **Calibrate** once with a **bank, credit or Aadhaar PVC card** (85.60 mm), an A4 or Letter sheet, a real ruler or your screen size. The calibration is saved and **adjusts itself when you zoom the browser**.
- Two draggable markers measure any length in mm, cm, inches, CSS pixels, device pixels and points.
- **Measure screenshots pixel by pixel**: zoom up to 6400% with a pixel grid, a magnifier showing the colour under the cursor, and lines that snap to pixel edges.
- **Smart measure**: click inside a button, box or gap to get its exact width and height. Set the screenshot scale (1×, 2×, 3×) to read sizes as CSS uses them.
- Paste a screenshot or **capture the screen** directly, then save an annotated PNG — everything stays in your browser.

### Features

- **True to size**: After a 30-second calibration, a centimetre on screen is a real centimetre.
- **Crisp ticks**: Every mark is drawn on whole device pixels, so lines stay sharp on any display.
- **Smart measure**: One click finds the edges of a button, card or gap and gives its width and height.
- **Magnifier and colour**: See the pixels around the cursor and their hex colour while you measure.
- **Screen facts**: Device pixel ratio, physical resolution, pixels per inch and screen diagonal.
- **Private**: Screenshots and captures never leave your device.

### How to use the screen ruler

1. **Calibrate** — Open **Calibrate**, hold a bank card against the screen and match the box to it — once per screen.
2. **Measure with the ruler** — Hold an object against the screen and drag the two markers to its ends.
3. **Measure a screenshot** — Paste or capture a screenshot, choose **Smart** and click an element — or drag lines and boxes.
4. **Save** — Copy the list of measurements or save the screenshot with them drawn on.

### Guide

#### Objects to calibrate with

| Object | Size |
| --- | --- |
| Bank, credit or debit card, Aadhaar PVC card | 85.60 × 53.98 mm (3.37 × 2.125 in) |
| A4 sheet | 210 × 297 mm |
| US Letter sheet | 8.5 × 11 in (215.9 × 279.4 mm) |

#### Pixels, explained

- **CSS pixel**: the unit web pages use. Browsers treat 96 CSS pixels as one inch, but on a real screen that is only a convention.
- **Device pixel**: one dot of the display. High-resolution screens have 2 or 3 device pixels per CSS pixel.
- **Device pixel ratio**: device pixels per CSS pixel — it also changes when you zoom the browser.
- **PPI (pixels per inch)**: how densely the screen packs its device pixels; calibration measures it for you.

### FAQ

**Is this ruler actual size?**
Yes, once you calibrate it. Browsers assume 96 pixels per inch, but real screens differ, so an uncalibrated on-screen centimetre can be noticeably off. Calibrate once with a bank card and the ruler matches real centimetres and inches.

**What size is a bank card?**
85.60 × 53.98 mm (3.37 × 2.125 inches) — the ISO/IEC 7810 ID-1 size used by bank, credit and debit cards and the Aadhaar PVC card. That makes a card the easiest thing to calibrate with.

**Can I measure something on my screen, like a window or an image?**
Yes. Take a screenshot (Win+Shift+S on Windows, Cmd+Shift+4 on a Mac) and paste it into **Measure a screenshot**, or press **Capture the screen**. Then click an element with **Smart**, or drag lines and boxes, to get sizes in pixels.

**Why do my screenshot measurements look twice as big?**
On high-resolution screens a screenshot has 2 or 3 image pixels for every CSS pixel. Set **Screenshot scale** to 2× or 3× to see the sizes as CSS and design tools use them.

**Does the calibration survive browser zoom?**
Yes. Zooming changes the device pixel ratio, and the ruler rescales itself to stay true to size. Calibrate again if you move the window to a different monitor.

**Does it work on phones?**
The ruler and screenshot measuring work on phones and tablets; calibrate with a card first. Capturing the screen directly needs a desktop browser.

## Regex Tester

URL: https://justtools.online/developer-tools/regex-tester/
Category: Developer Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-08

Free online regex tester: live match highlighting, groups, replace, a plain-English explanation, unit tests and code for Python, PHP, Java, C# and Go.

### At a glance

- Tests **JavaScript (ECMAScript) regular expressions** live as you type, with all six flags: **g, i, m, s, u and y**.
- Every **match and capture group** — numbered and named — is highlighted and listed with its position.
- A **plain-English explanation** of each part of the pattern: classes, quantifiers, groups, lookarounds and backreferences.
- **Replace** with $1, $<name> and $&, **list** matches with a template (handy for pulling data into CSV), and **unit tests** of strings that should and shouldn’t match.
- **Code** for JavaScript, Python, PHP, Java, C# and Go, with named groups, flags and replacements rewritten for each language.
- Patterns run in a separate worker and are **stopped after 1.5 seconds**, so a runaway (catastrophic backtracking) pattern can’t freeze the page. **24 ready-made patterns**, including Indian PAN, GSTIN, IFSC, PIN code, mobile and vehicle numbers.

### Features

- **Live highlighting**: Matches light up in your text as you type, alternating colours so neighbours stand apart.
- **Explained in English**: Each token of the pattern is described, indented by group, so you can read any regex.
- **Replace and extract**: Preview replacements and turn matches into lists or CSV lines in one step.
- **Unit tests**: Keep strings that must and mustn’t match beside the pattern and see which fail.
- **Safe to experiment**: A slow pattern is stopped automatically instead of hanging your browser tab.
- **Share a link**: The pattern, flags and text travel in the link itself — nothing is stored on a server.

### How to test a regular expression

1. **Write the pattern** — Type it between the slashes and switch on the flags you need — g to find every match.
2. **Add your text** — Paste the text to search; matches are highlighted and listed with their groups.
3. **Read the explanation** — Check what each part of the pattern does, and fix anything unexpected.
4. **Replace, test or copy code** — Use the tabs to preview a replacement, extract matches, run tests or copy code for your language.

### Guide

#### Regex quick reference

| Pattern | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| . | Any character except a line break (any at all with the s flag) |
| \d  \w  \s | A digit, a word character, whitespace (capitals for the opposite) |
| [abc]  [^abc]  [a-z] | One of a, b or c · anything else · a range |
| *  +  ?  {2,5} | 0 or more · 1 or more · optional · 2 to 5 times (add ? for as few as possible) |
| (…)  (?<name>…)  (?:…) | Capture group · named group · group without capturing |
| ^  $  \b | Start · end (of a line with the m flag) · word boundary |
| (?=…)  (?!…)  (?<=…)  (?<!…) | Followed by · not followed by · preceded by · not preceded by |
| \1  \k<name> | The same text a group matched |

#### Regex for Indian data

| What | Pattern |
| --- | --- |
| Mobile number | (?:\+91[\s-]?|0)?[6-9]\d{4}[\s-]?\d{5} |
| PAN | [A-Z]{5}\d{4}[A-Z] |
| GSTIN | \d{2}[A-Z]{5}\d{4}[A-Z][1-9A-Z]Z[0-9A-Z] |
| IFSC | [A-Z]{4}0[A-Z0-9]{6} |
| PIN code | [1-9]\d{2}\s?\d{3} |

### FAQ

**Which regex flavour does this use?**
JavaScript (ECMAScript), the engine built into your browser — the same one Node.js uses. The Code tab rewrites the pattern for Python, PHP, Java, C# and Go, and warns when something (such as lookbehind in Go) isn’t supported there.

**Why does my regex find only one match?**
Without the g (global) flag, a regular expression stops at the first match. Switch on g to find them all.

**What is catastrophic backtracking?**
Some patterns, usually with nested quantifiers like (a+)+ or (.*)*, can take exponentially long on text that almost matches. This tester runs patterns separately and stops them after 1.5 seconds, then tells you to make the pattern more specific.

**How do I validate a whole value, not just part of it?**
Anchor the pattern with ^ at the start and $ at the end, e.g. ^[A-Z]{5}\d{4}[A-Z]$ for a PAN. In the Tests tab, “The whole line must match” does this for you.

**Is my text sent anywhere?**
No. Everything runs in your browser. A shared link carries the pattern, flags and up to 2,000 characters of text inside the link itself.

## Hex to ASCII Converter

URL: https://justtools.online/developer-tools/hex-to-ascii/
Category: Developer Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-08

Convert hex to ASCII or UTF-8 text and text to hex as you type. Reads 0x, \x and spaced hex, flags bad bytes and shows a hex dump. Free, private, no upload.

### At a glance

- Converts **hex to text** and **text to hex** live, with text read as **UTF-8**, **Latin-1 (ISO-8859-1)** or **7-bit ASCII** — Hindi, ₹ and emoji round-trip in UTF-8.
- Reads hex however it’s written: `48 65 6C`, `48656c`, `0x48,0x65`, `\x48\x65`, `%48%65`, `48:65:6c` or `48h 65h`.
- Anything that isn’t a valid byte is listed with its position and skipped, instead of silently breaking the result.
- Text → hex output can use spaces, commas, new lines or no separator, `0x` or `\x` prefixes, and upper- or lowercase digits.
- Shows each character’s **code point and bytes**, a classic **hex dump** (offset, bytes, ASCII) and the same bytes in binary, decimal, octal and Base64.
- Runs entirely in your browser — nothing you paste or open is uploaded.

### Features

- **Any hex format**: Spaces, colons, commas, 0x, \x, URL-style %XX or one long string — paste it as it is.
- **UTF-8 aware**: Multi-byte characters like नमस्ते, ₹ and 👋 decode correctly, and invalid bytes are pointed out.
- **Hex dump**: See bytes the way a hex editor shows them — offsets, 16 bytes per line and printable characters.
- **Character table**: Every character with its Unicode code point and the exact bytes it takes, in hex and decimal.
- **Files too**: Open any file to see its hex, or download decoded hex back as a file — images and PDFs are recognised.
- **Decimal and octal**: Switch to decimal byte values (72 101 108…) or octal, both ways.

### How to convert hex to ASCII text

1. **Choose the direction** — Pick **Hex → Text** to decode, or **Text → Hex** to encode.
2. **Paste your input** — Paste the hex (any format) or type the text. The result appears as you type.
3. **Check the encoding** — Keep **UTF-8** for modern data; switch to **Latin-1** if accented letters look wrong.
4. **Copy the result** — Copy it, swap it back to check the round trip, or open **Hex dump** and **Characters** for detail.

### Guide

#### How hex becomes text

Computers store text as bytes, and hexadecimal is a compact way to write a byte: two digits from **00 to FF** (0 to 255). An encoding maps bytes to characters — in ASCII, **48** is “H”, **65** is “e” and **20** is a space, so `48 65 6C 6C 6F` reads “Hello”.

ASCII covers only English letters, digits and symbols (bytes 00–7F). **UTF-8** keeps ASCII as it is and uses 2–4 bytes for everything else: “₹” is `E2 82 B9` and “न” is `E0 A4 A8`. That’s why one Hindi character can turn into six hex digits.

#### Common ASCII values

| Character | Hex | Decimal | Binary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Space | 20 | 32 | 00100000 |
| 0 | 30 | 48 | 00110000 |
| A | 41 | 65 | 01000001 |
| a | 61 | 97 | 01100001 |
| Line feed (\n) | 0A | 10 | 00001010 |
| ~ | 7E | 126 | 01111110 |

### FAQ

**How do I convert hex to text?**
Choose **Hex → Text** and paste the hex. Spaces, 0x prefixes and separators don’t matter — every pair of digits is read as one byte and decoded as UTF-8 text.

**What is the difference between hex to ASCII and hex to UTF-8?**
For bytes 00–7F they are identical. Bytes above 7F aren’t ASCII at all; UTF-8 reads them as parts of multi-byte characters (Hindi, ₹, emoji), while Latin-1 reads each as one Western European letter such as é.

**Why do I see � in the result?**
Those bytes aren’t valid text in the chosen encoding. Try **Latin-1**, or the data may not be text at all — the tool recognises common files like PNG and PDF so you can download them.

**Why does it say a value has an odd number of digits?**
A byte is exactly two hex digits. An unbroken string like `486` can’t be split into whole bytes, so a digit is probably missing or extra.

**Can I convert binary or decimal too?**
Yes — switch **Bytes as** to Binary, Decimal or Octal. There’s also a dedicated [Binary to Text Converter](https://justtools.online/developer-tools/binary-to-text/).

**Is my data uploaded?**
No. Conversion happens entirely in your browser, including files you open.

## Binary to Text Converter

URL: https://justtools.online/developer-tools/binary-to-text/
Category: Developer Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-08

Translate binary code to text and text to binary, live. Handles spaced or joined 8-bit bytes, UTF-8 Hindi and emoji, and flags bad digits. Free and private.

### At a glance

- Translates **binary to text** and **text to binary** as you type, reading 8 bits as one byte.
- Accepts bytes separated by spaces, commas or new lines, one long run of bits, `0b` prefixes and 7-bit groups such as `1001000`.
- Text is read as **UTF-8** by default, so Hindi, ₹ and emoji work; **ASCII** and **Latin-1** are one switch away.
- Digits other than 0 and 1, values above 255 and runs that aren’t a multiple of 8 bits are listed with their position.
- A character table shows each letter’s bits, hex and decimal values; a hex dump and Base64 are included.
- Runs entirely in your browser — nothing is uploaded.

### Features

- **Any spacing**: Spaced bytes, one long string of bits or one byte per line — all read the same.
- **Both directions**: Swap the result back in a click to check a round trip.
- **Learn the bits**: See which 8 bits make each character, with its code point and decimal value.
- **Clear mistakes**: A stray 2, a missing bit or a byte over 255 is pointed out instead of producing gibberish.
- **Output your way**: Spaces, commas, new lines or none, with or without leading zeros and 0b prefixes.
- **Unicode ready**: UTF-8 turns emoji and Indian scripts into the right multi-byte binary.

### How to convert binary to text

1. **Choose the direction** — Pick **Binary → Text** to decode, or **Text → Binary** to encode.
2. **Paste or type** — Paste the 0s and 1s, or type the text. The result appears instantly.
3. **Adjust the format** — For text → binary, choose the separator and whether to keep leading zeros.
4. **Copy it** — Copy the result, or open **Characters** to see the bits behind each letter.

### Guide

#### How binary code becomes letters

Each 0 or 1 is a **bit**, and 8 bits make a **byte** — a number from 0 to 255. Text encodings give each number a character: in ASCII, `01001000` is 72, which is “H”, and `01101001` is 105, which is “i”. So `01001000 01101001` spells “Hi”.

English letters fit in one byte. Hindi letters, the rupee sign and emoji need 2–4 bytes each in **UTF-8**, so “₹” becomes `11100010 10000010 10111001`.

#### Letters in binary

| Character | Binary | Decimal | Hex |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | 01000001 | 65 | 41 |
| Z | 01011010 | 90 | 5A |
| a | 01100001 | 97 | 61 |
| z | 01111010 | 122 | 7A |
| 0 | 00110000 | 48 | 30 |
| Space | 00100000 | 32 | 20 |

### FAQ

**How do I translate binary to English?**
Choose **Binary → Text** and paste the binary code. Each group of 8 bits is one character; spaces between groups are optional.

**How do I write my name in binary?**
Choose **Text → Binary** and type your name. Each letter becomes 8 bits — “A” is 01000001 and “a” is 01100001.

**Why does my binary give strange characters?**
Usually a bit is missing or extra, which shifts every byte after it. The tool flags runs that aren’t a multiple of 8 bits; with spaces between bytes, each byte is read on its own.

**Can it read 7-bit binary?**
Yes, when the groups are separated — `1001000 1101001` reads as “Hi”. Without spaces, bits are read 8 at a time.

**Does it work with hex?**
Switch **Bytes as** to Hex, or use the [Hex to ASCII Converter](https://justtools.online/developer-tools/hex-to-ascii/).

**Is anything uploaded?**
No. Everything is converted in your browser.

## HMAC Generator

URL: https://justtools.online/developer-tools/hmac-generator/
Category: Developer Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-08

Generate HMAC-SHA256, SHA-512, SHA-1 or MD5 in hex or Base64, and verify GitHub, Stripe, Slack, Shopify and Razorpay webhook signatures. Private, no upload.

### At a glance

- Computes **HMAC (RFC 2104)** with SHA-256, SHA-512, SHA-384, SHA-224, SHA-1, MD5, SHA3-256, SHA3-512, Keccak-256, BLAKE2b and RIPEMD-160 — checked against the RFC 2202 and RFC 4231 test vectors.
- Shows the result as **hex, uppercase hex, Base64 and Base64URL**, and takes the key and message as text, hex or Base64 — or a file of any size.
- Verifies webhook signatures exactly as **GitHub, Stripe, Slack, Shopify, Razorpay, Cashfree, Paddle and Standard Webhooks** (Svix, Clerk, Resend) compute them.
- When a signature doesn’t match, it tests the usual causes — wrong algorithm, a trailing line break, re-formatted JSON, spaces around the secret, a hex key typed as text — and offers the fix.
- Gives working code for Node.js, Python, PHP, Java, Go, C# and OpenSSL, with constant-time comparison for webhook checks.
- Keys, secrets and messages stay in your browser and are never saved.

### Features

- **Webhook debugger**: Paste the secret, the signature header and the raw body to see whether the request is genuine.
- **Explains mismatches**: Finds the one change that makes the signature match — so you know whether to fix the body, the secret or the algorithm.
- **Replay check**: Shows how old a webhook timestamp is and warns when providers would reject it as too old.
- **Every format**: Hex, HEX, Base64 and Base64URL side by side; compare with a signature pasted in any of them.
- **Key advice**: Warns about short or empty keys and generates a strong random key in one click.
- **Copy-paste code**: The same HMAC in seven languages, and a ready verify function for each webhook provider.

### How to generate an HMAC

1. **Pick the algorithm** — Choose **HMAC-SHA256** unless your API asks for another.
2. **Enter the secret key** — Type or paste the key, or create a random one. Switch to Hex or Base64 if the key is given that way.
3. **Enter the message** — Paste the exact text or payload to sign, or choose a file.
4. **Copy or compare** — Copy the HMAC in the format you need, or paste a signature to check it matches.

### Guide

#### What an HMAC proves

An HMAC is a hash mixed with a secret key. Anyone with the same key and message gets the same value, and without the key it can’t be forged — so it proves a message came from someone who knows the secret **and** wasn’t changed on the way.

That’s why payment gateways and platforms sign webhooks with it: your server recomputes the HMAC of the raw body with the shared secret and accepts the request only if it matches the signature header. Compare with a **constant-time** function (`timingSafeEqual`, `hmac.compare_digest`, `hash_equals`) so the check itself doesn’t leak the signature.

#### How popular webhooks are signed

| Provider | Header | Signed message | Output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GitHub | X-Hub-Signature-256 | body | sha256=hex |
| Stripe | Stripe-Signature | timestamp.body | t=…,v1=hex |
| Slack | X-Slack-Signature | v0:timestamp:body | v0=hex |
| Shopify | X-Shopify-Hmac-Sha256 | body | Base64 |
| Razorpay | X-Razorpay-Signature | body | hex |
| Razorpay checkout | razorpay_signature | order_id|payment_id | hex |
| Cashfree | x-webhook-signature | timestamp + body | Base64 |
| Standard Webhooks | webhook-signature | id.timestamp.body | v1,Base64 |

### FAQ

**How do I generate HMAC-SHA256?**
Keep **HMAC-SHA256** selected, enter the secret key and the message. The HMAC appears instantly in hex and Base64 — copy the one your API expects.

**Why doesn’t my webhook signature match?**
Almost always because the body was changed before hashing — parsed and re-serialised JSON, a trailing newline, or different line breaks. Sign the raw bytes exactly as received. The second most common cause is the wrong secret, such as an API key instead of the webhook secret. This tool checks these for you.

**Is HMAC the same as hashing with a salt?**
No. HMAC uses the key in a special two-pass construction that stays secure even with hashes like MD5 or SHA-1. Simply hashing key + message is open to length-extension attacks. For passwords, use bcrypt or Argon2 instead — see the [Bcrypt Generator & Checker](https://justtools.online/security-tools/bcrypt-generator/).

**How long should an HMAC key be?**
At least as long as the hash output — 32 random bytes for HMAC-SHA256. Keys longer than the block size (64 bytes for SHA-256) are hashed first, so they add nothing.

**Hex or Base64 — which should I use?**
They are the same bytes written differently. Use whatever the other side expects: GitHub, Stripe and Razorpay use hex; Shopify, Cashfree and Standard Webhooks use Base64.

**Are my keys sent anywhere?**
No. Everything is computed in your browser, and keys, secrets and messages are not saved — only your algorithm and provider choice are remembered.

## Bcrypt Generator & Checker

URL: https://justtools.online/security-tools/bcrypt-generator/
Category: Security Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-08

Generate bcrypt hashes with cost 4–16 and $2a/$2b/$2y prefixes, or check a password against a bcrypt hash. Explains each part. Runs in your browser only.

### At a glance

- Creates **bcrypt** hashes with a cost from 4 to 16 and the **$2b$**, **$2y$** (PHP, Laravel) or **$2a$** prefix, using a fresh 16-byte random salt each time.
- **Checks a password against a bcrypt hash** as you type — $2a$, $2b$, $2y$, ASCII $2x$ and Django’s bcrypt_sha256 hashes are supported.
- Breaks a hash into **version, cost, salt and checksum**, and recognises Argon2, SHA-crypt, phpass and plain MD5/SHA hashes pasted by mistake.
- Warns when a password is over **72 bytes** — bcrypt ignores the rest — and counts bytes, not characters, so Hindi and emoji are measured correctly.
- Measures how long a hash takes **on your device** and estimates other costs; hashing runs in a background thread so the page never freezes.
- Verified against the OpenBSD and jBCrypt test vectors. Passwords and hashes never leave your browser and are not saved.

### Features

- **Generate and check together**: Type the password once, make a hash, and click “Check it” to confirm it verifies.
- **Hash explained**: Colour-coded prefix, cost, salt and checksum, with the salt shown as bytes.
- **Typing slips**: When a password doesn’t match, it checks for Caps Lock and stray spaces.
- **Real timings**: See how long cost 10 to 14 takes on this device before choosing one for your server.
- **Cut-off hashes caught**: A hash shorter than 60 characters usually means the database column is too small — it tells you so.
- **Private**: Nothing is uploaded or stored; close the tab and it’s gone.

### How to generate or check a bcrypt hash

1. **Type the password** — Enter it once at the top — both sides use it.
2. **Generate** — Pick a **cost** (12 is a good default) and a prefix, then press **Generate hash** and copy it.
3. **Or check** — Paste a hash under **Check a password** — the result appears as you type.
4. **Read the details** — See the version, cost and salt, and any warning about cost or length.

### Guide

#### How bcrypt works

Bcrypt is a password-hashing function built to be **slow on purpose**. The cost is a power of two: cost 12 runs the expensive key setup 2¹² = 4,096 times, and each +1 doubles the time — for you and for anyone trying to guess passwords from a stolen database.

Every hash includes its own random **salt**, so the same password gives a different hash each time. That’s why you can’t “decrypt” bcrypt or compare two hashes directly — you check a password by hashing it again with the salt stored in the hash.

Bcrypt only reads the **first 72 bytes** of a password. Long passphrases that start the same will match each other, so apps that allow very long passwords often pre-hash them (as Django’s bcrypt_sha256 does) or use Argon2id.

#### Anatomy of a bcrypt hash

| Part | Example | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Prefix | $2b$ | Bcrypt version — $2a$, $2b$ and $2y$ are interchangeable for normal passwords |
| Cost | 12$ | 2¹² = 4,096 rounds |
| Salt | R9h/cIPz0gi.URNNX3kh2O | 22 characters = 16 random bytes |
| Checksum | PST9/PgBkqquzi.Ss7KIUgO2t0jWMUW | 31 characters = 23 bytes of the result |

### FAQ

**Can a bcrypt hash be decrypted?**
No. Bcrypt is a one-way hash, not encryption. The only way to find a password is to guess it and check — which bcrypt makes deliberately slow. To test a password you know, paste the hash under **Check a password**.

**What cost should I use?**
OWASP recommends at least 10. Cost 12 (Laravel’s and PHP 8.4’s default) is a good balance; aim for roughly 250 ms per hash on your server. The tool shows timings on your device to help you choose.

**What is the difference between $2a$, $2b$ and $2y$?**
They produce the same hash for any password up to 72 bytes. $2b$ is OpenBSD’s 2014 revision, $2y$ is PHP’s name for the same fix, and $2a$ is the original. Most libraries read all three.

**Why does the same password give a different hash every time?**
Each hash gets a new random salt, stored inside the hash. That’s intended — it stops attackers from spotting users with the same password. Checking still works because the salt is read back from the hash.

**Why doesn’t my hash verify?**
Check that the hash is the full 60 characters (database columns that are too short cut it off), that the password has no extra spaces, and that Caps Lock was off — the tool looks for the last two for you.

**Is it safe to type a real password here?**
Everything runs in your browser; nothing is sent or saved. Even so, avoid pasting other people’s live passwords into any website, including this one.

## Minesweeper

URL: https://justtools.online/games/minesweeper/

Play Minesweeper free online: Beginner, Intermediate, Expert or custom boards, a safe first click, no-guess boards that never need luck, hints and best times.

### At a glance

- Three classic levels — **Beginner** (9×9, 10 mines), **Intermediate** (16×16, 40) and **Expert** (30×16, 99) — plus custom boards up to 40×30.
- The **first click is always safe** and opens a clearing; mines are placed only after it.
- **No-guess boards**: each board is checked by a logic solver so it can be cleared without a single 50/50 guess.
- **Hints** show the next safe cell or certain mine and explain why — and point out a wrong flag first.
- Right-click or long-press to flag, click a number to open around it (**chording**), question marks optional, full keyboard control.
- Tracks wins, **best times** and **3BV/s** for each level in your browser; your game is saved if you close the tab.

### Features

- **Never a forced guess**: No-guess mode builds boards a careful player can always solve by logic.
- **Hints that teach**: Learn patterns like 1-2-1 from hints that name the numbers involved.
- **Made for phones**: Tap to dig, long-press or switch to flag mode, and Expert turns tall to fit the screen.
- **Chording**: Click a satisfied number to open all its other neighbours at once.
- **Replay a board**: Hit a mine? Replay the same board from the same start.
- **Speedrun stats**: Best time and 3BV per second for each level, like the competitive players use.

### How to play Minesweeper

1. **Click any cell** — The first click is always safe and opens an area of the board.
2. **Read the numbers** — A number shows how many mines touch that cell, including diagonally.
3. **Flag the mines** — Right-click (or long-press) a cell you know is a mine to put a flag on it.
4. **Clear the rest** — Open every cell that isn’t a mine to win. Click a number whose mines are all flagged to open around it.

### Guide

#### Minesweeper patterns worth knowing

| Pattern | What it tells you |
| --- | --- |
| A 1 with one hidden neighbour | That neighbour is a mine. |
| A number with all its mines flagged | Every other neighbour is safe — click the number to open them. |
| 1-1 along a wall | The cell beyond the second 1 is safe. |
| 1-2-1 along a wall | The mines are under the 1s; the cell under the 2 is safe. |
| 1-2-2-1 along a wall | The mines are under the two 2s. |

#### What is 3BV?

3BV (Bechtel’s Board Benchmark Value) is the smallest number of clicks that can clear a board: one click per open area plus one per number not on the edge of an open area. Dividing it by your time gives **3BV/s**, the fairest way to compare speed across boards.

### FAQ

**Is the first click always safe?**
Yes. Mines are placed after your first click, away from it and its neighbours, so you always start with an open area.

**What are no-guess boards?**
Boards that a logic solver has cleared from your first click without guessing. With the option on, losing always means a mistake — never bad luck.

**How do I flag a mine on a phone?**
Long-press the cell, or switch the **Tap to** control to 🚩 Flag and tap.

**What does clicking a number do?**
If that number already has as many flags around it as its value, clicking it opens all its other neighbours. If a flag is wrong, you’ll set off a mine.

**Do hints count against my best time?**
Games where you used a hint still count as wins, but not for your best time or 3BV/s.

**Is my game saved?**
Yes, in this browser — the game in progress, your settings and your statistics. Nothing is uploaded.

## 2048 Game

URL: https://justtools.online/games/2048-game/
Category: Games
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-08

Play 2048 free online: swipe or use the arrow keys to join tiles. Undo, AI hints, an auto-play AI, 3×3 to 6×6 boards and your best score saved. No sign-up.

### At a glance

- The classic **2048** rules: slide all tiles up, down, left or right; two equal tiles that meet join into one, and a new 2 (or sometimes 4) appears after each move.
- Play with **swipes** on a phone or the **arrow keys / W A S D** on a keyboard, with smooth sliding and merging animations.
- **Undo** up to 50 moves, and a **hint** from an expectimax AI that usually reaches 2048 on its own.
- **Let the AI play** to watch the strategy — games where it plays don’t count towards your best score.
- Boards from **3×3 to 6×6**, with the goal scaled to the size (256 on 3×3, 2048 on 4×4, 4096 on 5×5, 8192 on 6×6).
- Your game, best score and top tile for each size are saved in your browser.

### Features

- **Undo**: Took a wrong turn? Step back up to 50 moves.
- **AI hints**: Ask for the best move from an AI that looks a few tiles ahead.
- **Watch the AI**: Let it play and see how keeping the big tile in a corner works.
- **Four board sizes**: A quick 3×3, the classic 4×4, or roomy 5×5 and 6×6 boards.
- **Keep going**: Reached the goal? Carry on for 4096 and beyond.
- **Saved as you play**: Close the tab and carry on later on this device.

### How to play 2048

1. **Slide the tiles** — Swipe, or press an arrow key, to move every tile as far as it can go.
2. **Join equal numbers** — Two tiles with the same number merge into their sum: 2 + 2 = 4, 4 + 4 = 8…
3. **Plan ahead** — Keep your biggest tile in a corner and build the row next to it in order.
4. **Reach 2048** — Make a 2048 tile to win — or keep going for a higher score. The game ends when no move is left.

### Guide

#### Strategy that works

- **Pick a corner** for your biggest tile and keep it there — mostly use two directions (say left and down) and a third only when needed.
- **Keep the edge row in order**, largest to smallest away from the corner, so tiles can chain into each other.
- **Avoid the fourth direction**: pressing it pulls the big tile out of its corner and lets a small tile land behind it.
- **Think about where the new tile will appear** — leave space on the side away from your corner.

#### Scoring

Each merge adds the new tile’s value to your score: joining two 8s gives 16 points. Reaching 2048 usually means a score of about 20,000.

### FAQ

**Is 2048 free to play here?**
Yes — unlimited games with undo, hints and every board size, with no sign-up or download.

**How do I play on a phone?**
Swipe up, down, left or right on the board. The page won’t scroll while you swipe on it.

**What happens after 2048?**
Choose **Keep going** to continue for 4096, 8192 and beyond, or start a new game.

**How does the AI hint work?**
It tries each move and averages over where the next tile could appear, a few moves ahead (expectimax), favouring boards with empty cells, merges and tiles in order.

**Does undo affect my best score?**
No — undo is part of this version of the game. Only games where the AI played for you are left out of your best score.

**Is my game saved?**
Yes, in this browser, along with your best score and top tile for each board size.
